`README.md`:

```md
# D-810 for Binary Ninja

> Inspired by [D-810](https://github.com/joydo/d810) by eShard, with MBA rules from
> [d810-ng](https://github.com/w00tzenheimer/d810-ng).

A Binary Ninja plugin that cleans up mixed boolean-arithmetic (MBA) obfuscation, opaque
predicates and control-flow flattening. It turns junk like `(x ^ y) + 2 * (x & y)` back into
`x + y`, folds conditions that always go the same way (OLLVM-style bogus control flow) so Binary
Ninja drops the dead branches, and turns flattened state machines back into branches and loops.
Nothing is written to the binary.

Here's an export from an OLLVM-obfuscated DLL before (399 lines of HLIL):

<img src="imgs/before.png" alt="Before" width="760">

And after (4 lines):

<img src="imgs/after.png" alt="After" width="760">

## What it handles

* MBA expressions, through D-810's rules, a built-in linear MBA simplifier, and
  [CoBRA](https://github.com/trailofbits/CoBRA) if you have it installed
* OLLVM-style instruction substitution, like `(x & y) | (x ^ y)` for `x | y`
* Arithmetic helpers with private register conventions, including nested helpers and proven
  scratch-slot round trips
* Dead private stack writes and non-escaping scratch accesses, including partial byte ranges
* Comparisons reconstructed from arithmetic flags and supported conditional-compare merges
* Private allocation round trips when explicit semantic contracts establish their memory behavior
* Bounded constant-input buffer computations, with decoded-text comments at their uses
* Opaque predicates, including ones hidden behind long chains of masked constants, ones that
  only hold on every path into a merge, values carried round loops, and the classic
  number-theoretic ones like `7 * y * y - 1 != x * x`
* Divisions that can never trap, like `2 / (x * x + 1)`
* Jumps and calls through encoded tables of code pointers (Hikari-style indirect branches and
  calls), including jumps back into the same function, and identity wrappers around them,
  when no visible code writes the table
* Constants encoded against a global key whose bytes are proven unwritten, like `x ^ key ^ 0x3c1d`.
  This includes bounded writes to neighboring buffers and helpers that only read the pointer,
  including returned pointers and whole local pointer slots whose later uses are proven safe.
* Control-flow flattening: state machines driven by compare trees or jump tables, including
  nested loops, and machines split across functions, where the dispatcher calls itself for the
  next state or calls a small function per state that returns through a stub back to it. Large
  handlers and their loops stay in place while the dispatcher is removed. Self-calls and outlined
  handlers can be recovered together, including dispatchers with large argument lists and
  undeclared register inputs that the handlers provably preserve. Known register and stack
  inputs can also be carried across handlers when their values and frame layout are proven
* Junk loops that only count a variable up to some value and then throw it away
* x86, x64 and ARM64 binaries (PE, ELF and Mach-O)

Every rewrite is checked before it's applied. Conditions are only folded when Z3 proves them,
and D-810's rules are only used at the bit widths Z3 proved them for. It runs in two passes,
MLIL then HLIL, and the HLIL pass picks up whatever MLIL couldn't express. Unflattening happens
in between, by copying code rather than guessing, so the program's behaviour doesn't change.

## Requirements

* Binary Ninja 6.0 (tested on 6.0 Personal, macOS arm64)
* `z3-solver` in Binary Ninja's Python
* Optional: CoBRA, through the `d810-cobra` package

## Install

Clone it and link it into your plugins folder:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/MZHeader/binja-d810
ln -s "$PWD/binja-d810/binja_d810" "$HOME/Library/Application Support/Binary Ninja/plugins/binja_d810"
```

Then install Z3 (and CoBRA if you want it) into Binary Ninja's Python, which is 3.13:

```sh
BN_SITE="$HOME/Library/Application Support/Binary Ninja/python313/site-packages"
uv pip install --python python3.13 --target "$BN_SITE" z3-solver
uv pip install --python python3.13 --target "$BN_SITE" --no-deps d810-cobra==0.1.7   # optional
```

Restart Binary Ninja. You should see `binja-d810: activities ... registered` in the log.

## Usage

It's off by default. Use **Plugins > D810 > Enable for Current Function**, or right-click the
function, go to **Function Settings** and tick **D-810: simplify MBA expressions**.
Both reanalyze the function straight away.

<img src="imgs/function-settings.png" alt="Function Settings menu" width="520">

To run it on a whole binary, use **Plugins > D810 > Enable for This Binary**, or tick the same
option in **File > Open with Options** before opening it. The menu also has disable commands
for the current function and the whole binary; these undo D810's flow fixes. Your skipped-function
list and time budgets still apply. Functions without obfuscation are skipped almost instantly,
but heavily obfuscated ones can use their whole time budget each, so on big binaries it's often
quicker to enable it only for the functions you care about.

Every rewrite is logged under `binja_d810`. The log says **D810: analysis complete** once native
analysis and D810's queued changes have finished. Pass failures are reported as errors; budget
warnings still mean some work was left unfinished.

Use **Plugins > D810 > Show Function Report** for the latest report, or run this in the Python console:

```python
current_function.request_debug_report("d810")
current_function.reanalyze()
```

## Settings

Everything is under **Settings > D-810** and can be set globally or per binary. The on/off switch
itself lives in a separate **extension** group that Binary Ninja creates.

<img src="imgs/settings.png" alt="D-810 settings" width="860">

<img src="imgs/settings-toggle.png" alt="The on/off switch" width="860">

* **Time budget per function**: 20 s by default. Binary Ninja gives up on a function that takes
  too long to analyze, so when a binary is opened with D-810 on, its per-function limit is raised
  to twice the budget. The passes share that allowance; jump-table dispatchers keep up to half
  for control-flow recovery and HLIL cleanup. Table and type changes can trigger another run, so total
  time can exceed the budget.
* **Generic MBA simplifier (Tier 2)**: the linear simplifier and CoBRA. Turn it off to use the
  rules only.
* **Skipped functions** and **Disabled rules**: addresses and rule names to leave alone.
* **Flow fixes**: on by default. Resolves code-pointer tables and identity wrappers, and undoes
  it all when D-810 is turned off. Your own types and branch targets always win.
* **Unflatten control flow**: on by default. It only touches a function with a clear dispatcher:
  a loop over a state variable that's only ever set to constants. It also removes junk loops.
* **Pure-callee summaries**: on by default. Exposes arithmetic across helper calls before MLIL
  generation. Turn it off to restore the calls; the limits are listed below.
* **Clean up private scratch slots**: on by default. Removes proven dead stack traffic and
  exposes private loads/stores to the expression passes. Disabling it restores the original IL.
* **Recombine flag conditions**: on by default. Replaces proven flag formulas with comparisons
  in MLIL and HLIL, including bounded conditional-compare merges.
* **Simplify private allocation round trips**: on by default. Requires explicit semantic
  contracts; ordinary allocator names and signatures are insufficient.
* **Read-only ranges**: address ranges (`0x1000-0x1fff`, end included) to treat as constant. Use
  them for data you know never changes. Clearing a range puts the old types back.
* **Enabled**: a kill switch for everything.

## Arithmetic helpers

D810 reads the helper's lifted IL to find its register inputs and outputs, including registers
missing from its declared calling convention. It builds fixed-width expression summaries and
substitutes checked copies of the body at ordinary calls. The copies retain flag writes and
call/return stack effects. Unsupported effects, loops, tail calls and recursion stay unchanged.

Scratch stores need a byte-level proof that the caller cannot read or escape them. This currently
requires a straight-line caller whose other calls also have summaries. Partial overwrites do not
hide later reads. The stores are retained in the copied IL; this pass does not clear alias flags or
remove arbitrary stack writes. Fixed read-only loads are allowed; writable and relocated loads are not.

The default limits are:

| Setting | Default |
| --- | ---: |
| Callee instruction limit, including nested expansion | 64 |
| Callee expression limit | 2,000 nodes |
| Callee summary depth | 4 |
| Callee frame byte limit | 256 |
| Callee caller instruction limit | 4,096 |
| Callee call-site limit | 64 caller sites |
| Callee proof timeout | 500 ms |
| Callee red-zone byte limit | 128, capped by the platform ABI |

Depth bounds composition through the current IL; helpers simplified in an earlier analysis can
already be flatter. Summary planning and substitution share the function time budget.
Unknown and kernel platforms get no red-zone
allowance; setting its limit to zero disables that support. The ABI bounds come from the
[System V AMD64 specification](https://gitlab.com/x86-psABIs/x86-64-ABI/-/blob/master/x86-64-ABI/low-level-sys-info.tex)
and [Apple's ARM64 documentation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/writing-arm64-code-for-apple-platforms).

**Prefer native callee inlining** is an optional comparison mode, off by default. For register-only
helpers it records a user inline flag and restores it when disabled. It needs Flow fixes for the
undo queue. Frame-dependent helpers continue to use direct substitution, since a global inline
flag would affect unproved callers too. Existing no-inline flags are respected.

The debug report's `callees` entries list substitutions and rejection reasons. Synthetic fixtures
cover ARM64, x86-64 and ordinary i686 calls at O0/O2, with independent arithmetic models and undo
checks. These tests do not establish coverage on real malware. Direct call-link substitution is
currently supported on those three architectures; other architectures are left unchanged.

## Private scratch slots

D810 follows stack addresses through copies and fixed offsets. When every use is accounted for,
it converts local loads/stores to variable accesses and clears their alias status in the generated
IL. It then removes a store only if no path can read any of its bytes before they are overwritten.
An additional SSA check preserves live logical values that happen to share a stack location.
Unused pure address calculations are removed with the stores.

Escaping addresses, unknown calls, volatile/protected slots and unmodeled memory accesses stay
conservative. Partial overwrites preserve the remaining bytes. Overlapping logical variables
keep their alias identities; partial accesses on big-endian targets are currently excluded.
The proof uses exact byte ranges and all CFG paths, without guessing which branch will run.

Cleanup runs before MBA rewriting and after control-flow recovery, under the shared function
budget. Its settings are:

| Setting | Default |
| --- | ---: |
| `binja_d810.scratchSlots` | true |
| `binja_d810.scratchInstructions` | 20,000 instructions |
| `binja_d810.scratchNodes` | 40,000 proof nodes per round |
| `binja_d810.scratchFrameBytes` | 4,096 distinct stack bytes |
| `binja_d810.scratchLivenessVisits` | 100,000 fixpoint visits |
| `binja_d810.scratchRounds` | 4 rounds per cleanup stage |
| `binja_d810.scratchAddressDepth` | 64 SSA definitions |

The report's `scratch` entries show removed stores, promoted accesses, cleared aliases and
rejection reasons. No user types or binary bytes are changed; disabling the feature regenerates
the original aliases. Synthetic ARM64, x86-64 and i686 fixtures check independent arithmetic
models, escapes, partial overlaps, budgets and disable/restore. One i686 PE O2 partial-store
fixture exposes an existing native MLIL error that loses the upper bytes before D810 runs;
the suite records it as an expected failure and separately checks that D810 preserves the baseline.
These fixtures do not establish coverage on real malware.

## Flag conditions

D810 rebuilds signed and unsigned comparisons from pure boolean and arithmetic expressions.
For conditional compares, it follows the actual SSA values leaving each arm of a branch and
combines them with the branch condition. It checks every proposed expression at its exact
bit widths, then removes newly unused flag calculations. A flag also used as external data
keeps that use and blocks the dependent rewrite.

The native passes read IL semantics, without matching register or symbol names. A small
subtraction model isolates ARM64's no-borrow carry convention from x86's borrow convention;
unit tests prove all ten comparisons at several widths. Native C fixtures cover all eight
ARM64/x86-64/i686 builds, with an independent symbolic interpreter checking complete branch
paths and observable stores. On x86-64, ordinary compare chains are often already simplified
by Binary Ninja. The ARM64 unsigned conditional-compare fixture loses its merged flag locals.

Supported merges are bounded two-arm branches, including one empty arm. Loops, ambiguous
merges, stale operands, volatile/protected values and unknown flag operations stay unchanged.
In particular, native `ADD_OVERFLOW` is currently unmodeled: some ARM64 signed conditional
compares retain their flag locals. Its semantics are not guessed from the displayed expression.
Explicit arithmetic overflow formulas are supported and proven. These are synthetic results;
no real-malware coverage is claimed.

| Setting | Default |
| --- | ---: |
| `binja_d810.flagConditions` | true; disable to restore the original conditions |
| `binja_d810.flagInstructions` | 20,000 instructions |
| `binja_d810.flagNodes` | 2,000 expression nodes |
| `binja_d810.flagWork` | 80,000 proof visits per pass |
| `binja_d810.flagCandidates` | 128 comparison attempts per expression |
| `binja_d810.flagConditionsPerPass` | 128 condition roots |
| `binja_d810.flagMergeDepth` | 8 nested merges |
| `binja_d810.flagProofMilliseconds` | 200 ms per proof |

Both stages share the function's time budget. The `flags` report entries list successful
recombinations and rejection reasons. These are regenerated IL edits, with no binary or user
metadata changes.

## Private allocation round trips

D810 can forward a private object's loads from preceding stores, including partial overlaps.
It proves all pointer uses, rejects escapes and observations of the pointer's numeric value,
and keeps unknown calls, memory effects and control-flow crossings conservative. Constant-size
and pointer-forwarding call/tail-call wrappers are checked from their MLIL bodies.

This needs a contract guaranteeing fresh, ordinary, nonnull storage. Removing the allocation,
stores and release also requires an explicit guarantee that the complete lifetime is unobservable,
including failure, exceptions and effects on later allocations. Without that stronger guarantee,
only loads are forwarded; calls and stores remain. Possible allocation failure retains the original
memory accesses. A null check does not authorize deletion of its failure path.

The installed type libraries we tested supplied signatures but no such effect guarantees.
D810 does **not** identify allocators by names such as `malloc` or `free`. Contracts can come from
the `binja_d810.memory` type attribute or explicit per-function metadata. Binary Ninja currently
drops custom attributes when rebuilding some function signatures, so metadata is the reliable
way to supply a verified contract. For a selected allocator with the required guarantees:

```python
current_function.store_metadata("binja_d810.memory",
    '{"version":1,"role":"allocate","parameter":0,"fresh":true,"ordinary":true,"nonnull":true,"elidable":false}')
```

`parameter` is the zero-based size argument. A release uses
`{"version":1,"role":"deallocate","parameter":0,"elidable":false}`, where the parameter is
the object pointer. Set `elidable` on both contracts only when the stronger lifetime guarantee
has been established. Reanalyze the callers after changing contracts. D810 reads these user-owned
contracts and leaves them intact when disabled; it makes no user type or binary changes.

| Setting | Default |
| --- | ---: |
| `binja_d810.allocationRoundTrips` | true; disable to restore the original IL |
| `binja_d810.allocationInstructions` | 20,000 instructions |
| `binja_d810.allocationNodes` | 40,000 proof visits |
| `binja_d810.allocationSites` | 64 calls |
| `binja_d810.allocationBytes` | 4,096 bytes per object |
| `binja_d810.allocationWrapperInstructions` | 64 instructions |
| `binja_d810.allocationWrapperDepth` | 4 wrappers |
| `binja_d810.allocationExpressionNodes` | 2,000 nodes |
| `binja_d810.allocationContractBytes` | 4,096 UTF-8 bytes |

The pass shares the function deadline. The `allocations` report lists forwarded loads, removed
lifetimes and rejection reasons. Synthetic C fixtures cover ordinary imported allocation calls,
boxed-value wrappers, partial writes, escapes, pointer observations, missing guarantees and undo
on all eight builds. Elision tests explicitly assume infallible, unobservable test contracts;
they do not prove those properties for a real allocator or for malware. Unannotated library
allocations remain unchanged.

## Constant buffers and decoded text

`binja_d810.constantBuffers` (default **true**) evaluates a deterministic MLIL region near
function entry. Scalar arithmetic, bounded loops, immutable image reads and local byte stores
are evaluated at their actual widths. The pass replaces that region with its final stores and
preserves register writes and live values. A retained path that can reenter the region vetoes
the change. Calls, unknown inputs, writable reads, pointer-bit observations and unmodeled effects
stop evaluation. It never executes the binary or calls a helper.

This is exact concrete evaluation of the input IL, with separate control-flow and live-out
checks. String recognition is a display heuristic: printable ASCII ending in NUL, or a buffer
followed by a constant length argument. The computed bytes are known; the callee's interpretation
of them is not assumed. The debug report records steps, text and rejection reasons.
`binja_d810.constantBufferComments` (default **true**) controls the comments. They use native
undo, preserve user edits, and are removed when the feature or D810 is disabled. Comments
require Flow fixes; IL evaluation does not. No binary bytes change.

Limits share the function time budget. Each key below has the `binja_d810.` prefix:

| Setting | Default |
| --- | --- |
| `constantInstructions` | 4,096 MLIL instructions |
| `constantExpressionNodes` | 2,000 nodes per expression |
| `constantSteps` | 10,000 executed instructions |
| `constantTrips` | 256 visits per instruction |
| `constantFrameBytes` | 4,096 bytes of local frame |
| `constantProofWork` | 100,000 proof visits |
| `constantRegionStarts` | 64 entry-block starting positions |
| `constantAnnotationSteps` | 4,096 retained-tail instructions |
| `constantScalarBits` | 128 bits |
| `constantStringBytes` | 256 bytes |
| `constantStringMinimum` | 4 printable bytes |
| `constantStoreBytes` | 8 bytes per emitted store; maximum 8 |

The current pass handles one entry region, not arbitrary regions after unknown calls. SIMD,
floating arithmetic, unknown pointer bytes and ambiguous logical/physical stack overlaps stay
unchanged. Native synthetic constant-copy operations are identified from their IL metadata and
original stores, never by library name. Their bytes have already been computed by Binary Ninja.

Tests generate rotate/multiply/add/XOR streams from 16 randomized seeds in loop and unrolled
forms, built for ARM64, x86-64 PE/ELF and i686 at O0/O2. Final IL bytes are read back independently
and compared with the Python generator. Fixtures disable compiler vectorization and stack
protectors to test scalar semantics. Three x86 O2 cases currently have incorrect native
constant-copy bytes **before D810**; strict expected failures record that limitation and check
that D810 preserves the original IL's bytes. These tests make no real-malware coverage claim.

## Notes

* D-810 removes the global reads its folds leave unused. Bare `data_...` lines that were there
  before it ran are left alone. They're harmless.
* Calls through resolved API pointers can show extra arguments, because Binary Ninja guesses them
  from whatever registers happen to be set. Giving the pointer a type fixes it.
* Unflattening can leave a flag-like compare behind when the next state is picked before a loop,
  or kept in two places at once. Machines that compute their next state are left alone.
* State functions pulled into their dispatcher are copied, not moved, so they're still there for
  anything else that calls them. Unoptimized builds that widen a state function's result on the
  way out keep their calls. Unmodeled stack/frame inputs and clobbered hidden registers also
  keep their calls.
* Table resolution checks the decoded targets and any visible writes to the table, but it can't
  see changes made by a loader. The debug report says why a table was rejected.

`binja_d810/allocations/contracts.py`:

```py
"""Typed semantic contracts; no symbol-name or library-name catalogue.

Fresh ordinary storage is enough to reason about a private object's bytes. Erasing the calls
additionally requires an explicit nonnull allocation and an unobservable allocation/free pair.
Ordinary function signatures, and a generic `pure` flag, do not supply these guarantees.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
import json

ATTRIBUTE = "binja_d810.memory"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Contract:
    role: str
    parameter: int
    nonnull: bool = False
    elidable: bool = False


def parse(text: str, max_bytes: int):
    if not isinstance(text, str) or len(text.encode("utf-8")) > max_bytes:
        raise ValueError("allocation contract byte limit")
    spec = json.loads(text)
    if not isinstance(spec, dict) or type(spec.get("version")) is not int or spec["version"] != 1:
        raise ValueError("unsupported allocation contract version")
    allowed = {"version", "role", "parameter", "fresh", "ordinary", "nonnull", "elidable"}
    if set(spec) - allowed:
        raise ValueError("unknown allocation contract fields")
    role = spec.get("role")
    parameter = spec.get("parameter")
    if role not in ("allocate", "deallocate") or type(parameter) is not int or parameter < 0:
        raise ValueError("invalid allocation contract role or parameter")
    for key in ("fresh", "ordinary", "nonnull", "elidable"):
        if key in spec and type(spec[key]) is not bool:
            raise ValueError("allocation contract guarantees must be booleans")
    if role == "allocate" and (spec.get("fresh") is not True or spec.get("ordinary") is not True):
        raise ValueError("fresh ordinary storage is not guaranteed")
    if role == "deallocate" and any(k in spec for k in ("fresh", "ordinary", "nonnull")):
        raise ValueError("allocation-only guarantees on a deallocator")
    return Contract(role, parameter, spec.get("nonnull", False), spec.get("elidable", False))

```

`binja_d810/allocations/lifetime.py`:

```py
"""Exact byte forwarding for one proven non-escaping, straight-line object lifetime."""

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from ..deadline import Deadline
from ..ir.expr import Expr
from ..summaries.frame import Frame
from .contracts import Contract


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Event:
    kind: str
    key: object
    offset: int = 0
    size: int = 0
    value: Expr | None = None


@dataclass
class Plan:
    loads: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    elide: bool = False
    notes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)


def prove(events, size: int, allocation: Contract, release: Contract | None, *,
          max_bytes: int, max_events: int, little_endian=True, deadline=Deadline.never()):
    result = Plan()
    if allocation.role != "allocate" or size <= 0 or size > max_bytes:
        return Plan(notes=["unknown or excessive allocation size"])
    if not allocation.nonnull:
        return Plan(notes=["allocation failure is possible; original memory accesses retained"])
    memory = Frame(max_bytes, little_endian)
    freed, complete = False, True
    seen = set()
    try:
        for index, event in enumerate(events):
            if index >= max_events or deadline.expired():
                raise ValueError("allocation lifetime budget exhausted")
            if event.key in seen:
                raise ValueError("allocation event identity is ambiguous")
            seen.add(event.key)
            if freed:
                raise ValueError("object used after release")
            if event.kind == "free":
                if release is None or release.role != "deallocate":
                    raise ValueError("deallocation contract unavailable")
                freed = True
                continue
            if event.kind not in ("store", "load"):
                raise ValueError("object escapes or has an unmodeled effect")
            if event.offset < 0 or event.size <= 0 or event.offset + event.size > size:
                raise ValueError("object access outside the proven allocation")
            if event.kind == "store":
                if event.value is None or event.value.width != event.size * 8:
                    raise ValueError("store value width is unproved")
                memory.write(event.offset, event.value)
            elif all(at in memory.written for at in range(event.offset, event.offset + event.size)):
                result.loads[event.key] = memory.read(event.offset, event.size)
            else:
                complete = False
                result.notes.append("load has bytes without a dominating store")
        result.elide = bool(complete and freed and allocation.nonnull and allocation.elidable and release.elidable)
        if not result.elide:
            result.notes.append("allocation, stores and release retained: failure or external effects are not proved removable")
        return result
    except ValueError as exc:
        return Plan(notes=[str(exc)])  # An eventual escape invalidates earlier forwarding too.

```

`binja_d810/binja/adapter.py`:

```py
"""The contract between the IL-independent engine and one IL level."""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Callable, Hashable, Iterator, Optional, Protocol

from ..ir.expr import Expr


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Candidate:
    """A maximal effect-free supported expression, lifted with version-safe leaves."""

    root: object  # the IL expression to replace
    address: int
    ir: Expr
    # For skipping work (v2.1): the SSA value this root is the whole definition of, whether that
    # value has exactly one use, and the definitions the lift inlined.
    defines: Optional[Hashable] = None
    single_use: bool = False
    consumes: frozenset = frozenset()
    # What the user sees today: the root as written plus the definitions that die with it (all of
    # their uses are in this root). None: unknown, no visible-cost check.
    visible_nodes: Optional[int] = None
    visible_mixed: Optional[bool] = None
    # For ILAdapter.shallow: the root's instruction or statement, and the inlined definitions that
    # stay alive after a rewrite (used elsewhere too).
    context: object = None
    shared: frozenset = frozenset()
    # The root lifted without version safety (through inputs whose registers were reused before the
    # root). Only a proven constant may come from it: a constant reads no variable. constant_only:
    # there is no version-safe lift (ir is the unchecked one).
    unchecked: Optional[Expr] = None
    constant_only: bool = False
    # The root lifted with shared values counted once (v3.1), when its tree is over maxNodes: only
    # a proven constant may come from it (constancy.fold_shared), and no tree algorithm touches it.
    shared_dag: Optional[Expr] = None
    # The statement HLIL shows the root in, beyond the root itself (v3.1): the kinds ("arith",
    # "bitwise") of the statements its value flows into through single uses, None if unknown, and
    # the kinds of the root's own statement. A replacement must not make that statement mixed.
    consumer_kinds: Optional[frozenset] = None
    root_kinds: frozenset = frozenset()
    # A condition over merged values that is no candidate itself (k != 0 with k = phi(...)) but whose
    # per-path variants are: offered constant-only with them, as alternative sets of
    # variants, cheapest first (ILAdapter.path_variants).
    paths: Optional[tuple] = None


Skip = Callable[..., None]  # skip(address, reason, expression=None): a root left as it is, and why


class ILAdapter(Protocol):
    level: str  # "mlil" or "hlil"

    def has_candidates(self) -> bool:
        """Cheap pre-check: does the function mix arithmetic and bitwise operations at all?"""

    def candidates(self, skip: Skip) -> Iterator[Candidate]:
        """Every candidate whose lift is an MBA, last first (a candidate before the definitions it
        inlines), lifted lazily; roots split by effects are reported to `skip`."""

    def shallow(self, candidate: Candidate, keep: Optional[frozenset] = None) -> Optional[Candidate]:
        """Optional. The same root lifted with the definitions in `keep` (default: those that other
        instructions also use, which stay visible) left as leaves where they are live; None if that
        changes nothing or is not possible."""

    def replace(self, candidate: Candidate, replacement: Expr) -> None:
        """Lower `replacement` and put it in place of the candidate's root, keeping a backup."""

    def finish(self) -> None:
        """Finalize the IL and regenerate SSA after a batch of replacements or removals."""

    def dead_assignments(self) -> set[Hashable]:
        """Pure assignments whose value is never used (shared policy: binja_d810.binja.deadcode)."""

    def remove(self, dead: set[Hashable]) -> None:
        """Remove those assignments, keeping backups."""

    def path_variants(self, candidate: Candidate) -> Optional[list[list[Expr]]]:
        """Optional. Alternative sets of a condition's lift once per incoming path of
        the merged values it reads (binja_d810.ir.paths), cheapest first; the engine folds it if every
        variant of one set is the same proven constant. None when there is nothing to split."""

    def cfg_shape(self) -> tuple:
        """A value that changes if and only if the function's control flow changes."""

    def restore(self) -> None:
        """Undo every replacement and removal made through this adapter (pass-level rollback)."""

```

`binja_d810/binja/allocation_roundtrips.py`:

```py
"""Private allocation lifetimes described by semantic type attributes, never library names."""

from collections import defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
import time

from binaryninja import (Endianness, ILInstructionAttribute as Attr, ILSourceLocation,
                         MediumLevelILFunction, MediumLevelILOperation as M, RegisterValueType,
                         SSAVariable, TypeClass, VariableSourceType)

from ..allocations.contracts import ATTRIBUTE, Contract, parse
from ..allocations.lifetime import Event, prove
from ..deadline import Deadline
from ..ir.evaluate import evaluate
from ..ir.expr import Const, Var, substitute, to_signed, variables
from .effects import mlil_effect
from .mlil.lift import lift
from .mlil.lower import lower
from .scratch import operands, walk


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Limits:
    instructions: int = 20000
    nodes: int = 40000
    sites: int = 64
    bytes: int = 4096
    wrapper_instructions: int = 64
    depth: int = 4
    expression_nodes: int = 2000
    contract_bytes: int = 4096


@dataclass
class Report:
    loads: int = 0
    lifetimes: int = 0
    notes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    seconds: float = 0.0
    cpu_seconds: float = 0.0
    exhausted: bool = False


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Binding:
    contract: Contract
    argument: object  # native argument expression, or a proven constant from a wrapper


_CALLS = {M.MLIL_CALL, M.MLIL_CALL_SSA, M.MLIL_TAILCALL, M.MLIL_TAILCALL_SSA}
_LOADS = {M.MLIL_LOAD_SSA, M.MLIL_LOAD_STRUCT_SSA}
_STORES = {M.MLIL_STORE_SSA, M.MLIL_STORE_STRUCT_SSA}
_PROTECTED = {Attr.ILPreventDeadStoreElimination, Attr.ILPreventAliasAnalysis}
_CONSTANT = {RegisterValueType.ConstantValue, RegisterValueType.ConstantPointerValue, RegisterValueType.ImportedAddressValue}


class Factory:
    def __init__(self, il, limits, deadline):
        self.il, self.view, self.limits, self.deadline = il, il.source_function.view, limits, deadline
        self.left = limits.nodes
        self.active = set()

    def tick(self):
        self.left -= 1
        if self.left < 0 or self.deadline.expired():
            raise ValueError("allocation proof budget exhausted")

    def call(self, call, depth=0):
        self.tick()
        value = call.dest.value
        func = self.view.get_function_at(value.value) if value.type in _CONSTANT else None
        types = [call.dest.expr_type, func.type if func is not None else None]
        contracts = []
        if func is not None:
            declared = func.get_metadata(ATTRIBUTE)
            if declared is not None:
                contracts.append(parse(declared, self.limits.contract_bytes))
        for typ in types:
            if typ is not None and typ.type_class == TypeClass.PointerTypeClass:
                typ = typ.target
            if typ is not None and ATTRIBUTE in typ.attributes:
                contract = parse(typ.attributes[ATTRIBUTE], self.limits.contract_bytes)
                if contract not in contracts:
                    contracts.append(contract)
        if len(contracts) > 1:
            raise ValueError("conflicting allocation contracts")
        if contracts:
            contract = contracts[0]
            if contract.parameter >= len(call.params):
                raise ValueError("allocation contract parameter is unavailable")
            return Binding(contract, call.params[contract.parameter])
        if func is None or depth >= self.limits.depth or func.start in self.active:
            raise ValueError("semantic allocation contract unavailable")
        il = func.mlil_if_available
        if il is None or len(il) > self.limits.wrapper_instructions or len(list(il.basic_blocks)) != 1:
            raise ValueError("no bounded allocation wrapper body")
        calls = [i for i in il.instructions if i.operation in _CALLS]
        if len(calls) != 1:
            raise ValueError("wrapper has no single contracted call")
        inner = calls[0]
        for instr in il.instructions:
            self.tick()
            if instr is inner or instr.expr_index == inner.expr_index or instr.operation in (M.MLIL_RET, M.MLIL_NOP):
                continue
            if instr.operation != M.MLIL_SET_VAR or mlil_effect(instr.src.ssa_form) is not None:
                raise ValueError("wrapper has extra effects")
            if instr.dest.source_type == VariableSourceType.StackVariableSourceType and instr.dest.storage >= 0:
                raise ValueError("wrapper writes incoming frame storage")
            if any(n.operation in (M.MLIL_ADDRESS_OF, M.MLIL_ADDRESS_OF_FIELD) or n.attributes & _PROTECTED
                   for n in walk(instr)):
                raise ValueError("wrapper has protected or address-taken storage")
        self.active.add(func.start)
        try:
            bound = self.call(inner, depth + 1)
            # An ordinary call wrapper must return exactly its pointer result (or void for
            # a deallocator); a tail call already has that structural property.
            if inner.operation == M.MLIL_CALL:
                returns = [i for i in il.instructions if i.operation == M.MLIL_RET]
                if len(returns) != 1 or returns[0].instr_index <= inner.instr_index:
                    raise ValueError("wrapper return is not bounded")
                ret = returns[0]
                if bound.contract.role == "allocate":
                    if len(inner.ssa_form.output) != 1 or len(ret.src) != 1:
                        raise ValueError("wrapper pointer return is ambiguous")
                    value = lift(ret.src[0].ssa_form, root_instr=ret, check_versions=False, dataflow=False,
                                 max_nodes=self.limits.expression_nodes)
                    if not isinstance(value, Var) or value.ref != inner.ssa_form.output[0]:
                        raise ValueError("wrapper changes the allocation result")
                elif ret.src:
                    raise ValueError("deallocation wrapper returns data")
            arg = bound.argument
            if isinstance(arg, Const):
                return bound
            expression = lift(arg.ssa_form, root_instr=inner, check_versions=False, dataflow=False,
                              max_nodes=self.limits.expression_nodes)
            if expression is not None and not variables(expression):
                return Binding(bound.contract, Const(evaluate(expression, {}), expression.width))
            if isinstance(expression, Var) and isinstance(expression.ref, SSAVariable) and expression.ref.version == 0:
                parameters = list(func.parameter_vars)
                if expression.ref.var in parameters and parameters.index(expression.ref.var) < len(call.params):
                    return Binding(bound.contract, call.params[parameters.index(expression.ref.var)])
            raise ValueError("wrapper does not fix constants or forward one whole parameter")
        finally:
            self.active.remove(func.start)


class Object:
    def __init__(self, call, factory, parents, readers):
        self.call, self.factory, self.parents, self.readers = call, factory, parents, readers
        if len(call.output) != 1:
            raise ValueError("allocation outputs are ambiguous")
        self.pointer = call.output[0]
        self.aliases = {self.pointer: 0}
        self.accesses, self.release = {}, None
        self.block = call.il_basic_block

    def address(self, node):
        displacement = 0
        while node.operation in (M.MLIL_ADD, M.MLIL_SUB) and node.size == self.factory.il.arch.address_size:
            self.factory.tick()
            base, constant = node.left, node.right
            if node.operation == M.MLIL_ADD and base.operation == M.MLIL_CONST:
                base, constant = constant, base
            if constant.operation != M.MLIL_CONST or constant.size != node.size:
                return None
            displacement += constant.constant if node.operation == M.MLIL_ADD else -constant.constant
            node = base
        self.factory.tick()
        if node.operation == M.MLIL_VAR_SSA and node.size == self.factory.il.arch.address_size and node.src in self.aliases:
            return to_signed(displacement + self.aliases[node.src], 8 * self.factory.il.arch.address_size)
        return None

    def prove_uses(self):
        pending = list(self.readers.get(self.pointer, ()))
        seen = set()
        while pending:
            self.factory.tick()
            node = pending.pop()
            if node.expr_index in seen:
                continue
            seen.add(node.expr_index)
            if node.operation not in (M.MLIL_VAR_SSA, M.MLIL_ADD, M.MLIL_SUB):
                raise ValueError("pointer merge, partial use or observation is not modeled")
            if node.il_basic_block != self.block or node.instr_index <= self.call.instr_index:
                raise ValueError("allocation lifetime crosses control flow")
            if node.attributes & _PROTECTED:
                raise ValueError("protected allocation access")
            if node.operation == M.MLIL_VAR_SSA:
                typ = node.src.var.type
                if typ is not None and (typ.volatile or typ.type_class == TypeClass.PointerTypeClass and typ.target.volatile):
                    raise ValueError("volatile allocation access")
            for parent, role in self.parents[node.expr_index]:
                self.factory.tick()
                if parent.operation == M.MLIL_SET_VAR_SSA and role == "src" \
                        and parent.size == self.factory.il.arch.address_size:
                    offset = self.address(node)
                    if offset is None:
                        raise ValueError("unknown pointer copy")
                    self.aliases[parent.dest] = offset
                    pending.extend(self.readers.get(parent.dest, ()))
                elif parent.operation in (M.MLIL_ADD, M.MLIL_SUB) and self.address(parent) is not None:
                    pending.append(parent)
                elif parent.operation in _LOADS and role == "src" or parent.operation in _STORES and role == "dest":
                    offset = self.address(node)
                    if offset is None:
                        raise ValueError("unknown object address")
                    self.accesses[parent.expr_index] = (parent, offset + getattr(parent, "offset", 0))
                elif parent.operation in _CALLS and role == "params":
                    bound = self.factory.call(parent)
                    if bound.contract.role != "deallocate" or isinstance(bound.argument, Const) \
                            or bound.argument.expr_index != node.expr_index or self.address(node) != 0:
                        raise ValueError("object escapes to a call")
                    if self.release is not None and self.release[0] != parent:
                        raise ValueError("multiple releases")
                    if parent.output:
                        raise ValueError("release produces additional values")
                    self.release = parent, bound.contract
                else:
                    raise ValueError("object pointer is observed or escapes")
        if self.release is None:
            raise ValueError("matching release not proved")
        release = self.release[0]
        if release.il_basic_block != self.block:
            raise ValueError("release crosses control flow")
        for instr in self.block:
            if not self.call.instr_index < instr.instr_index < release.instr_index:
                continue
            for node in walk(instr):
                self.factory.tick()
                if node.attributes & _PROTECTED:
                    raise ValueError("protected instruction in object lifetime")
                if node.expr_index in self.accesses or node.operation in (M.MLIL_SET_VAR_SSA, M.MLIL_VAR_SSA,
                                                                          M.MLIL_NOP, M.MLIL_MEM_PHI):
                    continue
                if mlil_effect(node, pure=lambda child: child.expr_index in self.accesses) is not None:
                    raise ValueError("unknown memory or call effect within object lifetime")


def _index(il, factory):
    parents, readers, seen = defaultdict(list), defaultdict(list), set()
    pending = [(i, None) for i in il.ssa_form.instructions]
    while pending:
        factory.tick()
        node, parent = pending.pop()
        if parent is not None:
            parents[node.expr_index].append(parent)
        if node.expr_index in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(node.expr_index)
        for role, value, _ in node.detailed_operands:
            for item in value if isinstance(value, list) else (value,):
                if hasattr(item, "operation"):
                    pending.append((item, (node, role)))
                elif isinstance(item, SSAVariable) and role not in ("dest", "output"):
                    readers[item].append(node)
    return parents, readers


def _copy(node, new, replacements, deadline):
    pending, copied = [(node, False)], {}
    while pending:
        if deadline.expired():
            raise ValueError("allocation commit budget exhausted")
        current, ready = pending.pop()
        if current.expr_index in copied:
            continue
        replacement = replacements.get(current.expr_index)
        if replacement is not None:
            copied[current.expr_index] = lower(new, replacement, ILSourceLocation.from_instruction(current))
            continue
        if not ready:
            pending.append((current, True))
            pending.extend((child, False) for _, child in operands(current) if hasattr(child, "operation"))
        else:
            copied[current.expr_index] = current.copy_to(new, lambda child: copied[child.expr_index])
            new.set_expr_attributes(copied[current.expr_index], current.attributes)
    return copied[node.expr_index]


def run(il, limits=Limits(), deadline=Deadline.never()):
    started, cpu = time.monotonic(), time.thread_time()
    report, replacements, dead = Report(), {}, set()
    try:
        if len(il) > limits.instructions:
            raise ValueError("allocation instruction limit")
        factory = Factory(il, limits, deadline)
        parents = readers = None
        calls = [i for i in il.ssa_form.instructions if i.operation == M.MLIL_CALL_SSA]
        for index, call in enumerate(calls):
            if index >= limits.sites:
                report.notes.append("allocation call-site limit")
                break
            try:
                bound = factory.call(call)
                if bound.contract.role != "allocate":
                    continue
                if parents is None:
                    parents, readers = _index(il, factory)
                arg = bound.argument
                size = arg if isinstance(arg, Const) else lift(arg, root_instr=call.non_ssa_form,
                          check_versions=False, dataflow=False, max_nodes=limits.expression_nodes)
                if size is None or variables(size):
                    raise ValueError("allocation size is not constant")
                obj = Object(call, factory, parents, readers)
                obj.prove_uses()
                memory, stores = [], {}
                ordered = []
                for instruction in obj.block:
                    pending = [(instruction, False)]
                    while pending:
                        factory.tick()
                        node, ready = pending.pop()
                        if not ready:
                            pending.append((node, True))
                            pending.extend((child, False) for _, child in reversed(list(operands(node))) if hasattr(child, "operation"))
                        elif node.expr_index in obj.accesses:
                            ordered.append(obj.accesses[node.expr_index])
                for node, offset in ordered:
                    factory.tick()
                    key = node.expr_index
                    if node.operation in _STORES:
                        stores[f"allocation_store_{key}"] = node
                        memory.append(Event("store", key, offset, node.size, Var(f"allocation_store_{key}", node.size * 8)))
                    else:
                        memory.append(Event("load", key, offset, node.size))
                memory.append(Event("free", obj.release[0].expr_index))
                if any(node.instr_index >= obj.release[0].instr_index for node, _ in obj.accesses.values()):
                    raise ValueError("object accessed at or after release")
                found = prove(memory, evaluate(size, {}), bound.contract, obj.release[1], max_bytes=limits.bytes,
                              max_events=limits.nodes, little_endian=il.arch.endianness == Endianness.LittleEndian,
                              deadline=deadline)
                report.notes.extend(f"{call.address:#x}: {note}" for note in found.notes)
                staged = {}
                for key, expression in found.loads.items():
                    node = obj.accesses[key][0]
                    mapping = {}
                    for value in variables(expression):
                        factory.tick()
                        store = stores[value.name]
                        actual = lift(store.src, root_instr=node.non_ssa_form, dataflow=False,
                                      max_nodes=limits.expression_nodes)
                        if actual is None or actual.width != value.width:
                            raise ValueError("stored value is effectful or no longer available at the load")
                        mapping[value.name] = actual
                    staged[node.non_ssa_form.expr_index] = substitute(expression, mapping)
                replacements.update(staged)
                report.loads += len(staged)
                if found.elide:
                    dead.update(node.non_ssa_form.instr_index for node in (call, obj.release[0]))
                    dead.update(node.non_ssa_form.instr_index for node, _ in obj.accesses.values() if node.operation in _STORES)
                    report.lifetimes += 1
                if staged or found.elide:
                    report.notes.append(f"{call.address:#x}: proved forwarding of {len(staged)} loads from private-byte reaching stores")
            except (ValueError, NotImplementedError) as exc:
                report.notes.append(f"{call.address:#x}: {exc}")
        if not replacements and not dead:
            return il, report
        new = MediumLevelILFunction(il.arch, low_level_il=il.llil)
        new.prepare_to_copy_function(il)
        for block in il.basic_blocks:
            new.prepare_to_copy_block(block)
            for instruction in block:
                if deadline.expired():
                    raise ValueError("allocation commit budget exhausted")
                loc = ILSourceLocation.from_instruction(instruction)
                new.set_current_address(instruction.address, block.arch)
                new.append(new.nop(loc) if instruction.instr_index in dead else _copy(instruction, new, replacements, deadline), loc)
        new.finalize()
        new.generate_ssa_form()
        return new, report
    except (ValueError, NotImplementedError, RecursionError) as exc:
        report.loads = report.lifetimes = 0
        report.notes.append(f"left unchanged: {exc}")
        return il, report
    finally:
        report.seconds, report.cpu_seconds = time.monotonic() - started, time.thread_time() - cpu
        report.exhausted = deadline.expired()

```

`binja_d810/binja/annotations.py`:

```py
"""Owned analysis comments applied through the existing idle/undo queue."""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from binaryninja import Settings
from ..flow.record import Change
from .flow import apply
from . import settings
from ..consteval.comments import remove_line


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Site:
    function: int
    address: int
    owner: str
    text: str
    evidence: tuple = ()
    requires: tuple = ()
    kind: str = "annotation"

    @property
    def key(self):
        return self.kind, self.owner, self.function, self.address, self.text


def change_kind(owner):
    return "comment:" + owner


def reconcile(func, owner, wanted, enabled):
    state = apply.state_of(func.view)
    wanted = {site.address: site for site in wanted} if enabled else {}
    changed = False
    with state.lock:
        for change in state.record.claimed_by(func.start):
            if change.kind != change_kind(owner): continue
            site = wanted.get(change.key)
            if site is None or change.detail["text"] != site.text:
                change.claims.discard(func.start); changed = True
        for key, site in list(state.pending.items()):
            if site.function == func.start and site.kind == "annotation" and site.owner == owner and wanted.get(site.address) != site:
                del state.pending[key]; changed = True
        if changed:
            state.decided[func.start] = {k for k in state.decided[func.start]
                                       if not (len(k) > 1 and k[0] == "annotation" and k[1] == owner)}
        state.recount()
    if changed: apply._arm(func.view, state)
    for site in wanted.values(): apply.enqueue(func.view, site)


def decide(work, site):
    func = work.view.get_function_at(site.function)
    prefs = Settings()
    if func is None or not prefs.get_bool(site.owner, func) or not prefs.get_bool(settings.ENABLED, func) or not prefs.get_bool(settings.FLOW_FIXES, func):
        return
    if any(not prefs.get_bool(key, func) for key in site.requires): return
    if any(work.view.read(address, len(raw)) != bytes(raw) for address, raw in site.evidence):
        work.note(site.function, f"{site.address:#x}: comment skipped; analysis inputs changed")
        return
    kind = change_kind(site.owner)
    existing = work.record.get(kind, site.address)
    if existing is not None:
        if existing.detail["function"] == site.function and existing.detail["text"] == site.text:
            work.add(Change(kind, site.address, claims={site.function}))
        return  # User edits and explicit undo always win.
    previous = func.get_comment_at(site.address)
    if site.text in previous.splitlines(): return
    wanted = previous + ("\n" if previous else "") + site.text
    action = work.view.begin_undo_actions()
    try: func.set_comment_at(site.address, wanted)
    finally: work.view.commit_undo_actions(action)
    work.add(Change(kind, site.address, {"function": site.function, "text": site.text}, claims={site.function}))
    work.note(site.function, f"{site.address:#x}: {site.text}")


def revert(view, change):
    func = view.get_function_at(change.detail["function"])
    if func is None: return set()
    current = func.get_comment_at(change.key)
    restored = remove_line(current, change.detail["text"])
    if restored != current:
        action = view.begin_undo_actions()
        try: func.set_comment_at(change.key, restored)
        finally: view.commit_undo_actions(action)
    return set()

```

`binja_d810/binja/budget.py`:

```py
"""The shared per-function allowance across both passes. No binaryninja import.

Accounting is keyed by (view session, function start) and by analysis generation. The generation
token is the address of the MLIL function the MLIL pass worked on: the HLIL activity sees that same
MLIL object within one analysis run, so it
inherits what the MLIL pass left. The ledger keeps a reference to that object, so its address cannot
be reused for another function while the entry lives. Repeated calls in one generation reuse the
entry; a new token (reanalysis) starts a fresh allowance; an HLIL invocation whose MLIL token is
unknown (HLIL regenerated alone) starts its own generation.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import threading
from collections import OrderedDict
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Hashable

from ..deadline import Deadline


@dataclass
class _Entry:
    generation: int
    keepalive: object
    allowance: float
    used: dict[str, float] = field(default_factory=lambda: {"mlil": 0.0, "hlil": 0.0})


class Allowance:
    """One pass's share of a generation's allowance. charge() what the pass spent."""

    def __init__(self, ledger: "Ledger", entry: _Entry, level: str, inherited: bool):
        self._ledger, self._entry, self.level, self.inherited = ledger, entry, level, inherited
        self.deadline = Deadline.after(self.remaining())

    def remaining(self) -> float:
        with self._ledger.lock:
            return max(0.0, self._entry.allowance - sum(self._entry.used.values()))

    def used(self) -> float:
        with self._ledger.lock:
            return self._entry.used[self.level]

    def charge(self, seconds: float) -> None:
        with self._ledger.lock:
            self._entry.used[self.level] += seconds

    def adopt(self, generation: int, keepalive: object) -> None:
        """The pass replaced its IL object (v4.2, unflattening): the next pass sees the new one, and inherits."""
        with self._ledger.lock:
            self._entry.generation, self._entry.keepalive = generation, keepalive


class Ledger:
    def __init__(self, capacity: int = 4096, keep: int = 256):
        self.lock = threading.Lock()
        self._entries: "OrderedDict[Hashable, _Entry]" = OrderedDict()
        self._capacity = capacity
        # Only the most recent entries hold their IL object: the token must stay unique between a
        # function's MLIL and HLIL passes, but thousands of held IL objects kept closed binaries'
        # analysis in memory. An older entry forgets its generation, so a later HLIL pass of it
        # starts a fresh allowance (never inherits a reused address).
        self._keep = keep
        self._kept: "OrderedDict[Hashable, None]" = OrderedDict()

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self._entries)

    def begin(self, key: Hashable, level: str, *, generation: int, keepalive: object, allowance: float) -> Allowance:
        with self.lock:
            entry = self._entries.get(key)
            inherited = entry is not None and entry.generation == generation
            if not inherited:
                entry = _Entry(generation, keepalive, allowance)
                self._entries[key] = entry
            self._entries.move_to_end(key)
            while len(self._entries) > self._capacity:
                self._entries.popitem(last=False)
            self._kept[key] = None
            self._kept.move_to_end(key)
            while len(self._kept) > self._keep:
                old, _ = self._kept.popitem(last=False)
                stale = self._entries.get(old)
                if stale is not None:
                    stale.keepalive, stale.generation = None, -1
        return Allowance(self, entry, level, inherited and level == "hlil")


LEDGER = Ledger()


def plugin_allowance(function_seconds: float, max_analysis_ms: int) -> float:
    """The shared allowance: the user's budget, but at most half of Binary Ninja's own per-function
    analysis limit, which abandons the whole function (no HLIL) when exceeded. 0 means no limit."""
    if max_analysis_ms <= 0:
        return function_seconds
    return min(function_seconds, max_analysis_ms / 2000)

```

`binja_d810/binja/callees/activity.py`:

```py
"""Early callee substitution; its time is charged to the later shared MLIL allowance."""

import threading
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from ...deadline import Deadline
from .. import budget, completion, log, settings
from ..flow import apply
from .rewrite import plan, rewrite
from . import native


@dataclass
class Report:
    seconds: float = 0.0
    cpu_seconds: float = 0.0
    notes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    exhausted: bool = False
    calls: int = 0


_LOCK = threading.Lock()
_LATEST = {}
_RETRIED = set()


def take(func):
    with _LOCK:
        return _LATEST.pop((func.view.file.session_id, func.start), None)


def run(ctx):
    from .. import limits, workflow

    func = ctx.function
    if func is None:
        return
    started, cpu = time.monotonic(), time.thread_time()
    key = (func.view.file.session_id, func.start)
    enabled = (workflow._enabled(ctx) and ctx.get_setting_bool(settings.CALLEES)
               and (workflow._levels_override is None or "mlil" in workflow._levels_override))
    native_enabled = enabled and ctx.get_setting_bool(settings.CALLEE_NATIVE) and ctx.get_setting_bool(settings.FLOW_FIXES)
    native.observe(func, native_enabled)
    if not enabled:
        with _LOCK:
            _LATEST.pop(key, None)
            _RETRIED.discard(key)
        return
    il = ctx.lifted_il
    if il is None:
        return
    report = Report()
    completion.touch(func.view)
    config = settings.callee_limits(ctx)
    seconds = budget.plugin_allowance(ctx.get_setting_uint64(settings.FUNCTION_SECONDS),
                                      limits.in_effect_ms(func, workflow._analysis_limit_ms(ctx)))
    deadline = Deadline.after(seconds)
    try:
        sites, report.notes = plan(il, func, config, deadline)
        if sites:
            new = rewrite(il, sites, config, deadline)
            ctx.lifted_il = new
            report.calls = len(sites)
            report.notes.insert(0, f"{len(sites)} call sites substituted; proven by exact IL copies preserving register and flag effects")
            for site in sites.values():
                if site.summary.function.inline_during_analysis.value:
                    report.notes.append(f"native inline flag left call at {il[site.index].address:#x}; used checked substitution")
            if native_enabled:
                native.request(func, sites, config)
        if any("lifted IL unavailable" in line for line in report.notes):
            with _LOCK:
                retry = key not in _RETRIED
                _RETRIED.add(key)
            if retry:
                apply.defer_reanalysis(func)
    except (ValueError, NotImplementedError) as exc:
        report.notes.append(f"left unchanged: {exc}")
    except Exception as exc:
        # The new IL is assigned only after every copied operation has passed its exact check.
        report.notes.append(f"left unchanged: {exc!r}")
        completion.failed(func.view)
        log.logger.log_error(f"{func.start:#x} callee summaries failed: {exc!r}")
    finally:
        report.seconds, report.cpu_seconds = time.monotonic() - started, time.thread_time() - cpu
        report.exhausted = deadline.expired()
        with _LOCK:
            _LATEST[key] = report

```

`binja_d810/binja/callees/calls.py`:

```py
"""The small architecture boundary for ordinary call links; no instruction-text matching."""

from binaryninja import LowLevelILOperation as Op


CALL_MODELS = {"aarch64": "link", "x86_64": "stack", "x86": "stack"}


def target(func, node):
    if node.operation != Op.LLIL_CALL:
        raise ValueError("not an ordinary call")
    if node.attributes:
        raise ValueError("call has unmodeled attributes")
    if node.dest.operation not in (Op.LLIL_CONST, Op.LLIL_CONST_PTR):
        raise ValueError("indirect call")
    if func.get_call_type_adjustment(node.address) is not None:
        raise ValueError("user call type")
    callee = func.view.get_function_at(node.dest.constant)
    if callee is None or callee.arch != func.arch:
        raise ValueError("callee unavailable")
    flag = callee.inline_during_analysis
    if not flag.value and flag.confidence:
        raise ValueError("callee has an explicit no-inline flag")
    return callee


def return_address(func, node):
    info = func.arch.get_instruction_info(func.view.read(node.address, func.arch.max_instr_length), node.address)
    if info is None or info.length <= 0:
        raise ValueError("call length unavailable")
    return node.address + info.length

`binja_d810/binja/callees/frame.py`:

```py
"""Prove scratch writes dead in a bounded straight-line caller, byte by byte.

All calls must have body summaries. Unknown effects and control-flow splits fail closed;
the general CFG liveness pass can extend this boundary without weakening the proof here.
Writes are tracked through complete overwrites. A partial overwrite never kills other bytes.
"""

from binaryninja import LowLevelILOperation as Op

from ...ir.expr import BinOp, Const, Var, variables
from ...summaries.frame import Frame
from ...summaries.abi import red_zone
from ...semantic.verify import Verdict, check
from .lift import Lifter, frame_offset


class TrackedFrame(Frame):
    def __init__(self, *args):
        super().__init__(*args)
        self.owner = None
        self.origins = {}
        self.live = set()
        self.stores = {}
        self.outside = set()
        self.stack_position = lambda: None

    def read(self, offset, size):
        for at in range(offset, offset + size):
            writer = self.origins.get(at)
            if writer is not None and writer != self.owner:
                self.live.add(writer)
        return super().read(offset, size)

    def write(self, offset, value):
        super().write(offset, value)
        if self.owner is not None:
            stack = self.stack_position()
            if stack is None or offset < stack or offset + value.width // 8 > 0:
                self.outside.add(self.owner)
        for at in range(offset, offset + value.width // 8):
            self.origins[at] = self.owner
            if self.owner is not None:
                self.stores.setdefault(self.owner, set()).add(at)


def prove(il, func, summaries, returns, limits, deadline):
    """Returns accepted call indices and a reason. No guessed call parameters or alias flags."""
    if len(il) > limits.caller_instructions:
        return set(), "caller-frame instruction limit"
    lifter = Lifter(func, limits, deadline)
    lifter.frame = frame = TrackedFrame(limits.frame_bytes, lifter.frame.little_endian)
    stack_name, size = func.arch.stack_pointer, func.arch.address_size
    reserve = red_zone(func.platform.name, func.arch.name, limits.red_zone_bytes)
    stack_reg = lifter.register(stack_name, size)
    def minimum_stack():
        offset = frame_offset(lifter.state.values[stack_name], stack_name, size * 8)
        return None if offset is None else offset - reserve
    frame.stack_position = minimum_stack
    lowest = -reserve
    instructions = list(il.instructions)
    if not instructions or instructions[-1].operation != Op.LLIL_RET:
        return set(), "caller-frame control flow is not a single return"
    try:
        for node in instructions[:-1]:
            if node.operation == Op.LLIL_CALL:
                summary = summaries.get(node.instr_index)
                if summary is None:
                    return set(), "caller-frame use crosses an unproved call"
                value = Const(returns[node.instr_index], size * 8)
                if summary.stack_return:
                    before = lifter.state.values[stack_name]
                    adjusted = BinOp("sub", before, Const(size, size * 8), size * 8)
                    lifter.state.write(stack_reg, adjusted)
                    offset = frame_offset(adjusted, stack_name, size * 8)
                    if offset is None:
                        return set(), "unknown caller stack position"
                    frame.write(offset, value)
                else:
                    lifter.state.write(lifter.register(func.arch.link_reg, size), value)
                frame.owner = node.instr_index
                for inner in summary.body:
                    lifter.execute(inner)
                    offset = frame_offset(lifter.state.values[stack_name], stack_name, size * 8)
                    if offset is None:
                        return set(), "unknown callee stack position"
                    lowest = min(lowest, offset - reserve)
                frame.owner = None
                if summary.stack_return:
                    lifter.expr(list(summary.lifted.instructions)[-1].dest)
            else:
                lifter.statement(node)
            offset = frame_offset(lifter.state.values[stack_name], stack_name, size * 8)
            if offset is None:
                return set(), "unknown caller stack position"
            lowest = min(lowest, offset - reserve)
        if lifter.state.values[stack_name] != Var(stack_name, size * 8):
            return set(), "unbalanced caller frame"
        end = instructions[-1]
        if end.attributes:
            return set(), "caller return has unmodeled attributes"
        if func.arch.link_reg is not None:
            returned = lifter.expr(end.dest)
            if check(returned, Var(func.arch.link_reg, size * 8), deadline=deadline,
                     z3_timeout_ms=limits.proof_ms).verdict is not Verdict.PROVEN:
                return set(), "caller return target is not preserved"
        elif end.dest.operation != Op.LLIL_POP or end.dest.size != size:
            return set(), "caller has no ordinary stack return"
        else:
            frame.read(0, size)  # return-address reads matter for byte liveness too
        # Any frame-derived register result could escape through the private convention too.
        for name, value in lifter.state.outputs().items():
            if name != stack_name and any(v.name == stack_name for v in variables(value)):
                return set(), "caller-frame address may escape in a register"
        accepted = {index for index, addresses in frame.stores.items()
                    if index not in frame.live | frame.outside and all(lowest <= at < 0 for at in addresses)}
        return accepted, "scratch bytes are read, outside the local frame, or otherwise unproved"
    except (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError) as exc:
        return set(), str(exc)

```

`binja_d810/binja/callees/lift.py`:

```py
"""Read leaf semantics before ABI inference discards nonstandard register results.

Frame accesses are represented explicitly, not declared pure. The caller must prove that
scratch writes cannot escape or be read after the call before a summary can be applied.
Implicit flag writes are retained in the source body; flag reads are not summarized here.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass

from binaryninja import Endianness, ILInstructionAttribute as Attr, LowLevelILOperation as Op

from ...deadline import Deadline
from ...ir.evaluate import evaluate
from ...ir.expr import BinOp, Const, Expr, UnOp, Var, distinct_nodes, to_signed, variables
from ...ir.normalize import normalize
from ...summaries.frame import Frame
from ...summaries.state import Register, State
from ...semantic.verify import Verdict, check
from ..memory import fixed_load_is_safe
from .calls import CALL_MODELS, return_address, target


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Limits:
    instructions: int = 64
    nodes: int = 2000
    frame_bytes: int = 256
    depth: int = 4
    caller_instructions: int = 4096
    proof_ms: int = 500
    sites: int = 64
    red_zone_bytes: int = 128


@dataclass
class Summary:
    function: object
    lifted: object
    outputs: dict[str, Expr]
    inputs: frozenset[str]
    frame_outputs: dict[int, Expr]
    frame_inputs: frozenset[int]
    flag_writes: frozenset[str]
    stack_return: bool
    body: tuple
    expanded_instructions: int


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Nested:
    node: object
    summary: Summary
    return_address: int


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Result:
    summary: Summary | None = None
    reason: str = ""


_BINARY = {Op.LLIL_ADD: "add", Op.LLIL_SUB: "sub", Op.LLIL_MUL: "mul", Op.LLIL_AND: "and",
           Op.LLIL_OR: "or", Op.LLIL_XOR: "xor", Op.LLIL_LSL: "shl", Op.LLIL_LSR: "lshr",
           Op.LLIL_ASR: "ashr", Op.LLIL_ROL: "rol", Op.LLIL_ROR: "ror"}
_UNARY = {Op.LLIL_NEG: "neg", Op.LLIL_NOT: "not", Op.LLIL_ZX: "zx", Op.LLIL_SX: "sx",
          Op.LLIL_LOW_PART: "trunc"}
_COMPARE = {Op.LLIL_CMP_E: "eq", Op.LLIL_CMP_NE: "ne", Op.LLIL_CMP_ULT: "ult", Op.LLIL_CMP_ULE: "ule",
            Op.LLIL_CMP_UGT: "ugt", Op.LLIL_CMP_UGE: "uge", Op.LLIL_CMP_SLT: "slt", Op.LLIL_CMP_SLE: "sle",
            Op.LLIL_CMP_SGT: "sgt", Op.LLIL_CMP_SGE: "sge"}
_EXTEND = {"NoExtend": "preserve", "ZeroExtendToFullWidth": "zero", "SignExtendToFullWidth": "sign"}


def frame_offset(expr, stack: str, width: int):
    """An exact modular displacement from the incoming stack pointer."""
    if expr == Var(stack, width):
        return 0
    if isinstance(expr, BinOp) and expr.op in ("add", "sub"):
        if isinstance(expr.right, Const):
            left = frame_offset(expr.left, stack, width)
            if left is not None:
                return to_signed(left + (expr.right.value if expr.op == "add" else -expr.right.value), width)
        if expr.op == "add" and isinstance(expr.left, Const):
            right = frame_offset(expr.right, stack, width)
            if right is not None:
                return to_signed(right + expr.left.value, width)
    return None


class Lifter:
    def __init__(self, func, limits: Limits, deadline: Deadline, factory=None, depth=0):
        self.func, self.arch, self.limits, self.deadline = func, func.arch, limits, deadline
        self.factory, self.depth = factory, depth
        self.state = State({name: info.size * 8 for name, info in self.arch.regs.items()
                            if name == info.full_width_reg})
        self.frame = Frame(limits.frame_bytes, self.arch.endianness == Endianness.LittleEndian)
        self.visits = 0
        self.flags = set()

    def tick(self):
        self.visits += 1
        if self.deadline.expired():
            raise ValueError("time budget exhausted")
        if self.visits > self.limits.nodes:
            raise ValueError("summary node limit")

    def register(self, reg, size):
        name = str(reg)
        info = self.arch.regs.get(name)
        if info is None or size <= 0 or size > info.size:
            raise ValueError("unsupported register view")
        extend = _EXTEND.get(info.extend.name)
        if extend is None:
            raise ValueError("unknown register extension")
        return Register(info.full_width_reg, size * 8, info.offset * 8, extend)

    def expr(self, node):
        self.tick()
        if node.attributes & {Attr.SrcInstructionUsesPointerAuth, Attr.ILPreventDeadStoreElimination,
                              Attr.ILPreventAliasAnalysis}:
            raise ValueError("callee expression has protected effects")
        op, bits = node.operation, node.size * 8
        if node.flags:
            written = self.arch.flags_written_by_flag_write_type.get(node.flags)
            if written is None:
                raise ValueError("unknown flag write")
            self.flags.update(written)
        if op in (Op.LLIL_CONST, Op.LLIL_CONST_PTR):
            return Const(node.constant, bits)
        if op == Op.LLIL_REG:
            return self.state.read(self.register(node.src, node.size))
        if op in _BINARY or op in _COMPARE:
            left, right = self.expr(node.left), self.expr(node.right)
            return BinOp(_BINARY.get(op) or _COMPARE[op], left, right, 1 if op in _COMPARE else bits)
        if op in _UNARY:
            value = self.expr(node.src)
            return value if value.width == bits and op in (Op.LLIL_ZX, Op.LLIL_SX, Op.LLIL_LOW_PART) \
                else UnOp(_UNARY[op], value, bits)
        if op == Op.LLIL_LOAD:
            address = self.expr(node.src)
            offset = frame_offset(address, self.arch.stack_pointer, self.arch.address_size * 8)
            if offset is not None:
                return self.frame.read(offset, node.size)
            if variables(address):
                raise ValueError("load from unknown memory")
            at = evaluate(address, {})
            segment = self.func.view.get_segment_at(at)
            if not fixed_load_is_safe(self.func.view, at, node.size) or segment.writable \
                    or self.func.view.relocation_ranges_in_range(at, node.size):
                raise ValueError("load is not fixed read-only data")
            raw = self.func.view.read(at, node.size)
            if len(raw) != node.size:
                raise ValueError("incomplete read-only data")
            order = "little" if self.arch.endianness == Endianness.LittleEndian else "big"
            return Const(int.from_bytes(raw, order), bits)
        if op == Op.LLIL_POP:
            stack = self.state.read(self.register(self.arch.stack_pointer, self.arch.address_size))
            offset = frame_offset(stack, self.arch.stack_pointer, self.arch.address_size * 8)
            if offset is None:
                raise ValueError("unknown stack position")
            value = self.frame.read(offset, node.size)
            self.state.write(self.register(self.arch.stack_pointer, self.arch.address_size),
                             BinOp("add", stack, Const(node.size, stack.width), stack.width))
            return value
        raise ValueError(f"unsupported expression: {op.name}")

    def statement(self, node):
        self.tick()
        if node.attributes & {Attr.SrcInstructionUsesPointerAuth, Attr.ILPreventDeadStoreElimination,
                              Attr.ILPreventAliasAnalysis}:
            raise ValueError("callee statement has protected effects")
        if node.operation == Op.LLIL_NOP:
            return
        if node.operation in (Op.LLIL_REG, Op.LLIL_POP):
            self.expr(node)  # return operands retained by an already-substituted nested helper
            return
        if node.operation == Op.LLIL_CALL:
            if self.factory is None:
                raise ValueError("call needs a nested summary")
            result = self.factory.get(target(self.func, node), self.depth + 1)
            if result.summary is None:
                raise ValueError(f"nested summary: {result.reason}")
            nested = Nested(node, result.summary, return_address(self.func, node))
            self.execute(nested)
            return nested
        if node.operation == Op.LLIL_SET_REG:
            reg = self.register(node.dest, node.size)
            value = self.expr(node.src)
            if distinct_nodes(value) > self.limits.nodes:
                raise ValueError("summary expression limit")
            self.state.write(reg, value)
            return
        if node.operation == Op.LLIL_PUSH:
            value = self.expr(node.src)
            reg = self.register(self.arch.stack_pointer, self.arch.address_size)
            stack = self.state.read(reg)
            address = BinOp("sub", stack, Const(node.size, stack.width), stack.width)
            self.state.write(reg, address)
        elif node.operation == Op.LLIL_STORE:
            address, value = self.expr(node.dest), self.expr(node.src)
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"unsupported statement: {node.operation.name}")
        offset = frame_offset(address, self.arch.stack_pointer, self.arch.address_size * 8)
        if offset is None:
            raise ValueError("write outside the frame")
        self.frame.write(offset, value)

    def execute(self, entry):
        if not isinstance(entry, Nested):
            self.statement(entry)
            return
        summary = entry.summary
        mode = CALL_MODELS.get(self.arch.name)
        if mode is None or summary.stack_return != (mode == "stack"):
            raise ValueError("unsupported nested call-link semantics")
        size = self.arch.address_size
        value = Const(entry.return_address, size * 8)
        if summary.stack_return:
            reg = self.register(self.arch.stack_pointer, size)
            stack = self.state.read(reg)
            adjusted = BinOp("sub", stack, Const(size, size * 8), size * 8)
            offset = frame_offset(adjusted, self.arch.stack_pointer, size * 8)
            if offset is None:
                raise ValueError("unknown nested stack position")
            self.state.write(reg, adjusted)
            self.frame.write(offset, value)
        else:
            self.state.write(self.register(self.arch.link_reg, size), value)
        for child in summary.body:
            self.execute(child)
        self.expr(list(summary.lifted.instructions)[-1].dest)

    def summary(self):
        il = self.func.lifted_il_if_available
        if il is None:
            return Result(reason="callee lifted IL unavailable")
        if len(il) > self.limits.instructions:
            return Result(reason="callee instruction limit")
        instructions = list(il.instructions)
        if not instructions or instructions[-1].operation != Op.LLIL_RET:
