`binja_d810/binja/mlil/adapter.py`:

```py
"""ILAdapter for MLIL: the v1 pass behind the engine's IL-independent contract."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Hashable, Iterator, Optional

from binaryninja import (
    ILSourceLocation, MediumLevelILFunction, MediumLevelILInstruction, MediumLevelILOperation as Op, RegisterValueType,
    SSAVariable,
)

from ...deadline import Deadline
from ...ir.expr import Expr, is_candidate, tree_size
from ...ir.paths import Merge, path_variants
from ..adapter import Candidate, Skip
from ..deadcode import dead_with_checks, dying_with_root, shown_in
from ..memory import FixedLoads
from ..ssa import definition_of, reaching as ssa_reaching
from .lift import DIVISION_OPS, SUPPORTED_OPS, candidate_roots, is_safe_division, lift, lift_value
from .lower import lower

_ARITH = frozenset({Op.MLIL_ADD, Op.MLIL_SUB, Op.MLIL_MUL, Op.MLIL_NEG, Op.MLIL_LSL})
_BITWISE = frozenset({Op.MLIL_AND, Op.MLIL_OR, Op.MLIL_XOR, Op.MLIL_NOT})
_COMBINING = frozenset({Op.MLIL_AND, Op.MLIL_OR, Op.MLIL_XOR})
_COMPARES = frozenset({Op.MLIL_CMP_E, Op.MLIL_CMP_NE, Op.MLIL_CMP_ULT, Op.MLIL_CMP_ULE, Op.MLIL_CMP_UGT,
                       Op.MLIL_CMP_UGE, Op.MLIL_CMP_SLT, Op.MLIL_CMP_SLE, Op.MLIL_CMP_SGT, Op.MLIL_CMP_SGE})
_SHARED_FACTOR = 4  # distinct nodes allowed for a shared-value lift, as a multiple of maxNodes
_PURE_LEAVES = frozenset({Op.MLIL_VAR_SSA, Op.MLIL_VAR_SSA_FIELD, Op.MLIL_CONST, Op.MLIL_CONST_PTR})
_COPIES = frozenset({Op.MLIL_VAR_SSA, Op.MLIL_VAR_SSA_FIELD})
# Flags a rewrite may leave dead (cond:0 = t != 0 once t's 0/1 value is inlined): pure, never trap.
_PURE_FLAGS = frozenset({Op.MLIL_CMP_E, Op.MLIL_CMP_NE, Op.MLIL_BOOL_TO_INT})
_FIXED_LOADS = frozenset({Op.MLIL_LOAD_SSA, Op.MLIL_LOAD_STRUCT_SSA})


class MLILAdapter:
    level = "mlil"

    def __init__(self, mlil: MediumLevelILFunction, max_nodes: int = 200, deadline: Deadline = Deadline.never()):
        self.mlil = mlil
        self.max_nodes = max_nodes
        # Enumeration lifts every root; in a large function with no MBA that is all the work, and
        # the engine only sees candidates it is given (one large export: 60 s, Binary Ninja gave up).
        self.deadline = deadline
        self.backups: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
        self.fixed_loads = FixedLoads(mlil.source_function.view)

    def has_candidates(self) -> bool:
        seen, combining = set(), 0
        for instr in self.mlil.instructions:
            if self.deadline.expired():
                return False
            rejected: list = []
            found = [op for root in candidate_roots(instr, rejected, divisions=False)  # operations seen either way
                     for op in _operations(root)]
            found += [op for expr, _ in rejected for op in _operations(expr)]
            seen.update(found)
            combining += sum(1 for op in found if op in _COMBINING)
        # MBA, a comparison over a bitwise operation or a product (opaque predicates), or bitwise
        # operations enough for substitution junk ((x & y) | (x ^ y) across instructions)
        return (bool(seen & _ARITH) and bool(seen & _BITWISE)) or (
            bool(seen & _COMPARES) and (bool(seen & _BITWISE) or Op.MLIL_MUL in seen)) or combining >= 2

    def candidates(self, skip: Skip) -> Iterator[Candidate]:
        if self.mlil.ssa_form is None:
            self.mlil.generate_ssa_form()
        definitions: dict = {}  # SSA definitions, shared by every lift of this SSA form
        for instr in reversed(list(self.mlil.instructions)):
            if self.deadline.expired():
                return
            rejected: list = []
            roots = list(candidate_roots(instr, rejected))
            for expr, reason in rejected:
                seen = lift(expr.ssa_form, root_instr=instr, max_nodes=self.max_nodes, effect_leaves=True,
                            definitions=definitions)
                if seen is not None and is_candidate(seen):
                    skip(expr.address, reason, seen)
            for root in reversed(roots):
                inlined: dict = {}
                stats: dict = {}
                ir = lift(root.ssa_form, root_instr=instr, max_nodes=self.max_nodes, inlined=inlined,
                          definitions=definitions, stats=stats)
                shared = None
                if stats.get("budget_hit"):
                    # Too large as a tree (v3.1): values read several times, as in an opaque
                    # predicate's masked-constant chain, counted once. Only a proven constant may
                    # come from it, so versions are not checked (as the unchecked lift below).
                    dag = lift(root.ssa_form, root_instr=instr, check_versions=False, shared_once=True,
                               max_nodes=_SHARED_FACTOR * self.max_nodes, definitions=definitions)
                    if dag is not None and tree_size(dag) > self.max_nodes and is_candidate(dag):
                        shared = dag
                unchecked = through = None
                unchecked_inlined: dict = {}
                if root.operation in _COMPARES or ir is None:
                    # A condition, or a root the version-safe lift could not see at all: a proven
                    # constant reads no variable, so it may come from a lift through inputs whose
                    # registers were reused before the root (x86-64 -O2). Not values the checked lift
                    # saw partly (stale inputs): folding two such values in mba_linear_030 (x86-64
                    # -O2) made Binary Ninja's HLIL drop the result's definition. Also the base of a
                    # condition's per-path variants, even beside a lift over shared values.
                    unchecked = through = lift(root.ssa_form, root_instr=instr, check_versions=False,
                                               max_nodes=self.max_nodes, inlined=unchecked_inlined,
                                               definitions=definitions)
                    if unchecked is not None and not is_candidate(unchecked):
                        unchecked = None
                constant_only = (ir is None or not is_candidate(ir)) and unchecked is not None
                if shared is not None and (ir is None or not is_candidate(ir)) and unchecked is None:
                    ir, inlined, constant_only = shared, {}, True
                elif constant_only:
                    ir, inlined = unchecked, unchecked_inlined
                paths = None
                if root.operation in _COMPARES and (ir is None or not is_candidate(ir)) and unchecked is None:
                    # A condition over merged values whose per-path variants are candidates (k != 0 with
                    # k = phi((x - 1) * x & 1, (x + x * x) & 1)): constant-only, from its paths.
                    alternatives = None if through is None else self._path_variants(through, instr)
                    if alternatives and any(is_candidate(v) for variants in alternatives for v in variants):
                        ir, inlined, constant_only, paths = through, {}, True, tuple(map(tuple, alternatives))
                if ir is not None and (is_candidate(ir) or paths is not None):
                    defines, single = self._defines(instr, root)
                    nodes, mixed, dying = self._visible(instr, root, inlined)
                    yield Candidate(root, root.address, ir, defines, single, frozenset(inlined), nodes, mixed,
                                    instr, frozenset(inlined) - dying, unchecked, constant_only, shared,
                                    self._consumer_kinds(instr, root), self.root_kinds, paths)

    def shallow(self, candidate: Candidate, keep: Optional[frozenset] = None) -> Optional[Candidate]:
        """The root lifted with `keep` (default: the definitions that stay alive) as leaves where
        they are live (ILAdapter.shallow)."""
        keep = candidate.shared if keep is None else keep
        if not keep or candidate.context is None:
            return None
        instr, root = candidate.context, candidate.root
        inlined: dict = {}
        ir = lift(root.ssa_form, root_instr=instr, max_nodes=self.max_nodes, inlined=inlined, keep=keep)
        if ir is None:  # bitwise-only is fine: Tier 1 rules simplify it (a ^ 0xff00ff)
            return None
        defines, single = self._defines(instr, root)
        nodes, mixed, _ = self._visible(instr, root, inlined)
        # The same statement as the candidate's: the same gate (v3.1 statement kinds).
        return Candidate(root, root.address, ir, defines, single, frozenset(inlined), nodes, mixed, instr,
                         consumer_kinds=self._consumer_kinds(instr, root), root_kinds=self.root_kinds)

    def path_variants(self, candidate: Candidate) -> Optional[list[list[Expr]]]:
        """The candidate's condition once per incoming path of the merged values it reads (spec v3.2
        goal 3), from its lift through every input (versions unchecked: only a proven constant may
        come from it), as alternatives: invariant merges alone, then every merge split (v3.3).
        Conditions only; None when it reads no merged value."""
        if candidate.context is None or candidate.root.operation not in _COMPARES:
            return None
        base = candidate.unchecked if candidate.unchecked is not None else candidate.ir
        return self._path_variants(base, candidate.context)

    def _path_variants(self, base: Expr, instr: MediumLevelILInstruction) -> Optional[list[Expr]]:
        merges: dict = {}
        definitions: dict = {}

        def merge_of(leaf) -> Optional[Merge]:
            if not isinstance(leaf.ref, SSAVariable):
                return None
            key = (leaf.ref.var.identifier, leaf.ref.version, leaf.width)
            if key not in merges:
                merges[key] = self._merge(leaf.ref, leaf.width, instr, definitions)
            return merges[key]

        alternatives = []
        for invariant_only in (True, False):
            variants = path_variants(base, merge_of, invariant_only=invariant_only)
            if variants and variants not in alternatives:
                alternatives.append(variants)
        return alternatives or None

    def _merge(self, ssa_var: SSAVariable, width: int, instr: MediumLevelILInstruction,
               definitions: dict) -> Optional[Merge]:
        """A phi's block and its incoming value along each of the block's incoming edges: the version
        of the variable at the end of the edge's source block, which must be one of the phi's sources."""
        ssa = self.mlil.ssa_form
        phi = definition_of(ssa, ssa_var, definitions)
        if phi is None or phi.operation != Op.MLIL_VAR_PHI:
            return None
        source = _invariant_source(ssa, ssa_var, definitions)
        if source is not None:
            # Every value of the merge is some instance of `source` (v3.3): one incoming value, which
            # path_variants renames apart like any other.
            return Merge(f"invariant:{ssa_var.var.identifier}:{ssa_var.version}",
                         (lift_value(ssa, source, width, root_instr=instr, max_nodes=self.max_nodes,
                                     definitions=definitions),))
        sources = {(s.var.identifier, s.version) for s in phi.src}
        block = phi.il_basic_block
        incoming = []
        for edge in block.incoming_edges:
            reaching = ssa_reaching(ssa, edge.source, ssa_var.var)
            if reaching is None or (reaching.var.identifier, reaching.version) not in sources:
                return None
            incoming.append(lift_value(ssa, reaching, width, root_instr=instr, max_nodes=self.max_nodes,
                                       definitions=definitions))
        return Merge(block.index, tuple(incoming))

    def _visible(self, instr: MediumLevelILInstruction, root: MediumLevelILInstruction, inlined: dict):
        """Size and mix of what the user sees: the root plus the definitions that die with it."""
        ssa = self.mlil.ssa_form
        definitions = {key: ssa.get_ssa_var_definition(var) for key, var in inlined.items()}
        definitions = {key: d for key, d in definitions.items() if d is not None and hasattr(d, "src")}
        uses = {key: [u.instr_index for u in ssa.get_ssa_var_uses(inlined[key])] for key in definitions}
        dying = dying_with_root(uses, {key: d.instr_index for key, d in definitions.items()},
                                instr.ssa_form.instr_index)
        # Copies (rax_6 = var_24 at -O0) are not counted: HLIL propagates them away, so a rewrite
        # that only removes copies while duplicating a kept value's definition grows the code shown.
        trees = [root] + [definitions[key].src for key in dying if definitions[key].src.operation not in _COPIES]
        # Mixed if one statement as HLIL shows it is. Single-use temporaries fold into their use
        # (three-address MBA: t = a + 3; u = t | b reads as one mixed line); a value used several times
        # is a statement of its own (OLLVM: a = x * 7 + y read twice by (a & M) | (~a & ~M) —
        # each unmixed, and merging them is what the gate refuses).
        statements: dict = {None: set(_operations(root))}
        shown = shown_in(dying, uses, {key: d.instr_index for key, d in definitions.items()},
                         instr.ssa_form.instr_index)
        for key in dying:
            statements.setdefault(shown[key], set()).update(_operations(definitions[key].src))
        mixed = any(ops & _ARITH and ops & _BITWISE for ops in statements.values())
        self.root_kinds = _kinds(statements[None])
        return sum(_size(tree) for tree in trees), mixed, dying

    def _consumer_kinds(self, instr: MediumLevelILInstruction, root: MediumLevelILInstruction) -> Optional[frozenset]:
        """The kinds of the statements the root's value flows into through single uses, as HLIL
        merges them into one statement (v3.1); None if the root is not a whole definition."""
        if instr.operation != Op.MLIL_SET_VAR or instr.src.expr_index != root.expr_index:
            return None
        ssa = self.mlil.ssa_form
        value, kinds = instr.ssa_form.dest, set()
        for _ in range(16):
            uses = ssa.get_ssa_var_uses(value)
            if len(uses) != 1 or uses[0].operation == Op.MLIL_VAR_PHI:
                break
            use = uses[0]
            tree = use.src if use.operation == Op.MLIL_SET_VAR_SSA else use
            kinds |= _kinds(set(_operations(tree)))
            if use.operation != Op.MLIL_SET_VAR_SSA or not _pure(use.src):
                break
            value = use.dest
        return frozenset(kinds)

    def _defines(self, instr: MediumLevelILInstruction, root: MediumLevelILInstruction):
        """The SSA value the root is the whole definition of, and whether it has one use."""
        if instr.operation != Op.MLIL_SET_VAR or instr.src.expr_index != root.expr_index:
            return None, False
        dest = instr.ssa_form.dest
        return _key(dest), len(self.mlil.ssa_form.get_ssa_var_uses(dest)) == 1

    def replace(self, candidate: Candidate, replacement: Expr) -> None:
        root = candidate.root
        loc = ILSourceLocation.from_instruction(root)
        self.backups.append((root.expr_index, root.copy_to(self.mlil)))
        self.mlil.replace_expr(root.expr_index, lower(self.mlil, replacement, loc))

    def propagate_constants(self, rewritten: list[Candidate]) -> int:
        """After a pass (SSA regenerated): reads of a value a rewritten instruction defines, when
        Binary Ninja's dataflow now knows it is a constant, read the constant (v3.1). Covers partial
        writes too (xor r14d, r14d; setne r14b folded: r14 is 1). Exact for the SSA value; phi nodes
        keep their sources (the dataflow carries constants through them). Returns the reads replaced;
        the definitions then die and are removed as newly dead."""
        ssa = self.mlil.ssa_form
        replaced = 0
        for candidate in rewritten:
            if candidate.context is None:
                continue
            instr = self.mlil[candidate.context.instr_index].ssa_form
            if instr.operation not in (Op.MLIL_SET_VAR_SSA, Op.MLIL_SET_VAR_SSA_FIELD):
                continue
            dest = instr.dest
            value = ssa.get_ssa_var_value(dest)
            if value.type != RegisterValueType.ConstantValue:
                continue
            for use in ssa.get_ssa_var_uses(dest):
                if use.operation == Op.MLIL_VAR_PHI:
                    continue
                # The use's own non-SSA instruction: SSA form numbers instructions differently (phi).
                for node, offset in _var_reads(use.non_ssa_form, dest.var):
                    bits = 8 * node.size or 1  # a flag's value is one bit (if (true), spike S2)
                    constant = (value.value >> (8 * offset)) & ((1 << bits) - 1)
                    self.backups.append((node.expr_index, node.copy_to(self.mlil)))
                    self.mlil.replace_expr(node.expr_index, self.mlil.const(node.size, constant,
                                                                            ILSourceLocation.from_instruction(node)))
                    replaced += 1
        return replaced

    def finish(self) -> None:
        self.mlil.finalize()
        self.mlil.generate_ssa_form()

    def dead_assignments(self, pure_loads: frozenset = frozenset()) -> set[Hashable]:
        """Instruction indices of pure SET_VARs whose value is never used, even indirectly.

        At -O0 a rewritten result leaves chains of copies through stack slots behind
        (x8_1 = x8 ^ x9; var_10 = x8_1; x8_2 = var_10; ...), which HLIL would still show. A load from a
        fixed address in the image's data is pure (v3.5: the reads of OLLVM's predicate globals, once the
        predicates fold). So are the loads in `pure_loads` (non-SSA expression indices, v4.0): the table reads
        of a target the flow fixes made constant. Whether a division can trap is decided only for definitions
        about to be removed.
        """
        load = self._fixed_load
        if pure_loads:
            load = lambda node: node.non_ssa_form.expr_index in pure_loads or self._fixed_load(node)  # noqa: E731
        pure, roots, index_of, checks = {}, [], {}, {}
        for instr in self.mlil.ssa_form.instructions:
            divisions: list = []
            if instr.operation == Op.MLIL_SET_VAR_SSA and _pure(instr.src, load, divisions):
                key = _key(instr.dest)
                pure[key] = [_key(v) for v in _ssa_vars(instr.src)]
                index_of[key] = instr.non_ssa_form.instr_index
            elif instr.operation == Op.MLIL_SET_VAR_SSA_FIELD and _pure(instr.src, load, divisions):
                # A partial write (var_8:5.b = x ^ y at -O0) reads the previous version as well.
                key = _key(instr.dest)
                pure[key] = [_key(instr.prev)] + [_key(v) for v in _ssa_vars(instr.src)]
                index_of[key] = instr.non_ssa_form.instr_index
            elif instr.operation == Op.MLIL_VAR_PHI:
                # A merge is not a use: its sources live only if its result does (a folded
                # predicate's per-path values, merged at -O0 through a stack slot). Not removable.
                pure[_key(instr.dest)] = [_key(v) for v in instr.src]
                continue
            else:
                roots.extend(_key(v) for v in _ssa_vars(instr))
                continue
            if divisions:
                checks[key] = lambda found=tuple(divisions): all(is_safe_division(d, d) for d in found)
        return {index_of[key] for key in dead_with_checks(pure, roots, checks) if key in index_of}

    def _fixed_load(self, node: MediumLevelILInstruction) -> bool:
        """A load from a constant address in the image's data (binja_d810.binja.memory)."""
        address = node.src
        if address.operation not in (Op.MLIL_CONST_PTR, Op.MLIL_CONST):
            return False
        offset = node.offset if node.operation == Op.MLIL_LOAD_STRUCT_SSA else 0
        return self.fixed_loads(address.constant + offset, node.size)

    def remove(self, dead: set[Hashable]) -> None:
        for index in sorted(dead):
            instr = self.mlil[index]
            self.backups.append((instr.expr_index, instr.copy_to(self.mlil)))
            self.mlil.replace_expr(instr.expr_index, self.mlil.nop(ILSourceLocation.from_instruction(instr)))

    def cfg_shape(self) -> tuple:
        return tuple((bb.start, bb.end, self.mlil[bb.end - 1].operation) for bb in self.mlil.basic_blocks)

    def restore(self) -> None:
        for expr_index, backup in reversed(self.backups):
            self.mlil.replace_expr(expr_index, backup)
        if self.backups:
            self.finish()
        self.backups.clear()


def _invariant_source(ssa, ssa_var: SSAVariable, definitions: Optional[dict] = None,
                      limit: int = 64) -> Optional[SSAVariable]:
    """The one value entering a web of merges and whole copies from outside it, if there is exactly one
    (v3.3): i = phi(i0, i'), i' = esi, esi = phi(i0, i), as an opaque predicate's y * y + 3 is carried round a loop.
    Every member then holds some instance of that value. None otherwise."""
    shared = definitions is not None
    definitions = {} if definitions is None else definitions
    web, outside, stack = set(), {}, [ssa_var]
    while stack:
        var = stack.pop()
        key = (var.var.identifier, var.version)
        if key in web or key in outside:
            continue
        definition = definition_of(ssa, var, definitions, by_storage=shared)
        if definition is not None and definition.operation == Op.MLIL_VAR_PHI:
            web.add(key)
            stack.extend(definition.src)
        elif (definition is not None and definition.operation == Op.MLIL_SET_VAR_SSA
              and definition.src.operation == Op.MLIL_VAR_SSA and definition.src.size == definition.size):
            web.add(key)
            stack.append(definition.src.src)
        else:
            outside[key] = var
        if len(web) + len(outside) > limit or len(outside) > 1:
            return None
    return next(iter(outside.values())) if len(outside) == 1 else None


def _operations(e: MediumLevelILInstruction):
    stack = [e]
    while stack:
        node = stack.pop()
        yield node.operation
        stack.extend(op for op in node.operands if isinstance(op, MediumLevelILInstruction))


def _size(e: MediumLevelILInstruction) -> int:
    return sum(1 for _ in _operations(e))


def _pure(e: MediumLevelILInstruction, load=None, divisions: Optional[list] = None) -> bool:
    """`load(node)`: whether a load is pure (a fixed address that cannot fault, v3.5); without it no load
    is. `divisions` collects the divisions, pure until checked (deadcode.dead_with_checks); without it a
    division is checked here."""
    if e.operation in _PURE_LEAVES:
        return True
    if e.operation in _FIXED_LOADS:
        return load is not None and load(e)
    if e.operation in DIVISION_OPS:
        if divisions is None:
            return is_safe_division(e, e)  # cannot trap: removable once dead
        divisions.append(e)
        return True
    if e.operation not in SUPPORTED_OPS and e.operation not in _PURE_FLAGS:
        return False
    return all(_pure(op, load, divisions) for op in e.operands if isinstance(op, MediumLevelILInstruction))


def _ssa_vars(e: MediumLevelILInstruction):
    """Every SSA variable in an expression tree. MLIL_RET's vars_read is empty, so walk operands.

    For instructions with side effects this also yields what they write (calls, phis), which only
    keeps more alive.
    """
    stack: list = [e]
    while stack:
        item = stack.pop()
        if isinstance(item, SSAVariable):
            yield item
        elif isinstance(item, MediumLevelILInstruction):
            stack.extend(item.operands)
        elif isinstance(item, list):
            stack.extend(item)


def _key(ssa_var: SSAVariable) -> tuple[int, int]:
    return ssa_var.var.identifier, ssa_var.version


def _var_reads(instr: MediumLevelILInstruction, var) -> list:
    """(node, byte offset) for each read of `var` in one non-SSA instruction: whole (MLIL_VAR) or a
    field (MLIL_VAR_FIELD, r14.d). Its destination is not a read."""
    found, stack = [], [instr]
    while stack:
        node = stack.pop()
        if node.operation == Op.MLIL_VAR and node.src == var:  # size 0: a flag (cond:0)
            found.append((node, 0))
            continue
        if node.operation == Op.MLIL_VAR_FIELD and node.src == var and node.size > 0:
            found.append((node, node.offset))
            continue
        for operand in node.operands:
            if isinstance(operand, MediumLevelILInstruction):
                stack.append(operand)
            elif isinstance(operand, list):
                stack.extend(o for o in operand if isinstance(o, MediumLevelILInstruction))
    return found


def _kinds(operations: set) -> frozenset:
    return frozenset(({"arith"} if operations & _ARITH else set()) | ({"bitwise"} if operations & _BITWISE else set()))

```

`binja_d810/binja/mlil/lift.py`:

```py
"""MLIL (SSA) -> binja_d810 IR, following SSA definitions across instructions.

Version safety: every SSA variable left as a leaf must hold the version that is current at the
root instruction, because the rewrite is lowered there and reads variables by name. Binary Ninja
numbers SSA versions per storage location (x and x0 share register x0), so a variable counts as
overwritten when another variable in the same register is written. Intermediate definitions are
inlined, so their own reads need not be live; only the final leaves are checked.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Iterator, Optional

from binaryninja import (
    MediumLevelILInstruction, MediumLevelILOperation as Op, RegisterValueType, SSAVariable, VariableSourceType,
)

from ...ir.expr import COUNT_OPS, BinOp, Const, Expr, UnOp, Var, variables
from ...ir.normalize import narrowed
from ...semantic.traps import never_traps
from ..effects import mlil_effect
from ..ssa import definition_of
from ..storage import (
    as_integer, contained, exact, field_read, fit, merge_partial_write, read_over_write, unary,
)

_BINARY = {Op.MLIL_ADD: "add", Op.MLIL_SUB: "sub", Op.MLIL_MUL: "mul", Op.MLIL_AND: "and",
           Op.MLIL_OR: "or", Op.MLIL_XOR: "xor", Op.MLIL_LSL: "shl", Op.MLIL_LSR: "lshr", Op.MLIL_ASR: "ashr",
           Op.MLIL_ROL: "rol", Op.MLIL_ROR: "ror"}
_UNARY = {Op.MLIL_NEG: "neg", Op.MLIL_NOT: "not", Op.MLIL_ZX: "zx", Op.MLIL_SX: "sx", Op.MLIL_LOW_PART: "trunc"}
_COMPARE = {Op.MLIL_CMP_E: "eq", Op.MLIL_CMP_NE: "ne", Op.MLIL_CMP_ULT: "ult", Op.MLIL_CMP_ULE: "ule",
            Op.MLIL_CMP_UGT: "ugt", Op.MLIL_CMP_UGE: "uge", Op.MLIL_CMP_SLT: "slt", Op.MLIL_CMP_SLE: "sle",
            Op.MLIL_CMP_SGT: "sgt", Op.MLIL_CMP_SGE: "sge"}
_LOADS = frozenset({Op.MLIL_LOAD_SSA, Op.MLIL_LOAD_STRUCT_SSA})
# x86 sbb/adc (v4.2): (l - r) - carry and (l + r) + carry, followed through definitions but never roots.
_CARRY = {Op.MLIL_SBB: "sub", Op.MLIL_ADC: "add"}
SUPPORTED_OPS = frozenset(_BINARY) | frozenset(_UNARY) | frozenset(_COMPARE) | {Op.MLIL_BOOL_TO_INT}
# Division: lifted only when it cannot trap; otherwise an effect, as before.
_DIVIDE = {Op.MLIL_DIVU: "udiv", Op.MLIL_DIVS: "sdiv", Op.MLIL_MODU: "urem", Op.MLIL_MODS: "srem"}
_DIVIDE_DP = {Op.MLIL_DIVU_DP: "udiv", Op.MLIL_DIVS_DP: "sdiv", Op.MLIL_MODU_DP: "urem", Op.MLIL_MODS_DP: "srem"}
DIVISION_OPS = frozenset(_DIVIDE) | frozenset(_DIVIDE_DP)


_UNREAD = object()


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Opaque:
    """Leaf for a pure unsupported sub-expression of the root instruction (non-SSA form)."""

    expr: MediumLevelILInstruction


def candidate_roots(instr: MediumLevelILInstruction, rejected: Optional[list] = None,
                    divisions: bool = True) -> Iterator[MediumLevelILInstruction]:
    """Maximal supported expressions that contain no effect.

    A supported expression containing a load, call or other effect is not a candidate: rewriting
    it could delete, duplicate or reorder the effect (0 & [p] -> 0). Its effect-free supported
    sub-expressions are candidates instead. Each such split is appended to `rejected` as
    (expression, reason). A division that cannot trap is pure; `divisions=False` treats
    every division as an effect without proving anything (the cheap pre-check).
    """
    pure = (lambda node: is_safe_division(node, instr)) if divisions else None

    def visit(e):
        if e.operation in SUPPORTED_OPS:
            reason = mlil_effect(e.ssa_form, pure)
            if reason is None:
                yield e
                return
            if rejected is not None:
                rejected.append((e, reason))
        for operand in e.operands:
            if isinstance(operand, MediumLevelILInstruction):
                yield from visit(operand)
            elif isinstance(operand, list):
                for item in operand:
                    if isinstance(item, MediumLevelILInstruction):
                        yield from visit(item)

    yield from visit(instr)


def is_safe_division(ssa_node: MediumLevelILInstruction, root_instr: MediumLevelILInstruction) -> bool:
    """A division (SSA form) the lifter builds: one that cannot trap for any value of its inputs."""
    return ssa_node.operation in DIVISION_OPS and lift(ssa_node, root_instr=root_instr, check_versions=False) is not None


def lift_value(ssa_func, ssa_var: SSAVariable, width: int, *, root_instr: MediumLevelILInstruction,
               max_nodes: int = 200, definitions: Optional[dict] = None) -> Expr:
    """One SSA value lifted on its own, versions unchecked (a merge's incoming value, spec v3.2 goal 3):
    its definitions inlined, or the value itself as a leaf. Only a proven constant may come from it."""
    lifter = _Lifter(ssa_func, root_instr, False, max_nodes, False, definitions)
    found = lifter.var(ssa_var, width)
    if found is None:
        return Var(f"{ssa_var.var.name}#{ssa_var.version}", width, ref=ssa_var)
    return lifter.relate(found)


def lift_live(ssa_func, ssa_var: SSAVariable, width: int, *, root_instr: MediumLevelILInstruction,
              max_nodes: int = 200, definitions: Optional[dict] = None) -> Optional[Expr]:
    """One SSA value as an expression of values live at `root_instr` (v4.2, a split's condition), or None."""
    lifter = _Lifter(ssa_func, root_instr, True, max_nodes, False, definitions)
    found = lifter.var(ssa_var, width)
    return None if found is None else lifter.relate(found)


def lift(ssa_expr: MediumLevelILInstruction, *, root_instr: MediumLevelILInstruction,
         check_versions: bool = True, max_nodes: int = 200, effect_leaves: bool = False,
         inlined: Optional[set] = None, stats: Optional[dict] = None,
         definitions: Optional[dict] = None, keep: frozenset = frozenset(),
         shared_once: bool = False, load_leaves: bool = False, dataflow: bool = True) -> Optional[Expr]:
    """`effect_leaves` is for diagnostics only: effectful sub-expressions of the root become leaves
    without a Binary Ninja ref, so the result can be classified but never lowered. `stats` receives
    the number of IL nodes visited ("visits"), failed inlining attempts included. `definitions`
    memoizes SSA definitions across lifts of one SSA form. `keep` holds (identifier, version) keys of
    SSA values left as leaves when live at the root (ILAdapter.shallow). `shared_once` (v3.1): a value
    read again costs nothing, so max_nodes bounds the distinct nodes and the result may be far larger
    as a tree (for constancy.fold_shared only). stats["budget_hit"]: the size bound left values as
    leaves (or failed the lift). `load_leaves` (v4.0, flow fixes): every load, inlined definitions
    included, becomes a leaf named load@<SSA expression index> whose ref is the SSA load, so a jump's or
    call's target can be evaluated per table entry. Never lowered. `dataflow` False (v4.2, unflattening): a
    leaf keeps its variable when Binary Ninja's dataflow knows its value, so the variables a test reads show."""
    lifter = _Lifter(ssa_expr.function, root_instr, check_versions, max_nodes, effect_leaves, definitions)
    lifter.keep = keep
    lifter.shared_once = shared_once
    lifter.load_leaves = load_leaves
    lifter.dataflow = dataflow
    e = lifter.expr(ssa_expr, inlined=False)
    if stats is not None:
        stats["visits"] = lifter.visits
        stats["budget_hit"] = lifter.budget_hit
        stats["stale"] = lifter.stale
    if e is not None and inlined is not None:
        inlined.update(lifter.inlined)  # (variable identifier, version) -> SSA variable, each definition followed
    return None if e is None else lifter.relate(e)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Backing:
    """One SSA version of a whole storage location: every bit unknown.

    `var` is a variable living in that storage, used to lower reads of it.
    """

    var: object
    version: int
    size: int  # bytes


class _Lifter:
    def __init__(self, ssa_func, root, check_versions: bool, max_nodes: int, effect_leaves: bool = False,
                 definitions: Optional[dict] = None):
        self.ssa = ssa_func
        self.root = root
        self.check = check_versions
        self.budget = max_nodes
        # Bounded work (v2.1): when values are read several times (VM handlers), the fully inlined
        # tree is exponential and a failed inlining attempt, undone, was retried at every read.
        # Failed attempts are remembered with their budget, inlined values are reused, and no new
        # attempt starts after 3 * max_nodes visits.
        self.visits = 0
        self.max_visits = 3 * max_nodes
        self.failed: dict[tuple, int] = {}  # (identifier, version, width) -> largest budget that failed
        self.done: dict[tuple, tuple] = {}  # (identifier, version, width) -> (expr, nodes, inlined)
        self.shared_cache = definitions is not None
        self.definitions = {} if definitions is None else definitions
        self.keep: frozenset = frozenset()
        self.effect_leaves = effect_leaves
        self.names: dict[tuple, str] = {}  # leaf identity -> IR name; names are labels, not identities
        self.backings: dict[tuple, Var] = {}
        self.inlined: dict[tuple[int, int], object] = {}  # (identifier, version) -> SSA variable
        self.shared_once = False
        self.load_leaves = False
        self.dataflow = True
        self.budget_hit = False
        self.stale = False  # an input was overwritten before the root (version safety stopped inlining)

    def get(self, e, name: str):
        """`e.<name>`, read once per SSA form (v3.3): Binary Ninja builds a new Python object at every
        read of an operand, and roots read the same definitions again and again (one
        large function spent half its budget building them). Shared with `definitions` (other keys)."""
        key = (e.expr_index, name)
        found = self.definitions.get(key, _UNREAD)
        if found is _UNREAD:
            found = self.definitions[key] = getattr(e, name)
        return found

    def expr(self, e: MediumLevelILInstruction, *, inlined: bool) -> Optional[Expr]:
        self.visits += 1
        self.budget -= 1
        if self.budget < 0:
            self.budget_hit = True
            return None
        op, width = e.operation, e.size * 8
        if op in _COMPARE:
            return self.compare(e, inlined=inlined)
        if op == Op.MLIL_VAR_SSA and width == 0:
            return self.boolean(e, inlined=inlined)  # a flag variable (cond:0)
        if width == 0:
            return None
        if op in (Op.MLIL_CONST, Op.MLIL_CONST_PTR):
            return Const(e.constant, width)
        if op == Op.MLIL_VAR_SSA:
            return self.var(self.get(e, "src"), width)
        if op == Op.MLIL_VAR_SSA_FIELD:
            found = self.field(self.get(e, "src"), self.get(e, "offset"), width)
            if found is not None or inlined:
                return found
        elif op in _BINARY:
            left = self.expr(self.get(e, "left"), inlined=inlined)
            right = self.expr(self.get(e, "right"), inlined=inlined)
            if left is None or right is None:
                return None
            left = as_integer(left, width)  # a comparison read as an integer: 0 or 1
            if _BINARY[op] not in COUNT_OPS:
                # HLIL folds lea into x * 5 with an 8-byte constant under a 4-byte multiply.
                left, right = fit(left, width), fit(as_integer(right, width), width)
                if left is None or right is None:
                    return None
            try:
                return BinOp(_BINARY[op], left, right, width)
            except ValueError:
                return None
        elif op in _UNARY:
            operand = self.expr(self.get(e, "src"), inlined=inlined)
            return None if operand is None else unary(_UNARY[op], operand, width)
        elif op in _CARRY:
            return self.with_carry(e, width, inlined=inlined)
        elif op == Op.MLIL_BOOL_TO_INT:
            found = self.boolean(self.get(e, "src"), inlined=inlined)
            if found is not None:
                return UnOp("zx", found, width)
        elif op in DIVISION_OPS:
            found = self.division(e, width, inlined=inlined)
            if found is not None:
                return found
        if self.load_leaves and op in _LOADS:
            # v4.0 flow fixes: a table read, evaluated per entry and never lowered.
            return Var(self.name(("load", e.expr_index), f"load@{e.expr_index}"), width, ref=e)
        if inlined:
            return None  # never move loads or other unsupported expressions across instructions
        if mlil_effect(e) is not None:
            # Only pure leaves may be evaluated again, or not at all.
            return Var(f"effect@{e.expr_index}", width) if self.effect_leaves else None
        return Var(f"opaque@{e.expr_index}", width, ref=Opaque(e.non_ssa_form))

    def with_carry(self, e: MediumLevelILInstruction, width: int, *, inlined: bool) -> Optional[Expr]:
        """sbb.d(l, r, c) = (l - r) - zx(c), adc.d(l, r, c) = (l + r) + zx(c): the carry is a boolean."""
        left = self.expr(self.get(e, "left"), inlined=inlined)
        right = self.expr(self.get(e, "right"), inlined=inlined)
        carry = self.boolean(self.get(e, "carry"), inlined=inlined)
        if left is None or right is None or carry is None:
            return None
        left, right = fit(as_integer(left, width), width), fit(as_integer(right, width), width)
        if left is None or right is None:
            return None
        op = _CARRY[e.operation]
        return BinOp(op, BinOp(op, left, right, width), UnOp("zx", carry, width), width)

    def division(self, e: MediumLevelILInstruction, width: int, *, inlined: bool) -> Optional[Expr]:
        """A division that cannot trap, else None: it stays an effect. Operands
        must have the division's own width (a division reads every bit, so a wider operand is not
        its low bits). x86's double-width forms are the narrow division when the dividend is the
        zero (unsigned) or sign (signed) extension of its low half."""
        saved, saved_inlined = self.budget, dict(self.inlined)
        double = e.operation in _DIVIDE_DP
        op = (_DIVIDE_DP if double else _DIVIDE)[e.operation]
        if double:
            dividend = self.narrow_dividend(self.get(e, "left"), op, width, inlined=inlined)
        else:
            dividend = exact(self.expr(self.get(e, "left"), inlined=inlined), width)
        divisor = exact(self.expr(self.get(e, "right"), inlined=inlined), width) if dividend is not None else None
        if divisor is not None and never_traps(op, dividend, divisor):
            return BinOp(op, dividend, divisor, width)
        self.budget, self.inlined = saved, saved_inlined
        return None

    def narrow_dividend(self, left: MediumLevelILInstruction, op: str, width: int, *, inlined: bool) -> Optional[Expr]:
        """The low half of a double-width dividend (x86 edx:eax) that is the zero (unsigned) or sign
        (signed) extension of it, else None. A dividend Binary Ninja folded to a constant is never
        used: its high half is not visible."""
        ext, wide = ("zx" if op[0] == "u" else "sx"), 2 * width
        if left.operation == Op.MLIL_VAR_SPLIT_SSA:
            whole = self.split_source(self.get(left, "high"), self.get(left, "low"), wide)
            if whole is not None:
                return narrowed(whole, width, ext)  # cdq: edx:eax = sx.q(eax)
            high = self.var(self.get(left, "high"), width)
            if ext == "zx" and high == Const(0, width):
                return self.var(self.get(left, "low"), width)  # xor edx, edx
            return None
        if left.operation in (Op.MLIL_CONST, Op.MLIL_CONST_PTR) or left.size * 8 != wide:
            return None
        whole = self.expr(left, inlined=inlined)
        return None if whole is None else narrowed(whole, width, ext)

    def split_source(self, high: SSAVariable, low: SSAVariable, wide: int) -> Optional[Expr]:
        """The value one instruction wrote to both halves of a split pair (edx:eax = sx.q(eax)),
        followed through whole copies (x86-64: temp4 = rdx; rdx = temp2), as a `wide`-bit value."""
        followed = []
        ends = []
        for ssa_var in (high, low):
            for _ in range(8):
                definition = self.definition_of(ssa_var)
                if definition is None or definition.operation != Op.MLIL_SET_VAR_SSA:
                    break
                src = self.get(definition, "src")
                if src.operation != Op.MLIL_VAR_SSA or src.size != definition.size:
                    break
                followed.append(ssa_var)
                ssa_var = self.get(src, "src")
            ends.append(ssa_var)
        definition = self.definition_of(ends[0])
        if (definition is None or definition.operation != Op.MLIL_SET_VAR_SPLIT_SSA
                or (self.get(definition, "high"), self.get(definition, "low")) != (ends[0], ends[1])
                or self.get(definition, "src").size * 8 != wide):
            return None
        whole = self.expr(self.get(definition, "src"), inlined=True)
        if whole is not None:
            for ssa_var in followed + ends:
                self.inlined[(ssa_var.var.identifier, ssa_var.version)] = ssa_var
        return whole

    def var(self, ssa_var: SSAVariable, width: int) -> Optional[Expr]:
        key = (ssa_var.var.identifier, ssa_var.version, width)
        reused = self.reuse(key)
        if reused is not None:
            return reused
        definition = self.definition_of(ssa_var)
        kept = key[:2] in self.keep and self.live(ssa_var)
        if definition is not None and not kept and self.may_inline(key):
            saved, saved_inlined = self.budget, dict(self.inlined)
            inner = self.definition(definition, ssa_var, width)
            if inner is not None:
                self.inlined[(ssa_var.var.identifier, ssa_var.version)] = ssa_var
                self.remember(key, inner, saved, saved_inlined)
                return inner
            self.failed[key] = max(self.failed.get(key, 0), saved)
            self.budget, self.inlined = saved, saved_inlined
        constant = self.dataflow_constant(ssa_var, definition, width) if self.dataflow else None
        if constant is not None:
            return constant
        if not self.live(ssa_var):
            self.stale = True
            return None  # overwritten before the root and not rebuildable from live values
        # One IR name per (variable, version, width): the verifier keys samples and Z3 symbols by name.
        return Var(self.name(("var", ssa_var.var.identifier, ssa_var.version, width), f"{ssa_var.var.name}#{ssa_var.version}"),
                   width, ref=ssa_var)

    def dataflow_constant(self, ssa_var: SSAVariable, definition, width: int) -> Optional[Const]:
        """Binary Ninja's dataflow value of a leaf, when it is a single constant (v3.1): a merge of
        equal constants (phi), or a definition a rewrite made constant. Never a loaded value: memory
        may change. A constant reads no variable, so it is version-safe."""
        if (definition is not None and definition.operation == Op.MLIL_SET_VAR_SSA
                and self.get(definition, "src").operation in _LOADS):
            return None
        try:
            value = self.ssa.get_ssa_var_value(ssa_var)
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - no dataflow for this variable
            return None
        if value.type != RegisterValueType.ConstantValue:
            return None
        return Const(value.value & ((1 << width) - 1), width)

    def definition_of(self, ssa_var: SSAVariable):
        # By storage when the variable's is missing, with a cache shared by many lifts (binja_d810.binja.ssa).
        return definition_of(self.ssa, ssa_var, self.definitions, by_storage=self.shared_cache)

    def may_inline(self, key: tuple) -> bool:
        if self.budget > self.failed.get(key, 0) and self.visits < self.max_visits:
            return True
        self.budget_hit = True
        return False

    def reuse(self, key: tuple) -> Optional[Expr]:
        found = self.done.get(key)
        if found is None or (found[1] > self.budget and not self.shared_once):
            return None
        expr, nodes, inlined = found
        if not self.shared_once:
            self.budget -= nodes
        self.inlined.update(inlined)
        return expr

    def remember(self, key: tuple, expr: Expr, saved_budget: int, saved_inlined: dict) -> None:
        added = {k: v for k, v in self.inlined.items() if k not in saved_inlined}
        self.done[key] = (expr, saved_budget - self.budget, added)

    def compare(self, e: MediumLevelILInstruction, *, inlined: bool) -> Optional[Expr]:
        """A comparison: 1 bit, over operands of the comparison's own size, or of their own size
        when it has none (HLIL gives loop conditions size 0 over 4-byte operands)."""
        left, right = self.expr(self.get(e, "left"), inlined=inlined), self.expr(self.get(e, "right"), inlined=inlined)
        if left is None or right is None:
            return None
        width = e.size * 8 or max(left.width, right.width)
        # Never extends operands of two sizes, but a comparison read as an integer is 0 or 1 (as_integer).
        left, right = fit(as_integer(left, width), width), fit(as_integer(right, width), width)
        if left is None or right is None:
            return None
        return BinOp(_COMPARE[e.operation], left, right, 1)

    def boolean(self, e: MediumLevelILInstruction, *, inlined: bool) -> Optional[Expr]:
        """A 1-bit value (x86 setcc, ARM64 cset, an if's condition): a comparison, or a flag variable
        (cond:0 = t != 0), followed through its definition or kept as a 1-bit leaf. Normalization reads
        zx(t != 0) as t when t can only be 0 or 1 (v2.1's 0/1 rule)."""
        if e.operation in _COMPARE:
            return self.compare(e, inlined=inlined)
        if e.operation != Op.MLIL_VAR_SSA or e.size != 0:
            return None
        ssa_var = self.get(e, "src")
        definition = self.definition_of(ssa_var)
        if (definition is not None and definition.operation == Op.MLIL_SET_VAR_SSA
                and _is_flag(self.get(definition, "src"))
                and self.budget > 0 and self.visits < self.max_visits
                and (ssa_var.var.identifier, ssa_var.version) not in self.keep):
            found = self.boolean(self.get(definition, "src"), inlined=True)
            if found is not None:
                self.inlined[(ssa_var.var.identifier, ssa_var.version)] = ssa_var
                return found
        if not self.live(ssa_var):
            return None
        return Var(self.name(("var", ssa_var.var.identifier, ssa_var.version, 1), f"{ssa_var.var.name}#{ssa_var.version}"),
                   1, ref=ssa_var)

    def definition(self, definition, ssa_var: SSAVariable, width: int) -> Optional[Expr]:
        if definition.operation == Op.MLIL_SET_VAR_SSA and _is_flag(self.get(definition, "src")):
            found = self.boolean(self.get(definition, "src"), inlined=True)  # r15 = cond:0, r15 = (x != 0)
            return found if found is None or width == 1 else UnOp("zx", found, width)
        if definition.operation == Op.MLIL_SET_VAR_SSA and self.get(definition, "src").size * 8 == width:
            return self.expr(self.get(definition, "src"), inlined=True)
        if definition.operation == Op.MLIL_SET_VAR_SSA_FIELD and _declared_bits(ssa_var.var) == width:
            # A write of part of the variable that keeps the rest of it: rax#2 = rax#1 with .al = e.
            value = self.written(definition)
            if value is None or 8 * self.get(definition, "offset") + value.width > width:
                return None
            old = self.var(self.get(definition, "prev"), width)
            if old is None:
                return None
            try:
                return merge_partial_write(old, value, 8 * self.get(definition, "offset"))
            except ValueError:
                return None
        return None

    def written(self, definition) -> Optional[Expr]:
        """The value a partial write (SET_VAR_SSA_FIELD) stores: rcx#2.cl = rax#2 != 0 @ rcx#1."""
        if _is_flag(self.get(definition, "src")):
            found = self.boolean(self.get(definition, "src"), inlined=True)
            return None if found is None else UnOp("zx", found, 8 * _written_bytes(definition))
        return self.expr(self.get(definition, "src"), inlined=True)

    def field(self, ssa_var: SSAVariable, offset: int, width: int) -> Optional[Expr]:
        """A read of `width` bits at byte `offset` of a variable's storage."""
        declared = _declared_bits(ssa_var.var)
        definition = self.definition_of(ssa_var)
        kept = (ssa_var.var.identifier, ssa_var.version) in self.keep
        if (definition is not None and definition.operation == Op.MLIL_SET_VAR_SSA_FIELD and self.budget > 0
                and self.visits < self.max_visits and not kept):
            # Read over a partial write: x86 -O0 spills bytes into one slot (var_8:7.b = y; ...).
            kind = read_over_write(offset, width // 8, self.get(definition, "offset"), _written_bytes(definition))
            saved = self.budget
            if kind == "inside":
                value = self.written(definition)
                if value is not None:
                    self.inlined[(ssa_var.var.identifier, ssa_var.version)] = ssa_var
                    return field_read(value, 8 * (offset - self.get(definition, "offset")), width)
            elif kind == "disjoint":
                found = self.field(self.get(definition, "prev"), offset, width)
                if found is not None:
                    return found
            self.budget = saved
        if declared and contained(offset, width // 8, declared // 8):
            # Within the variable itself: its definition, if any, gives every bit.
            definition = self.definition_of(ssa_var)
            if definition is not None and self.budget > 0 and self.visits < self.max_visits and not kept:
                saved = self.budget
                whole = self.definition(definition, ssa_var, declared)
                if whole is not None:
                    self.inlined[(ssa_var.var.identifier, ssa_var.version)] = ssa_var
                    return field_read(whole, 8 * offset, width)
                self.budget = saved
        backing = self.backing(self.forward(ssa_var, offset, width // 8))
        if backing is None or not contained(offset, width // 8, backing.width // 8):
            return None
        return field_read(backing, 8 * offset, width)

    def forward(self, ssa_var: SSAVariable, offset: int, size: int) -> SSAVariable:
        """The current version of the variable, if no partial write since `ssa_var` touched these
        bytes: Windows x64 -O0 spills x to var_8:6.b and then reuses rcx, so x#0 is dead at the
        root while var_8's current version still holds the byte."""
        if not self.check:
            return ssa_var
        current = self.root.get_ssa_var_version(ssa_var.var)
        version = current
        for _ in range(64):
            if version == ssa_var.version:
                return SSAVariable(ssa_var.var, current)
            definition = self.definition_of(SSAVariable(ssa_var.var, version))
            if (definition is None or definition.operation != Op.MLIL_SET_VAR_SSA_FIELD
                    or self.get(definition, "prev").var != ssa_var.var
                    or read_over_write(offset, size, self.get(definition, "offset"),
                                       _written_bytes(definition)) != "disjoint"):
                return ssa_var
            version = self.get(definition, "prev").version
        return ssa_var

    def backing(self, ssa_var: SSAVariable) -> Optional[Var]:
        var = ssa_var.var
        size = _storage_bytes(self.ssa, var)
        if size is None or not self.live(ssa_var):
            return None
        key = (int(var.source_type), var.storage, ssa_var.version)
        if key not in self.backings:
            label = f"@{_storage_name(self.ssa, var)}#{ssa_var.version}"
            self.backings[key] = Var(self.name(("backing",) + key, label), 8 * size,
                                     ref=Backing(var, ssa_var.version, size))
        return self.backings[key]

    def relate(self, e: Expr) -> Expr:
        """Express plain reads of a storage version that also has field reads through its backing
        value, so x and x.w0 are known to share their low byte."""
        groups: dict[tuple, list[Var]] = {}
        for leaf in variables(e):
            if isinstance(leaf.ref, SSAVariable):
                key = (int(leaf.ref.var.source_type), leaf.ref.var.storage, leaf.ref.version)
                groups.setdefault(key, []).append(leaf)
        mapping = {}
        for key, leaves in groups.items():
            # A version also read through fields, or read at two widths (x as 32 and 64 bits):
            # the reads share their low bits, and an IR variable has a single width.
            if key not in self.backings and len({leaf.width for leaf in leaves}) < 2:
                continue
            backing = self.backing(leaves[0].ref)
            if backing is None:
                continue
            for leaf in leaves:
                if leaf.width <= backing.width:
                    mapping[(leaf.name, leaf.width)] = field_read(backing, 0, leaf.width)
        return _substitute_leaves(e, mapping) if mapping else e

    def live(self, ssa_var: SSAVariable) -> bool:
        return not self.check or self.root.get_ssa_var_version(ssa_var.var) == ssa_var.version

    def name(self, identity: tuple, label: str) -> str:
        if identity not in self.names:
            taken = set(self.names.values())
            name = label
            while name in taken:
                name += "'"
            self.names[identity] = name
        return self.names[identity]


def _substitute_leaves(e: Expr, mapping: dict[tuple[str, int], Expr], memo: Optional[dict] = None) -> Expr:
    """Like ir.expr.substitute, keyed by (name, width): one name may be read at two widths. Each
    shared value is rebuilt once and stays shared."""
    memo = {} if memo is None else memo
    if id(e) in memo:
        return memo[id(e)]
    if isinstance(e, Var):
        out = mapping.get((e.name, e.width), e)
    elif isinstance(e, Const):
        out = e
    elif isinstance(e, UnOp):
        out = UnOp(e.op, _substitute_leaves(e.operand, mapping, memo), e.width)
    else:
        out = BinOp(e.op, _substitute_leaves(e.left, mapping, memo), _substitute_leaves(e.right, mapping, memo), e.width)
    memo[id(e)] = out
    return out


def _is_flag(e: MediumLevelILInstruction) -> bool:
    return e.operation in _COMPARE or (e.operation == Op.MLIL_VAR_SSA and e.size == 0)


def _written_bytes(definition) -> int:
    """Bytes a partial write stores: its own size (a comparison's size is its operands')."""
    return definition.size if _is_flag(definition.src) else definition.src.size


def _declared_bits(var) -> int:
    try:
        return 8 * var.type.width if var.type is not None else 0
    except Exception:
        return 0


def _storage_name(ssa_func, var) -> str:
    if var.source_type == VariableSourceType.RegisterVariableSourceType:
        return ssa_func.arch.get_reg_name(var.storage)
    return f"stack{var.storage:+#x}"


def _storage_bytes(ssa_func, var) -> Optional[int]:
    """Width of the storage a variable lives in: its register, or its own type on the stack."""
    if var.source_type == VariableSourceType.RegisterVariableSourceType:
        info = ssa_func.arch.regs.get(ssa_func.arch.get_reg_name(var.storage))
        return info.size if info is not None else None
    if var.source_type == VariableSourceType.StackVariableSourceType:
        return _declared_bits(var) // 8 or None
    return None

```

`binja_d810/binja/mlil/lower.py`:

```py
"""binja_d810 IR -> new MLIL expression in the function being analyzed."""

from __future__ import annotations

from binaryninja import ExpressionIndex, ILSourceLocation, MediumLevelILFunction, SSAVariable

from ...ir.expr import CMP_OPS, BinOp, Const, Expr, UnOp, Var
from .lift import Backing, Opaque
from ..storage import as_field


def lower(mlil: MediumLevelILFunction, e: Expr, loc: ILSourceLocation) -> ExpressionIndex:
    size = e.width // 8
    field = as_field(e)
    if field is not None and isinstance(field[0].ref, Backing):
        backing, offset, width = field
        var = backing.ref.var
        if offset == 0 and width == 8 * var.type.width:
            return mlil.var(size, var, loc)
        return mlil.var_field(size, var, offset // 8, loc)
    if isinstance(e, Const):
        return mlil.const(size, e.value, loc)  # a 1-bit constant has size 0: if (true) (spike S2)
    if isinstance(e, Var):
        if isinstance(e.ref, SSAVariable):
            return mlil.var(size, e.ref.var, loc)
        if isinstance(e.ref, Opaque):
            return e.ref.expr.copy_to(mlil)
        raise ValueError(f"cannot lower variable without a Binary Ninja ref: {e.name}")
    if isinstance(e, UnOp) and e.op == "zx" and e.operand.width == 1:
        return mlil.bool_to_int(size, lower(mlil, e.operand, loc), loc)
    if isinstance(e, UnOp):
        operand = lower(mlil, e.operand, loc)
        build = {"neg": mlil.neg_expr, "not": mlil.not_expr, "zx": mlil.zero_extend,
                 "sx": mlil.sign_extend, "trunc": mlil.low_part}[e.op]
        return build(size, operand, loc)
    assert isinstance(e, BinOp)
    left, right = lower(mlil, e.left, loc), lower(mlil, e.right, loc)
    if e.op in CMP_OPS:
        compare = {"eq": mlil.compare_equal, "ne": mlil.compare_not_equal,
                   "ult": mlil.compare_unsigned_less_than, "ule": mlil.compare_unsigned_less_equal,
                   "ugt": mlil.compare_unsigned_greater_than, "uge": mlil.compare_unsigned_greater_equal,
                   "slt": mlil.compare_signed_less_than, "sle": mlil.compare_signed_less_equal,
                   "sgt": mlil.compare_signed_greater_than, "sge": mlil.compare_signed_greater_equal}[e.op]
        return compare(e.left.width // 8, left, right, loc)
    build = {"add": mlil.add, "sub": mlil.sub, "mul": mlil.mult, "and": mlil.and_expr, "or": mlil.or_expr,
             "xor": mlil.xor_expr, "shl": mlil.shift_left, "lshr": mlil.logical_shift_right,
             "ashr": mlil.arith_shift_right, "rol": mlil.rotate_left, "ror": mlil.rotate_right,
             "udiv": mlil.div_unsigned, "sdiv": mlil.div_signed, "urem": mlil.mod_unsigned,
             "srem": mlil.mod_signed}[e.op]
    return build(size, left, right, loc)

```
