`tests/unit/test_engine_contract.py`:

```py
"""The IL-independent engine against a fake ILAdapter (no Binary Ninja needed)."""

from binja_d810.binja.adapter import Candidate
from binja_d810.binja.engine import EngineConfig, simplify_function
from binja_d810.ir.expr import is_mba, node_count
from binja_d810.ir.parse import parse
from binja_d810.semantic.linear_mba import LinearMBABackend


class FakeAdapter:
    """A 'function' of named roots holding IR; replacements write into it."""

    level = "fake"

    def __init__(self, roots, dead_before=(), dead_after=(), change_cfg=False, fail_on_replace=None):
        self.roots = dict(roots)
        self.original = dict(roots)
        self.dead = set(dead_before)
        self.dead_after = set(dead_after)
        self.removed: set = set()
        self.finished = 0
        self.restored = False
        self.change_cfg = change_cfg
        self.fail_on_replace = fail_on_replace
        self.shape = ("blocks", 1)

    def has_candidates(self):
        return any(is_mba(e) for e in self.roots.values())

    def candidates(self, skip):
        skip(0x99, "effect: MLIL_LOAD_SSA")
        for name, e in self.roots.items():
            if is_mba(e):
                yield Candidate(name, 0x1000, e)

    def replace(self, candidate, replacement):
        if candidate.root == self.fail_on_replace:
            raise RuntimeError("injected")
        self.roots[candidate.root] = replacement
        if self.change_cfg:
            self.shape = ("blocks", 2)

    def finish(self):
        self.finished += 1
        self.dead |= self.dead_after

    def dead_assignments(self):
        return set(self.dead) - self.removed

    def remove(self, dead):
        self.removed |= dead

    def cfg_shape(self):
        return self.shape

    def restore(self):
        self.roots = dict(self.original)
        self.removed.clear()
        self.restored = True


def p(text, width=32, widths=None):
    return parse(text, width, widths)


def test_rewrites_are_applied_and_reported_with_level():
    adapter = FakeAdapter({"r": p("(x ^ y) + 2 * (x & y)")})
    report = simplify_function(adapter, [], [LinearMBABackend()], EngineConfig())
    assert adapter.roots["r"] == p("x + y")
    assert [(r.level, r.verdict, r.method) for r in report.rewrites] == [("fake", "PROVEN", "signature")]
    assert [(s.address, s.reason, s.level) for s in report.skipped][:1] == [(0x99, "effect: MLIL_LOAD_SSA", "fake")]


def test_only_newly_dead_assignments_are_removed():
    adapter = FakeAdapter({"r": p("(x ^ y) + 2 * (x & y)")}, dead_before={"z_1"}, dead_after={"t0", "t1"})
    simplify_function(adapter, [], [LinearMBABackend()], EngineConfig())
    assert adapter.removed == {"t0", "t1"}


def test_control_flow_change_rolls_back():
    adapter = FakeAdapter({"r": p("(x ^ y) + 2 * (x & y)")}, change_cfg=True)
    report = simplify_function(adapter, [], [LinearMBABackend()], EngineConfig())
    assert adapter.restored and adapter.roots["r"] == p("(x ^ y) + 2 * (x & y)")
    assert report.rolled_back and report.rewrites == [] and report.rolled_back_rewrites == 1
    assert report.errors[-1].source == "engine" and "control flow" in report.errors[-1].message


def test_failure_mid_replacement_rolls_back_everything():
    adapter = FakeAdapter({"a": p("(x ^ y) + 2 * (x & y)"), "b": p("(x | y) - (x & y)")}, fail_on_replace="b")
    report = simplify_function(adapter, [], [LinearMBABackend()], EngineConfig())
    assert adapter.restored and adapter.roots == adapter.original
    assert report.rolled_back and not report.rewrites


def test_function_without_mixed_operations_is_untouched():
    adapter = FakeAdapter({"r": p("x + y")})
    report = simplify_function(adapter, [], [LinearMBABackend()], EngineConfig())
    assert adapter.finished == 0 and report.rewrites == [] and report.skipped == []


def test_iteration_cap_is_reported():
    class Endless(FakeAdapter):
        def replace(self, candidate, replacement):
            super().replace(candidate, p("(x ^ y) + 2 * (x & y)"))  # never converges

    adapter = Endless({"r": p("(x ^ y) + 2 * (x & y)")})
    report = simplify_function(adapter, [], [LinearMBABackend()], EngineConfig(max_iterations=3))
    assert report.capped and report.still_firing == ["tier2:linear"] and len(report.rewrites) == 3


def test_expired_allowance_does_nothing():
    from binja_d810.deadline import Deadline

    adapter = FakeAdapter({"r": p("(x ^ y) + 2 * (x & y)")})
    report = simplify_function(adapter, [], [LinearMBABackend()], EngineConfig(), Deadline.after(0))
    assert report.budget_exhausted and adapter.roots["r"] == p("(x ^ y) + 2 * (x & y)") and adapter.finished == 0


def test_exhaustion_mid_planning_still_applies_verified_candidates():
    import time

    from binja_d810.deadline import Deadline

    class SlowLinear(LinearMBABackend):
        def simplify(self, e, deadline=None):
            time.sleep(0.08)
            return super().simplify(e, deadline)

    roots = {name: p(f"({name} ^ y) + 2 * ({name} & y)") for name in ("a", "b", "c", "d", "e")}
    adapter = FakeAdapter(roots)
    report = simplify_function(adapter, [], [SlowLinear()], EngineConfig(), Deadline.after(0.12))
    applied = {r for r, e in adapter.roots.items() if e != roots[r]}
    assert report.budget_exhausted and 1 <= len(applied) < len(roots)
    assert len(report.rewrites) == len(applied) and not report.rolled_back
    assert report.plan_seconds >= 0.12 and report.overrun_seconds < 0.2


class ChainAdapter(FakeAdapter):
    """t1 = MBA (single use, inlined by r); r = t1 + MBA."""

    def __init__(self, consumer_simplifies=True):
        super().__init__({"t1": p("(x ^ y) + 2 * (x & y)"),
                          "r": p("((x ^ y) + 2 * (x & y)) + ((x | y) - (x & y))") if consumer_simplifies else p("z")})
        self.planned: list = []

    def candidates(self, skip):  # last first
        yield Candidate("r", 0x20, self.roots["r"], consumes=frozenset({"t1"}))
        yield Candidate("t1", 0x10, self.roots["t1"], defines="t1", single_use=True)


def test_single_use_definitions_inlined_by_a_planned_candidate_are_not_simplified_twice():
    adapter = ChainAdapter()
    report = simplify_function(adapter, [], [LinearMBABackend()], EngineConfig(max_iterations=1))
    assert [r.address for r in report.rewrites] == [0x20] and report.subsumed == 1


def test_a_consumer_that_does_not_simplify_leaves_its_inputs_to_be_simplified():
    adapter = ChainAdapter(consumer_simplifies=False)
    report = simplify_function(adapter, [], [LinearMBABackend()], EngineConfig(max_iterations=1))
    assert [r.address for r in report.rewrites] == [0x10] and report.subsumed == 0


class VisibleAdapter(FakeAdapter):
    """One root whose lift inlined definitions that stay alive (visible form: 5 nodes, unmixed)."""

    def __init__(self, visible_nodes, visible_mixed):
        super().__init__({"r": p("(b - a) + (a & 0xffffff80)")})
        self.visible = (visible_nodes, visible_mixed)

    def candidates(self, skip):
        yield Candidate("r", 0x30, self.roots["r"], visible_nodes=self.visible[0], visible_mixed=self.visible[1])


def test_a_rewrite_never_introduces_a_mix_the_visible_code_did_not_have():
    # strcasecmp: rsi_2 = arg2 - arg1 + rdi_1 with rdi_1 = arg1 & ~0x7f still used elsewhere. The lift
    # is mixed and shrinks to arg2 - (0x7f & arg1), but what the user sees was unmixed.
    from binja_d810.semantic.backend import default_backends

    adapter = VisibleAdapter(visible_nodes=5, visible_mixed=False)
    report = simplify_function(adapter, [], default_backends(), EngineConfig())
    assert report.rewrites == [] and any("visible" in s.reason for s in report.skipped)


def test_a_rewrite_that_shrinks_the_visible_code_is_applied():
    from binja_d810.semantic.backend import default_backends

    adapter = VisibleAdapter(visible_nodes=9, visible_mixed=True)
    report = simplify_function(adapter, [], default_backends(), EngineConfig())
    assert len(report.rewrites) == 1


class CountingBackend:
    """LinearMBABackend that counts the expressions it is asked to simplify."""

    name = "counting"

    def __init__(self):
        from collections import Counter

        self.inner = LinearMBABackend()
        self.calls: Counter = Counter()

    def simplify(self, e, deadline=None):
        self.calls[e] += 1
        return self.inner.simplify(e, deadline=deadline)


def test_an_unchanged_candidate_that_did_not_simplify_is_not_planned_again():
    # Iteration 1 rewrites "b", so the engine runs a second iteration; "a" is the same expression
    # then, and its outcome (no rewrite) is a function of that expression alone.
    stuck = p("(x * y) ^ (x + z)")
    adapter = FakeAdapter({"a": stuck, "b": p("(x ^ y) + 2 * (x & y)")})
    backend = CountingBackend()
    report = simplify_function(adapter, [], [backend], EngineConfig())
    assert [r.address for r in report.rewrites] == [0x1000]
    assert backend.calls[stuck] == 1


def test_cheap_backends_reach_every_candidate_before_slow_ones_spend_the_budget():
    # A Tigress VM: one function with 248 candidates. CoBRA's slow failures on the first candidates
    # left no budget for later ones the linear backend answers in milliseconds.
    import time

    from binja_d810.deadline import Deadline

    class Slow:
        name = "slow"

        def simplify(self, e, deadline=None):
            time.sleep(0.2)
            return None

    roots = {"n1": p("(x * y) ^ (x + z)"), "n2": p("(y * z) ^ (y + x)")}
    roots.update({f"l{i}": p(f"(x ^ {i}) + 2 * (x & {i})") for i in range(1, 4)})
    adapter = FakeAdapter(roots)
    report = simplify_function(adapter, [], [LinearMBABackend(), Slow()], EngineConfig(), Deadline.after(0.3))
    assert {r for r, e in adapter.roots.items() if e != roots[r]} == {"l1", "l2", "l3"}
    assert report.budget_exhausted


class SharedAdapter(FakeAdapter):
    """r = (a ^ z) + 2 * (a & z) where a = (x * y) - (x | y) + (x & 7) is also used elsewhere: the
    deep lift inlines a, and its result a + z copies a's definition into r (a Tigress VM's handlers)."""

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__({"r": p("((((x * y) - (x | y)) + (x & 7)) ^ z) + 2 * ((((x * y) - (x | y)) + (x & 7)) & z)")})
        self.shallow_asked = []

    def candidates(self, skip):
        if is_mba(self.roots["r"]):  # as the real adapters: only MBA roots are candidates
            yield Candidate("r", 0x40, self.roots["r"], visible_nodes=7, visible_mixed=True, shared=frozenset({"a"}))

    def shallow(self, candidate, keep=None):
        self.shallow_asked.append(candidate.root)
        return Candidate("r", 0x40, p("(a ^ z) + 2 * (a & z)"), visible_nodes=7, visible_mixed=True)


def test_a_root_whose_deep_lift_grows_the_visible_code_is_simplified_over_its_shared_values():
    from binja_d810.semantic.backend import default_backends

    adapter = SharedAdapter()
    report = simplify_function(adapter, [], default_backends(), EngineConfig())
    assert adapter.shallow_asked == ["r"]
    assert adapter.roots["r"] == p("a + z") or adapter.roots["r"] == p("z + a")
    assert len(report.rewrites) == 1 and not any("visible" in s.reason for s in report.skipped)


def test_a_smaller_result_over_shared_values_wins_even_when_the_deep_one_shrinks():
    # i686 -O2: the deep rewrite shrank the root (11 -> 9 nodes) but copied a's definition.
    from binja_d810.semantic.backend import default_backends

    adapter = SharedAdapter()
    adapter.candidates = lambda skip: iter([Candidate("r", 0x40, adapter.roots["r"], visible_nodes=40,
                                                      visible_mixed=True, shared=frozenset({"a"}))])
    simplify_function(adapter, [], default_backends(), EngineConfig(max_iterations=1))
    assert adapter.roots["r"] in (p("a + z"), p("z + a"))


def test_roots_that_do_not_simplify_are_not_lifted_again_over_their_shared_values():
    # Ordinary code: most roots with shared definitions do not simplify at all; lifting each again
    # over its shared values doubled planning time on one sample (median 0.06 -> 0.26 s).
    adapter = SharedAdapter()
    adapter.roots["r"] = p("(x * y) ^ (x + z)")  # no deep rewrite, not too complex
    simplify_function(adapter, [], [LinearMBABackend()], EngineConfig())
    assert adapter.shallow_asked == []


def test_reports_separate_cpu_time_from_waiting():
    # Under contention (many functions' passes in parallel), wall time stretches while the pass's
    # own CPU time does not; the report keeps both so overruns can be told apart from slow work.
    import time

    class Sleepy:
        name = "sleepy"

        def simplify(self, e, deadline=None):
            time.sleep(0.2)  # waiting, not computing
            return None

    adapter = FakeAdapter({"a": p("(x * y) ^ (x + z)")})
    report = simplify_function(adapter, [], [Sleepy()], EngineConfig(max_iterations=1))
    assert report.plan_seconds >= 0.2 and report.plan_cpu_seconds < 0.1


def test_concurrent_passes_are_limited_and_waiting_counts_against_the_deadline():
    # Functions analyzed in parallel contend for Python's lock: on one DLL an HLIL pass took 27 s
    # of wall time for about 1 s of work, past Binary Ninja's 20 s limit, and Binary Ninja abandoned
    # such functions. At most PASS_SLOTS passes plan at once; a pass that does not get a slot before
    # its deadline does no work and reports its budget exhausted.
    import threading
    import time

    from binja_d810.binja import engine
    from binja_d810.deadline import Deadline

    running, peak, guard = [0], [0], threading.Lock()

    class Busy:
        name = "busy"

        def simplify(self, e, deadline=None):
            with guard:
                running[0] += 1
                peak[0] = max(peak[0], running[0])
            time.sleep(0.05)
            with guard:
                running[0] -= 1
            return None

    reports = []

    def work():
        adapter = FakeAdapter({"a": p("(x * y) ^ (x + z)")})
        reports.append(simplify_function(adapter, [], [Busy()], EngineConfig(max_iterations=1), Deadline.after(0.3)))

    threads = [threading.Thread(target=work) for _ in range(16)]
    for t in threads:
        t.start()
    for t in threads:
        t.join()
    assert peak[0] <= engine.PASS_SLOTS
    assert any(r.budget_exhausted and r.plan_seconds == 0 for r in reports)
    assert all(r.total_seconds < 0.3 + 0.15 for r in reports)


def test_reports_say_where_planning_time_goes():
    import time

    class Slow:
        name = "slow"

        def simplify(self, e, deadline=None):
            time.sleep(0.05)
            return None

    adapter = FakeAdapter({"a": p("(x * y) ^ (x + z)"), "b": p("(x * z) ^ (y + z)")})
    report = simplify_function(adapter, [], [Slow()], EngineConfig(max_iterations=1))
    assert report.enumerate_seconds >= 0
    assert len(report.slowest) == 2 and report.slowest[0][1] >= 0.05  # (address, seconds, nodes, outcome)


class SplitAdapter(FakeAdapter):
    """OLLVM: b = (a & M) | (~a & ~M) over a = x * K + y (single use). Inlining a gives a mixed
    expression where each visible statement was arithmetic or bitwise only; over a alone, b is
    ~(a ^ M)."""

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__({"b": p("((x * 7 + y) & 0xff00ff00) | (~(x * 7 + y) & 0x00ff00ff)")})
        self.asked: list = []

    def candidates(self, skip):
        if self.roots["b"] == self.original["b"]:
            yield Candidate("b", 0x50, self.roots["b"], visible_nodes=12, visible_mixed=False,
                            consumes=frozenset({"a"}))

    def shallow(self, candidate, keep=None):
        self.asked.append(keep)
        if keep == frozenset({"a"}):
            return Candidate("b", 0x50, p("(a & 0xff00ff00) | (~a & 0x00ff00ff)"), visible_nodes=12,
                             visible_mixed=False)
        return None


def test_a_rewrite_refused_as_newly_mixed_is_tried_over_the_roots_own_inputs():
    from binja_d810.semantic.backend import default_backends

    from binja_d810.rules.registry import load_rules

    adapter = SplitAdapter()
    simplify_function(adapter, load_rules(), default_backends(), EngineConfig())  # a d810 rule does it
    assert frozenset({"a"}) in adapter.asked
    result = adapter.roots["b"]
    assert result != adapter.original["b"] and not is_mba(result) and node_count(result) <= 5, result


class ReuseAdapter(FakeAdapter):
    """x86-64 -O2: `if ((rcx & 1) != 0)` with rcx = (x + 1) * x, x's register reused before the if.
    The version-safe lift keeps rcx; the unchecked lift sees (x + 1) * x and proves the condition
    constant, and a constant reads no variable, so it may replace the condition."""

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__({"c": p("ne(rcx & 1, 0)", 1, {"rcx": 32})})

    def has_candidates(self):
        return True  # a condition: the real adapters' pre-check accepts comparisons over bitwise ops

    def candidates(self, skip):
        if self.roots["c"] == self.original["c"]:
            yield Candidate("c", 0x60, self.roots["c"],
                            unchecked=p("ne(((x + 1) * x) & 1, 0)", 1, {"x": 32}))


def test_a_condition_proven_constant_through_reused_registers_is_folded():
    from binja_d810.ir.expr import Const
    from binja_d810.semantic.backend import default_backends

    adapter = ReuseAdapter()
    report = simplify_function(adapter, [], default_backends(), EngineConfig())
    assert adapter.roots["c"] == Const(0, 1) and report.rewrites[0].verdict == "PROVEN"


def test_an_unchecked_lift_never_gives_a_non_constant_rewrite():
    from binja_d810.semantic.backend import default_backends

    adapter = ReuseAdapter()
    adapter.roots["c"] = adapter.original["c"] = p("(rcx ^ y) + 2 * (rcx & y)", 32, None)
    adapter.candidates = lambda skip: iter([Candidate("c", 0x60, adapter.roots["c"],
                                                      unchecked=p("((x * 3) ^ y) + 2 * ((x * 3) & y)", 32))])
    simplify_function(adapter, [], default_backends(), EngineConfig(max_iterations=1))
    from binja_d810.ir.expr import variables

    assert {v.name for v in variables(adapter.roots["c"])} <= {"rcx", "y"}  # from the checked lift only


class SharedDagAdapter(FakeAdapter):
    """A condition whose lift, as a tree, is far over maxNodes (an OLLVM-obfuscated export): the adapter
    offers it as shared values only, and only a proven constant may replace it."""

    def __init__(self, condition):
        super().__init__({"c": condition})

    def has_candidates(self):
        return True

    def candidates(self, skip):
        from binja_d810.ir.expr import Const as C

        if not isinstance(self.roots["c"], C):
            yield Candidate("c", 0x60, self.roots["c"], constant_only=True, shared_dag=self.roots["c"])


def test_a_condition_over_shared_values_is_folded_by_constancy_only():
    import sys
    from pathlib import Path

    sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent))
    from test_constancy import _bcf_condition

    from binja_d810.ir.expr import Const

    adapter = SharedDagAdapter(_bcf_condition())
    report = simplify_function(adapter, [], [LinearMBABackend()], EngineConfig())
    assert adapter.roots["c"] == Const(1, 1), report
    record = report.rewrites[0]
    assert record.verdict == "PROVEN" and "shared" in record.source and len(record.before) < 400, record


class EnclosedAdapter(FakeAdapter):
    """glibc's pointer alignment: d = p - ((p + 8) & -8) is its own instruction, used once by
    n + d - 8, which HLIL shows as one arithmetic statement with it. d is -8 | p: correct and
    smaller, but the statement would read n + (-8 | p) - 8, mixed where it was not."""

    def __init__(self, consumer):
        super().__init__({"d": p("p - ((p + 8) & 0xfffffff8)")})
        self.consumer = consumer

    def candidates(self, skip):
        if self.roots["d"] == self.original["d"]:
            yield Candidate("d", 0x70, self.roots["d"], visible_nodes=7, visible_mixed=True,
                            consumer_kinds=self.consumer, root_kinds=frozenset({"arith"}))  # q is its own statement


def test_a_rewrite_never_makes_the_statement_that_uses_it_mixed():
    from binja_d810.rules.registry import load_rules
    from binja_d810.semantic.backend import default_backends

    refused = EnclosedAdapter(frozenset({"arith"}))
    report = simplify_function(refused, load_rules(), default_backends(), EngineConfig())
    assert refused.roots["d"] == refused.original["d"], report.rewrites
    assert any("newly mixed" in s.reason for s in report.skipped), report.skipped
    allowed = EnclosedAdapter(frozenset({"bitwise"}))  # a bitwise user: -8 | p reads fine there
    simplify_function(allowed, load_rules(), default_backends(), EngineConfig())
    assert allowed.roots["d"] != allowed.original["d"]


class PathAdapter(FakeAdapter):
    """An opaque predicate: 2 / (x * x + 1) == i with i merged from y1 * y1 + 3 and y2 * y2 + 3: not constant
    over i, false on each incoming path. The adapter offers the per-path variants."""

    def __init__(self, variants):
        super().__init__({"c": p("eq(udiv(2, (x * x) + 1), i)", 1, {"x": 32, "i": 32})})
        self.variants = variants

    def has_candidates(self):
        return True

    def candidates(self, skip):
        if self.roots["c"] == self.original["c"]:
            yield Candidate("c", 0x80, self.roots["c"])

    def path_variants(self, candidate):
        return [self.variants]  # alternatives, cheapest first: one here


def test_a_condition_constant_on_every_incoming_path_is_folded():
    from binja_d810.ir.expr import Const
    from binja_d810.semantic.backend import default_backends

    widths = {"x": 32, "y": 32, "z": 32}
    agree = PathAdapter([p("eq(udiv(2, (x * x) + 1), (y * y) + 3)", 1, widths),
                         p("eq(udiv(2, (x * x) + 1), (z * z) + 3)", 1, widths)])
    report = simplify_function(agree, [], default_backends(), EngineConfig())
    assert agree.roots["c"] == Const(0, 1), report
    assert report.rewrites[0].source == "constancy (per path)" and report.rewrites[0].verdict == "PROVEN"
    for variants in ([p("eq(udiv(2, (x * x) + 1), (y * y) + 3)", 1, widths), p("eq(udiv(2, (x * x) + 1), z)", 1, widths)],
                     [p("eq(x, x)", 1, widths), p("ne(y, y)", 1, widths)]):  # one path varies; two constants
        refused = PathAdapter(variants)
        simplify_function(refused, [], default_backends(), EngineConfig())
        assert refused.roots["c"] == refused.original["c"], variants


def test_a_condition_offered_with_its_paths_is_folded_from_them():
    # A condition over merged values that is no candidate itself (k != 0, k = phi(...)): the adapter
    # offers it constant-only with the per-path variants it computed.
    from binja_d810.ir.expr import Const
    from binja_d810.semantic.backend import default_backends

    widths = {"x": 32, "y": 32, "k": 32}
    adapter = PathAdapter(None)
    adapter.roots["c"] = adapter.original["c"] = p("ne(k, 0)", 1, widths)
    paths = (p("ne(((x - 1) * x) & 1, 0)", 1, widths), p("ne((y + (y * y)) & 1, 0)", 1, widths))
    adapter.candidates = lambda skip: iter([Candidate("c", 0x90, adapter.roots["c"], constant_only=True, paths=(paths,))]
                                           if adapter.roots["c"] == adapter.original["c"] else [])
    report = simplify_function(adapter, [], default_backends(), EngineConfig())
    assert adapter.roots["c"] == Const(0, 1), report


def test_path_alternatives_are_tried_in_order():
    # v3.3: invariant merges substituted alone first (one variant, the other merges free), then the
    # full split. Either may fold; a set folds only if all its variants are the same proven constant.
    from binja_d810.ir.expr import Const
    from binja_d810.semantic.backend import default_backends

    widths = {"x": 32, "y": 32, "z": 32}
    never = p("eq(udiv(2, (x * x) + 1), (y * y) + 3)", 1, widths)
    varies = p("eq(udiv(2, (x * x) + 1), z)", 1, widths)
    for alternatives, folds in (([[never], [varies]], True), ([[varies], [never, never]], True),
                                ([[varies], [never, varies]], False)):
        adapter = PathAdapter(None)
        adapter.path_variants = lambda candidate, alternatives=alternatives: alternatives
        simplify_function(adapter, [], default_backends(), EngineConfig())
        assert (adapter.roots["c"] == Const(0, 1)) == folds, alternatives


def test_per_path_constancy_waits_for_every_other_candidate():
    # v3.3: per-path folding is the costliest mechanism and the rarest; it runs after the last round's
    # other attempts on every candidate, with what remains of the budget (one export's 271 shared-value
    # folds came after per-path attempts on earlier conditions and ran out of time).
    from binja_d810.ir.expr import Const
    from binja_d810.semantic.backend import default_backends

    events = []
    widths = {"x": 32, "y": 32, "z": 32, "i": 32}
    adapter = PathAdapter([p("eq(udiv(2, (x * x) + 1), (y * y) + 3)", 1, widths)])
    adapter.roots["m"] = adapter.original["m"] = p("(x ^ y) + 2 * (x & y)")
    first = Candidate("c", 0x80, adapter.roots["c"])

    def candidates(skip):
        if adapter.roots["c"] == adapter.original["c"]:
            yield first  # the condition comes first, as the adapter's last-first order may put it
        if adapter.roots["m"] == adapter.original["m"]:
            yield Candidate("m", 0x84, adapter.roots["m"])

    def path_variants(candidate):
        events.append("paths")
        return [adapter.variants]

    real_replace = adapter.replace
    adapter.candidates, adapter.path_variants = candidates, path_variants
    adapter.replace = lambda candidate, replacement: (events.append(f"replace {candidate.root}"),
                                                      real_replace(candidate, replacement))
    backend = default_backends()[0]
    real_simplify = backend.simplify
    backend.simplify = lambda e, **kw: (events.append("tier2"), real_simplify(e, **kw))[1]
    simplify_function(adapter, [], [backend], EngineConfig(max_iterations=1))
    assert adapter.roots["c"] == Const(0, 1) and adapter.roots["m"] != adapter.original["m"]
    assert events.index("paths") > max(i for i, e in enumerate(events) if e == "tier2"), events


def test_constant_folds_come_before_every_backend():
    # v3.3: in one OLLVM-obfuscated function, hundreds of junk MBA roots took the whole budget in Tier 2
    # before the opaque predicates' constant-only folds (shared values, 10-60 ms each) were reached.
    # Constant folds run first in each pass: a folded predicate removes the junk behind it.
    import sys
    import time
    from pathlib import Path

    from binja_d810.deadline import Deadline
    from binja_d810.ir.expr import Const

    sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent))
    from test_constancy import _bcf_condition

    class Slow:
        name = "slow"

        def simplify(self, e, deadline=None):
            time.sleep(0.2)
            return None

    roots = {f"m{k}": p(f"(x{k} ^ y) + 2 * (x{k} & y)") for k in range(10)}
    roots["c"] = _bcf_condition()
    adapter = FakeAdapter(roots)
    adapter.has_candidates = lambda: True

    def candidates(skip):
        for name, e in adapter.roots.items():
            if name == "c" and not isinstance(e, Const):
                yield Candidate("c", 0x60, e, constant_only=True, shared_dag=e)  # last, as the order may put it
            elif name != "c" and adapter.roots[name] == adapter.original[name]:
                yield Candidate(name, 0x10, e)

    adapter.candidates = candidates
    simplify_function(adapter, [], [Slow()], EngineConfig(max_iterations=1), Deadline.after(1.0))
    assert adapter.roots["c"] == Const(1, 1)


def test_a_pass_that_folds_constants_commits_them_before_any_backend_runs():
    # v3.3: folded predicates remove the code behind them, so the backends wait for the next pass, over
    # what remains (an OLLVM-obfuscated function: Tier 2 on junk in branches that were about to disappear).
    import sys
    from pathlib import Path

    from binja_d810.ir.expr import Const

    sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent))
    from test_constancy import _bcf_condition

    calls = []

    class Recording:
        name = "recording"

        def simplify(self, e, deadline=None):
            calls.append(adapter.roots["c"])
            return None

    adapter = FakeAdapter({"c": _bcf_condition(), "m": p("(x ^ y) + 2 * (x & y) + (x | y)")})
    adapter.has_candidates = lambda: True

    def candidates(skip):
        if not isinstance(adapter.roots["c"], Const):
            yield Candidate("c", 0x60, adapter.roots["c"], constant_only=True, shared_dag=adapter.roots["c"])
        yield Candidate("m", 0x10, adapter.roots["m"])

    adapter.candidates = candidates
    report = simplify_function(adapter, [], [Recording()], EngineConfig())
    assert adapter.roots["c"] == Const(1, 1), report
    assert calls and all(root == Const(1, 1) for root in calls), "a backend ran before the fold was committed"


def test_a_stuck_candidate_still_gets_its_constant_only_attempts():
    # The cache of stuck candidates is keyed by the version-safe lift, but the per-path variants and the
    # constant-only lifts depend on more (an opaque predicate: a merge that resolves only once other
    # folds changed the IL). Only the simplification is skipped; those attempts run again.
    from binja_d810.ir.expr import Const
    from binja_d810.semantic.backend import default_backends

    widths = {"x": 32, "y": 32, "z": 32}
    other = p("(z ^ y) + 2 * (z & y)")
    adapter = PathAdapter([p("eq(udiv(2, (x * x) + 1), z)", 1, widths)])  # not constant in the first pass
    adapter.roots["m"] = adapter.original["m"] = other
    real_candidates = adapter.candidates

    def candidates(skip):
        yield from real_candidates(skip)
        if adapter.roots["m"] == adapter.original["m"]:
            yield Candidate("m", 0x90, adapter.roots["m"])  # its rewrite gives a second pass

    def replace(candidate, replacement):
        adapter.roots[candidate.root] = replacement
        adapter.variants = [p("eq(udiv(2, (x * x) + 1), (y * y) + 3)", 1, widths)]  # the IL around changed

    adapter.candidates, adapter.replace = candidates, replace
    simplify_function(adapter, [], default_backends(), EngineConfig())
    assert adapter.roots["c"] == Const(0, 1)


def test_an_inconclusive_constant_is_proven_once_per_run_by_shape(monkeypatch):
    from binja_d810.semantic import constancy, memo

    memo.clear()
    calls = []
    monkeypatch.setattr(constancy, "_z3_prove", lambda *a: (calls.append(1), (None, "z3 timeout"))[1])
    monkeypatch.setattr(constancy, "low_bits_value", lambda e: None)  # only the stubbed solver decides
    a, b = p("eq((x * (x + 1)) & 1, 0)", 1), p("eq((y * (y + 1)) & 1, 0)", 1)

    class Constants(FakeAdapter):
        def has_candidates(self):
            return True

        def candidates(self, skip):
            for name, e in self.roots.items():
                yield Candidate(name, 0x1000, e, unchecked=e, constant_only=True)

    report = simplify_function(Constants({"a": a, "b": b}), [], [LinearMBABackend()], EngineConfig())
    assert not report.rewrites and len(calls) == 1


def test_skips_carry_the_expression():
```

`tests/unit/test_evaluate_batch.py`:

```py
"""Shared values evaluated on a batch of samples in one walk (v3.3): the same values as evaluate."""

import random

from exprgen import random_expr

from binja_d810.ir.evaluate import evaluate, evaluate_shared_batch
from binja_d810.ir.expr import CMP_OPS, BinOp, Const, UnOp, Var

OPS = ("add", "sub", "mul", "and", "or", "xor", "neg", "not", "shl", "lshr", "ashr", "rol", "ror",
       "udiv", "urem", "sdiv", "srem")


def _envs(rng, n=40):
    return [{name: rng.choice([0, 1, 0xFF, 0x80000000, 0xFFFFFFFF, rng.getrandbits(32)]) for name in "abc"}
            for _ in range(n)]


def test_agrees_with_evaluate_on_random_expressions():
    rng = random.Random(7)
    for _ in range(300):
        e = random_expr(rng, depth=5, ops=OPS)
        envs = _envs(rng)
        assert evaluate_shared_batch(e, envs) == [evaluate(e, env) for env in envs], e


def test_comparisons_extensions_and_truncations():
    rng = random.Random(8)
    a, b = Var("a", 32), Var("b", 32)
    exprs = [BinOp(op, a, b, 1) for op in sorted(CMP_OPS)]
    exprs += [UnOp("zx", BinOp("ult", a, b, 1), 8), UnOp("sx", UnOp("trunc", a, 8), 32), UnOp("trunc", a, 16),
              BinOp("shl", a, UnOp("trunc", b, 8), 32), BinOp("add", UnOp("zx", UnOp("trunc", a, 8), 32), Const(7, 32), 32)]
    envs = _envs(rng)
    for e in exprs:
        assert evaluate_shared_batch(e, envs) == [evaluate(e, env) for env in envs], e


def test_shared_values_are_walked_once():
    t = Var("a", 32)
    for i in range(30):  # 2^30 nodes as a tree
        m = Const(0x9E3779B9 * (i + 1), 32)
        t = BinOp("or", BinOp("and", t, m, 32), BinOp("and", UnOp("not", t, 32), UnOp("not", m, 32), 32), 32)
    envs = [{"a": v} for v in (0, 1, 0xDEADBEEF)]
    assert len(evaluate_shared_batch(t, envs)) == 3


def test_an_empty_batch():
    assert evaluate_shared_batch(Var("a", 32), []) == []
```

`tests/unit/test_flag_conditions.py`:

```py
import pytest

from binja_d810.deadline import Deadline
from binja_d810.flags.recombine import Limits, recombine
from binja_d810.flags.semantics import CARRY_IS_NO_BORROW, add_overflow, choose, condition, subtraction
from binja_d810.ir.evaluate import evaluate
from binja_d810.ir.expr import BinOp, Const, Var, CMP_OPS, to_signed
from binja_d810.ir.normalize import normalize
from binja_d810.semantic.verify import Verdict, check_equivalent


@pytest.mark.parametrize("architecture", CARRY_IS_NO_BORROW)
@pytest.mark.parametrize("width", (4, 8, 16, 32, 64))
@pytest.mark.parametrize("comparison", sorted(CMP_OPS))
def test_all_flag_conditions_have_exact_width_proofs(architecture, width, comparison):
    a, b = Var("a", width), Var("b", width)
    flags = subtraction(a, b, architecture)
    original = condition(flags, comparison, architecture)
    expected = BinOp(comparison, a, b, 1)
    assert check_equivalent(original, expected) is Verdict.PROVEN
    found = recombine(original).expression
    assert check_equivalent(found, expected) is Verdict.PROVEN
    assert normalize(found) == normalize(expected)


def test_overflow_matches_independent_exhaustive_signed_arithmetic():
    a, b = Var("a", 4), Var("b", 4)
    addition = add_overflow(a, b)
    overflow = subtraction(a, b, "aarch64")["v"]
    for x in range(16):
        for y in range(16):
            signed_x, signed_y = to_signed(x, 4), to_signed(y, 4)
            assert evaluate(addition, {"a": x, "b": y}) == (not -8 <= signed_x + signed_y <= 7)
            assert evaluate(overflow, {"a": x, "b": y}) == (not -8 <= signed_x - signed_y <= 7)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("otherwise", (0, 1))
def test_conditional_flags_recombine_through_their_selector(otherwise):
    a, b, g = Var("a", 32), Var("b", 32), Var("g", 1)
    values = subtraction(a, b, "aarch64")
    selected = {k: choose(g, value, Const(otherwise if k == "n" else 0, 1))
                for k, value in values.items()}
    original = condition(selected, "slt", "aarch64")
    expected = choose(g, BinOp("slt", a, b, 1), Const(otherwise, 1))
    result = recombine(original, guards=(g,))
    assert result.expression == expected
    assert check_equivalent(original, result.expression) is Verdict.PROVEN


def test_flag_reconstruction_does_not_guess_overflow_or_borrow():
    a, b = Var("a", 32), Var("b", 32)
    n = subtraction(a, b, "aarch64")["n"]
    assert check_equivalent(n, BinOp("slt", a, b, 1)) is Verdict.REFUTED
    assert recombine(n).expression != BinOp("slt", a, b, 1)


def test_every_flag_reconstruction_budget_fails_closed():
    a, b = Var("a", 32), Var("b", 32)
    original = condition(subtraction(a, b, "aarch64"), "sle", "aarch64")
    for limits, deadline in ((Limits(nodes=1), Deadline.never()),
                             (Limits(work=0), Deadline.never()),
                             (Limits(), Deadline.after(0))):
        result = recombine(original, limits=limits, deadline=deadline)
        assert result.expression == original and result.notes
```

`tests/unit/test_flow_codecheck.py`:

```py
from binja_d810.flow.codecheck import call_problem, is_self_call, is_tail_call, jump_problem, split_starts


class Code:
    """Code in [start, end) ranges; functions by start -> end; `split`: starts the sweep split off the
    jumping function."""

    def __init__(self, code=((0x1000, 0x2000),), undecodable=(), functions=None, split=()):
        self.code, self.undecodable = code, set(undecodable)
        self.functions, self.split = functions or {}, set(split)

    def is_code(self, address):
        return any(start <= address < end for start, end in self.code)

    def decodes(self, address):
        return address not in self.undecodable

    def owners(self, address):
        return [start for start, end in self.functions.items() if start <= address < end]

    def function_at(self, address):
        return address in self.functions

    def split_off(self, function, address):
        return address in self.split


F = 0x1000  # the jumping function, 0x1000-0x1100


def test_jump_targets_in_plain_code():
    assert jump_problem([0x1200, 0x1210], F, Code(functions={F: 0x1100})) is None


def test_a_jump_target_outside_code_or_not_decoding():
    assert "not code" in jump_problem([0x3000], F, Code())
    assert "does not decode" in jump_problem([0x1200], F, Code(undecodable=[0x1200]))


def test_a_jump_target_inside_another_function():
    code = Code(functions={F: 0x1100, 0x1800: 0x1900})
    assert "inside the function at 0x1800" in jump_problem([0x1810], F, code)


def test_a_jump_target_inside_its_own_function_and_another():
    code = Code(functions={F: 0x1300, 0x1200: 0x1300})
    assert jump_problem([0x1210], F, code) is None


def test_one_function_start_is_a_tail_call():
    code = Code(functions={F: 0x1100, 0x1800: 0x1900})
    assert jump_problem([0x1800], F, code) is None
    assert is_tail_call([0x1800], F, code)


def test_a_function_start_among_several_targets():
    code = Code(functions={F: 0x1100, 0x1800: 0x1900})
    assert "starts another function" in jump_problem([0x1200, 0x1800], F, code)
    assert not is_tail_call([0x1200, 0x1800], F, code)


def test_code_the_sweep_split_off_is_the_jumps_own():
    code = Code(functions={F: 0x1100, 0x1100: 0x1110, 0x1110: 0x1120}, split=[0x1100, 0x1110])
    assert jump_problem([0x1100, 0x1110], F, code) is None
    assert not is_tail_call([0x1110], F, code)
    assert split_starts([0x1100, 0x1110, 0x1110], F, code) == [0x1100, 0x1110]


def test_call_targets():
    code = Code(functions={0x1800: 0x1900})
    assert call_problem([0x1800], code) is None
    assert call_problem([0x1200], code) is None  # code inside no function: it becomes one
    assert "inside the function at 0x1800" in call_problem([0x1810], code)
    assert "not code" in call_problem([0x3000], code)


def test_a_jump_to_the_function_itself_is_a_self_call_not_a_tail_call():
    code = Code(functions={F: 0x1100, 0x1800: 0x1900})
    assert is_self_call([F, F], F) and not is_tail_call([F], F, code) and jump_problem([F], F, code) is None
    assert not is_self_call([F, 0x1800], F) and not is_self_call([0x1800], F)
```

```py
from binja_d810.flow.ranges import layout, parse


def test_ranges_parse_merge_and_name_bad_entries():
    found, errors = parse(["0x2000-0x20ff", "0x1000-0x1fff", "0x1800-0x2003", "nonsense", "0x30-0x10", "0x1-0x2-0x3"])
    assert found == [(0x1000, 0x2100)]
    assert errors == ["nonsense", "0x30-0x10", "0x1-0x2-0x3"]


def test_adjacent_ranges_merge_and_the_end_is_included():
    assert parse(["0x10-0x1f", "0x20-0x2f"]) == ([(0x10, 0x30)], [])
    assert parse([" 0x10 - 0x10 "]) == ([(0x10, 0x11)], [])


def test_a_range_is_laid_over_its_variables():
    variables = [(0x101c, 8), (0x0ffc, 8), (0x1004, 8), (0x1010, 8), (0x2000, 4)]
    inside, gaps = layout(0x1000, 0x1020, variables)
    assert inside == [(0x1004, 8), (0x1010, 8)]  # the two straddling the edges are not retyped
    assert gaps == [(0x100C, 0x1010), (0x1018, 0x101C)]  # nor are their bytes gaps


def test_an_empty_range_is_one_gap():
    assert layout(0x1000, 0x1010, []) == ([], [(0x1000, 0x1010)])


def test_addresses_must_fit_binary_ninjas_unsigned_address_space():
    invalid = ["-1-0x10", "0x0-0x10000000000000000", "0x10000000000000000-0x10000000000000001"]
    assert parse(invalid) == ([], invalid)
```

`tests/unit/test_flow_record.py`:

```py
from binja_d810.flow.record import SETTING, Change, Record


def table(start, end, *claims):
    return Change("table", start, {"end": end, "defined": [[start, "uint64_t const __d810[2]"]]},
                  [[start, "int64_t __d810"]], set(claims))


def test_a_change_is_kept_by_kind_and_key():
    record = Record()
    record.add(table(0x1000, 0x1010, 0x400))
    assert record.get("table", 0x1000).detail["end"] == 0x1010
    assert record.get("range", 0x1000) is None and len(record) == 1


def test_adding_the_same_change_again_adds_its_claims():
    record = Record()
    first = record.add(table(0x1000, 0x1010, 0x400))
    assert record.add(table(0x1000, 0x1010, 0x500)) is first
    assert first.claims == {0x400, 0x500}


def test_a_change_is_unclaimed_once_every_claimant_releases_it():
    record = Record([table(0x1000, 0x1010, 0x400, 0x500)])
    record.release(0x400)
    assert record.unclaimed() == [] and [c.key for c in record.claimed_by(0x500)] == [0x1000]
    record.release(0x500)
    assert [c.key for c in record.unclaimed()] == [0x1000]
    record.drop("table", 0x1000)
    assert len(record) == 0


def test_covering_and_overlapping():
    record = Record([table(0x1000, 0x1010, 1), Change("range", 0x2000, {"end": 0x2100}, [], {SETTING})])
    assert record.covering(0x1008, 0x1010).key == 0x1000
    assert record.covering(0x1008, 0x1018) is None
    assert record.overlapping(0x1008, 0x1018).key == 0x1000
    assert record.covering(0x2010, 0x2018).kind == "range"
    assert record.overlapping(0x1010, 0x2000) is None


def test_branches_by_function():
    record = Record([Change("branches", 0x1234, {"function": 0x1200, "targets": [0x1240]}, [], {0x1200}),
                     Change("branches", 0x5678, {"function": 0x5600, "targets": [0x5680, 0x5690]}, [], {0x5600})])
    assert record.branches_of(0x1200) == [(0x1234, [0x1240])]
    assert record.branches_of(0x9999) == []


def test_the_record_round_trips_through_json():
    record = Record([table(0x1000, 0x1010, 0x400), Change("range", 0x2000, {"end": 0x2100}, [], {SETTING})])
    again = Record.from_json(record.to_json())
    assert again.to_json() == record.to_json()
    assert again.get("range", 0x2000).claims == {SETTING}
    assert again.get("table", 0x1000).previous == [[0x1000, "int64_t __d810"]]
```

`tests/unit/test_flow_tables.py`:

```py
from binja_d810.flow.tables import MAX_ENTRIES, Decoded, Load, Span, addresses_from, decode, span_of
from binja_d810.ir.expr import BinOp, Const, Var

KEY = 0x13371337
M64 = (1 << 64) - 1


def memory(words: dict):
    return lambda address, size: words.get(address)


def minus_key(e, width=64):
    return BinOp("sub", e, Const(KEY, width), width)


def test_a_constant_index():
    decoded, why = decode(minus_key(Var("t", 64)), [Load("t", (0x1008,), 8)], memory({0x1008: 0x4000 + KEY}))
    assert why == "" and decoded == Decoded((0x4000,), (Span(0x1008, 8, 1),))


def test_four_entries_decoded_with_xor_and_a_key_global():
    key = 0x5A5A
    words = {0x1000 + 8 * i: (0x4000 + 0x10 * i) ^ key for i in range(4)} | {0x2000: key}
    loads = [Load("t", (0x1000, 0x1008, 0x1010, 0x1018), 8), Load("k", (0x2000,), 8)]
    decoded, _ = decode(BinOp("xor", Var("t", 64), Var("k", 64), 64), loads, memory(words))
    assert decoded.targets == (0x4000, 0x4010, 0x4020, 0x4030)
    assert decoded.spans == (Span(0x1000, 8, 4), Span(0x2000, 8, 1))


def test_an_mba_decode():
    t, k = Var("t", 64), Const(-KEY & M64, 64)
    mba = BinOp("add", BinOp("xor", t, k, 64), BinOp("shl", BinOp("and", t, k, 64), Const(1, 64), 64), 64)  # t + k
    decoded, _ = decode(mba, [Load("t", (0x1008,), 8)], memory({0x1008: 0x4000 + KEY}))
    assert decoded.targets == (0x4000,)


def test_a_32_bit_table():
    decoded, _ = decode(minus_key(Var("t", 32), 32), [Load("t", (0x1004,), 4)], memory({0x1004: 0x401000 + KEY}))
    assert decoded.targets == (0x401000,) and decoded.spans == (Span(0x1004, 4, 1),)


def test_a_target_that_reads_a_variable_is_not_decoded():
    decoded, why = decode(BinOp("add", Var("t", 64), Var("x", 64), 64), [Load("t", (0x1000,), 8)],
                          memory({0x1000: 1}))
    assert decoded is None and "x" in why


def test_two_indexed_tables_are_not_decoded():
    loads = [Load("t", (0x1000, 0x1008), 8), Load("u", (0x2000, 0x2008), 8)]
    decoded, why = decode(BinOp("add", Var("t", 64), Var("u", 64), 64), loads, memory({}))
    assert decoded is None and "more than one" in why


def test_an_unreadable_entry_is_not_decoded():
    decoded, why = decode(minus_key(Var("t", 64)), [Load("t", (0x1000, 0x1008), 8)], memory({0x1000: KEY}))
    assert decoded is None and "0x1008" in why


def test_entries_must_be_whole_entries_apart():
    assert span_of(Load("t", (0x1000, 0x1004), 8)) is None
    assert span_of(Load("t", (0x1000, 0x1010), 8)) == Span(0x1000, 8, 3)  # every other entry: the span covers both


def test_value_sets():
    assert addresses_from("ConstantPointerValue", value=0x1000) == (0x1000,)
    assert addresses_from("UnsignedRangeValue", ranges=[(0x1000, 0x1018, 8)]) == (0x1000, 0x1008, 0x1010, 0x1018)
    assert addresses_from("InSetOfValues", values=[0x1010, 0x1000]) == (0x1000, 0x1010)
    assert addresses_from("UndeterminedValue") is None
    assert addresses_from("SignedRangeValue", ranges=[(0x1018, 0x1000, 8)]) is None


def test_at_most_max_entries():
    last = 0x1000 + 8 * (MAX_ENTRIES - 1)
    assert len(addresses_from("SignedRangeValue", ranges=[(0x1000, last, 8)])) == MAX_ENTRIES
    assert addresses_from("SignedRangeValue", ranges=[(0x1000, last + 8, 8)]) is None
```

`tests/unit/test_flow_uses.py`:

```py
from binja_d810.flow.uses import ESCAPE, READ, WRITE, classify, encodes, reaches_target, reaches_write


class Graph:
    """A use graph from tables: kinds by node, (parent, operand) by node, readers by defining node."""

    def __init__(self, kinds, parents, readers=None):
        self.kinds, self.parents, self.readers_of = kinds, parents, readers or {}

    def kind(self, node):
        return self.kinds[node]

    def parent(self, node):
        return self.parents.get(node)

    def readers(self, node):
        return self.readers_of.get(node, [])

    def operands(self, node):
        return [(name, child) for child, (parent, name) in self.parents.items() if parent == node]


def _copies(n, end_kind="load", end_operand="src"):
    """c -> set_var s1 -> var v1 -> set_var s2 -> ... -> var vn -> end."""
    kinds, parents, readers = {"c": "const", "end": end_kind}, {}, {}
    node = "c"
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        kinds[f"s{i}"], kinds[f"v{i}"] = "set_var", "var"
        parents[node] = (f"s{i}", "src")
        readers[f"s{i}"] = [f"v{i}"]
        node = f"v{i}"
    parents[node] = ("end", end_operand)
    return Graph(kinds, parents, readers)


def test_a_load_through_address_arithmetic_is_a_read():
    g = Graph({"c": "const", "shl": "shl", "add": "add", "ld": "load"},
              {"c": ("add", "left"), "add": ("ld", "src")})
    assert classify(["c"], g) == (READ, None)


def test_a_store_destination_is_a_write():
    g = Graph({"c": "const", "st": "store"}, {"c": ("st", "dest")})
    assert classify(["c"], g) == (WRITE, "st")


def test_a_stored_value_escapes():
    g = Graph({"c": "const", "st": "store"}, {"c": ("st", "src")})
    assert classify(["c"], g) == (ESCAPE, "st")


def test_a_call_argument_escapes():
    g = Graph({"c": "const", "call": "call"}, {"c": ("call", "params")})
    assert classify(["c"], g) == (ESCAPE, "call")


def test_a_call_proof_applies_to_one_argument_not_the_whole_call():
    g = Graph({"a": "const", "b": "const", "call": "call"},
              {"a": ("call", "params"), "b": ("call", "params")})
    g.call_read_only = lambda parent, node: node == "a"
    assert classify(["a"], g) == (READ, None)
    assert classify(["a", "b"], g) == (ESCAPE, "call")


def test_a_local_store_proof_never_accepts_writing_through_the_pointer():
    g = Graph({"c": "const", "st": "store"}, {"c": ("st", "src")})
    g.stored_read_only = lambda *_: True
    assert classify(["c"], g) == (READ, None)
    g.parents["c"] = ("st", "dest")
    assert classify(["c"], g) == (WRITE, "st")


def test_a_slot_load_requires_the_loaded_pointers_consumer_proof():
    g = Graph({"c": "const", "ld": "load"}, {"c": ("ld", "src")})
    g.loaded_read_only = lambda *_: False
    assert classify(["c"], g) == (ESCAPE, "ld")


def test_returning_a_pointer_requires_an_explicit_consumer_proof():
    g = Graph({"c": "const", "ret": "mlil_ret"}, {"c": ("ret", "src")})
    assert classify(["c"], g) == (ESCAPE, "ret")
    g.return_read_only = lambda *_: True
    assert classify(["c"], g) == (READ, None)


def test_outside_address_search_follows_writes_but_not_stored_or_passed_pointers():
    assert reaches_write("c", _copies(2, "store", "dest"))
    assert not reaches_write("c", _copies(2, "store", "src"))
    assert not reaches_write("c", _copies(2, "call", "params"))
    assert reaches_write("c", _copies(2, "store", "dest"), limit=1)


def test_a_comparison_escapes():
    g = Graph({"c": "const", "cmp": "mlil_cmp_e"}, {"c": ("cmp", "left")})
    assert classify(["c"], g) == (ESCAPE, "cmp")


def test_copies_are_followed_up_to_the_depth_limit():
    assert classify(["c"], _copies(8)) == (READ, None)
    assert classify(["c"], _copies(9)) == (ESCAPE, "s9")


def test_a_write_through_a_copy_is_a_write():
    assert classify(["c"], _copies(2, "store", "dest")) == (WRITE, "end")


def test_a_copy_nobody_reads_is_harmless():
    g = Graph({"c": "const", "s": "set_var"}, {"c": ("s", "src")}, {"s": []})
    assert classify(["c"], g) == (READ, None)


def test_a_merge_is_followed():
    g = Graph({"c": "const", "s": "set_var", "phi": "phi", "v": "var", "ld": "load"},
              {"c": ("s", "src"), "v": ("ld", "src")}, {"s": ["phi"], "phi": ["v"]})
    assert classify(["c"], g) == (READ, None)


def test_a_partial_read_of_a_copy_escapes():
    g = Graph({"c": "const", "s": "set_var", "f": "field", "ld": "load"},
              {"c": ("s", "src"), "f": ("ld", "src")}, {"s": ["f"]})
    assert classify(["c"], g) == (ESCAPE, "f")


def test_a_statement_of_its_own_escapes():
    assert classify(["c"], Graph({"c": "const"}, {})) == (ESCAPE, "c")


def test_every_start_must_only_read():
    g = Graph({"c1": "const", "c2": "const", "ld": "load", "st": "store"},
              {"c1": ("ld", "src"), "c2": ("st", "dest")})
    assert classify(["c1", "c2"], g) == (WRITE, "st")


def test_no_use_at_all_is_a_read():
    assert classify([], Graph({}, {})) == (READ, None)


def test_a_result_used_as_a_call_target():
    assert reaches_target(["v"], Graph({"v": "var", "call": "call"}, {"v": ("call", "dest")}))


def test_a_result_copied_into_a_jump_target():
    g = Graph({"v": "var", "s": "set_var", "w": "var", "j": "jump"},
              {"v": ("s", "src"), "w": ("j", "dest")}, {"s": ["w"]})
    assert reaches_target(["v"], g)


def test_a_result_used_as_an_argument_or_in_arithmetic_is_not_a_target():
    assert not reaches_target(["v"], Graph({"v": "var", "call": "call"}, {"v": ("call", "params")}))
    g = Graph({"v": "var", "add": "add", "call": "call"}, {"v": ("add", "left"), "add": ("call", "dest")})
    assert not reaches_target(["v"], g)


def test_an_access_outside_the_object_is_not_a_use():
    # An arm64 page address (adrp) that a neighbour's store goes through: [page + 0x10] misses the object.
    g = Graph({"c": "const", "add": "add", "st": "store_outside"}, {"c": ("add", "left"), "add": ("st", "dest")})
    assert classify(["c"], g) == (READ, None)
    g = Graph({"c": "const", "add": "add", "ld": "load_outside"}, {"c": ("add", "left"), "add": ("ld", "src")})
    assert classify(["c"], g) == (READ, None)


def test_an_address_computed_past_the_object_is_not_a_use():
    # adrp page; add #0x14: the page is the object's start, the sum a neighbour above it, passed on.
    g = Graph({"c": "const", "add": "address_outside", "call": "call"}, {"c": ("add", "left"), "add": ("call", "params")})
    assert classify(["c"], g) == (READ, None)


def test_an_address_stored_outside_the_object_still_escapes():
    g = Graph({"c": "const", "st": "store_outside"}, {"c": ("st", "src")})
    assert classify(["c"], g) == (ESCAPE, "st")


def _key(*chain, other="var", end=None):
    """ld (the key's load) -> chain[0] -> chain[1] ...; each op's other operand is `other` ("var", "const" or
    None for none); the last node's result goes to `end` (kind, operand) when given."""
    kinds, parents, node = {"ld": "load"}, {}, "ld"
    for i, op in enumerate(chain):
        kinds[f"op{i}"] = op
        parents[node] = (f"op{i}", "right")
        if other is not None and op != "neg":
            kinds[f"o{i}"] = other
            parents[f"o{i}"] = (f"op{i}", "left")
        node = f"op{i}"
    if end is not None:
        kinds["end"] = end[0]
        parents[node] = ("end", end[1])
    return Graph(kinds, parents)


def test_a_key_combined_with_a_variable_encodes():
    for op in ("add", "sub", "mul", "xor"):
        assert encodes(["ld"], _key(op)), op  # x op K


def test_a_constant_encoded_against_a_key_and_used_encodes():
    # c - K returned, stored, passed; -K returned.
    for end in (("mlil_ret", "src"), ("store", "src"), ("call", "params")):
        assert encodes(["ld"], _key("sub", other="const", end=end)), end
    assert encodes(["ld"], _key("neg", end=("mlil_ret", "src")))


def test_a_key_through_constant_operations_into_a_variable_encodes():
    # x << ((K + c) & 31)
    g = _key("add", "and", other="const")
    g.kinds.update({"shl": "shl", "x": "var"})
    g.parents.update({"op1": ("shl", "right"), "x": ("shl", "left")})
    assert encodes(["ld"], g)


def test_a_key_compared_after_constant_operations_does_not_encode():
    # (K ^ c) == d is K == c ^ d; K - 7 tested at -O0 is K == 7: a setting, not a key.
    assert not encodes(["ld"], _key("xor", other="const", end=("mlil_cmp_e", "left")))
    assert not encodes(["ld"], _key("sub", other="const", end=("mlil_if", "condition")))


def test_a_key_used_without_an_encoding_operation_does_not_encode():
    # return K; x & K; [K + 8]; K passed or stored: a setting, a mask or a pointer.
    for chain, end in (((), ("mlil_ret", "src")), (("and",), ("mlil_ret", "src")), (("or",), ("store", "src")),
                       ((), ("load", "src")), ((), ("call", "params")), ((), ("store", "src")),
                       ((), ("mlil_cmp_e", "left"))):
        assert not encodes(["ld"], _key(*chain, end=end)), (chain, end)


def test_a_key_through_a_truncation_and_a_copy_encodes():
    g = Graph({"ld": "load", "t": "trunc", "s": "set_var", "v": "var", "neg": "neg", "r": "mlil_ret"},
              {"ld": ("t", "src"), "t": ("s", "src"), "v": ("neg", "src"), "neg": ("r", "src")}, {"s": ["v"]})
    assert encodes(["ld"], g)


def test_a_key_through_a_merge_encodes():
    g = Graph({"ld": "load", "s": "set_var", "phi": "phi", "v": "var", "x": "xor", "y": "var"},
              {"ld": ("s", "src"), "v": ("x", "left"), "y": ("x", "right")}, {"s": ["phi"], "phi": ["v"]})
    assert encodes(["ld"], g)


def test_an_encoding_beyond_the_copy_limit_does_not_encode():
    kinds, parents, readers, node = {"ld": "load", "end": "sub", "x": "var"}, {"x": ("end", "right")}, {}, "ld"
    for i in range(1, 10):
        kinds[f"s{i}"], kinds[f"v{i}"] = "set_var", "var"
        parents[node] = (f"s{i}", "src")
        readers[f"s{i}"] = [f"v{i}"]
        node = f"v{i}"
    parents[node] = ("end", "left")
    assert not encodes(["ld"], Graph(kinds, parents, readers))
    assert encodes(["ld"], Graph(kinds, parents, readers), max_depth=9)
```

`tests/unit/test_generalization.py`:

```py
"""Rules whose constraints name negative or width-relative constants (v2.1 Task 1)."""

import pytest

from binja_d810.ir.normalize import normalize
from binja_d810.ir.parse import parse
from binja_d810.rules.d810_adapter import D810Rule, ModInt
from binja_d810.rules.registry import instance
from binja_d810.semantic.verify import Verdict, check_equivalent


def test_modular_integers_compare_and_compute_modulo_the_width():
    c = ModInt(0xFE, 8)
    assert c == -2 and -2 == c and c != 2
    assert c + 3 == 1 and isinstance(c + 3, ModInt)
    assert ~c == 1 and -c == 2 and (c & 0xF) == 0xE and (c << 1) == 0xFC
    assert ModInt(0xFFFFFFFE, 32) == -2 and ModInt(0x7FFFFFFF, 32) + 1 == 0x80000000


@pytest.mark.parametrize("width", [8, 16, 32, 64])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("name,text,expected", [
    ("Add_OllvmRule_4", "(x ^ y) - (-2) * (x & y)", "x + y"),
    ("NegAdd_HackersDelightRule_1", "(-2) * (x | y) + (x ^ y)", "-(x + y)"),
    ("Xor_SpecialConstantRule_2", "(x + y) + (-2) * (x & y)", "x ^ y"),
    ("Sub1_FactorRule_1", "((-x) - 1) - (-2) * x", "x - 1"),
])
def test_constraints_with_negative_constants_hold_at_every_width(name, text, expected, width):
    rule = D810Rule(instance(name), [8, 16, 32, 64])
    e = normalize(parse(text, width))
    rewrite = rule.match(e)
    assert rewrite is not None, (name, width, e)
    assert check_equivalent(rewrite.replacement, normalize(parse(expected, width))) is Verdict.PROVEN


# --- offline per-width proofs ---------------------------------------------------------------

from binja_d810.rules.prove import prove_rule  # noqa: E402

THIRTEEN = ["Add_OllvmRule_2", "Add_OllvmRule_4", "Add_SpecialConstantRule_2", "Add_SpecialConstantRule_3",
            "Bnot_Hodur_1", "CstSimplificationRule14", "CstSimplificationRule20", "CstSimplificationRule21",
            "CstSimplificationRule22", "CstSimplificationRule3", "NegAdd_HackersDelightRule_1", "Sub1_FactorRule_1",
            "Xor_SpecialConstantRule_2"]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", ["Add_OllvmRule_4", "NegAdd_HackersDelightRule_1", "Xor_SpecialConstantRule_2"])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("width", [8, 16, 32, 64])
def test_width_independent_identities_are_proven_at_every_width(name, width):
    assert prove_rule(instance(name), width) == "proven"


def test_proof_agrees_with_d810_where_d810_could_prove():
    for name in ("Add_HackersDelightRule_2", "Xor_HackersDelightRule_1", "Or_HackersDelightRule_1"):
        for width in (8, 32):
            assert prove_rule(instance(name), width) == "proven", (name, width)


def test_a_wrong_identity_is_refuted():
    class Wrong:
        """(x ^ y) - c * (x & y) => x - y, c == -2: false."""

    rule = instance("Add_OllvmRule_4")
    from binja_d810.third_party.d810.mba.dsl import Var

    Wrong.pattern, Wrong.replacement = rule.pattern, Var("x_0") - Var("x_1")
    Wrong.CONSTRAINTS = rule.CONSTRAINTS
    Wrong.get_constraints = lambda self, z3_vars: []
    assert prove_rule(Wrong(), 32).startswith("refuted")


# --- constraint-satisfying instances (v2.1 Task 3) ------------------------------------------

from binja_d810.ir.expr import Const as IRConst, walk  # noqa: E402
from binja_d810.rules.instantiate import instantiate  # noqa: E402
from binja_d810.rules.prove import solve_constants  # noqa: E402


def test_constants_are_solved_from_the_constraints():
    rule = instance("CstSimplificationRule7")  # (x & c_1) >> c_2 => (x >> c_2) & c_res, c_res == c_1 >> c_2
    constants = solve_constants(rule, 32)
    assert constants is not None and constants["c_res"] == constants["c_1"] >> constants["c_2"]
    assert constants["c_2"] < 32
    e = instantiate(rule.pattern, 32, constants=constants)
    assert e is not None and any(isinstance(n, IRConst) for n in walk(e))


def test_unsatisfiable_constraints_give_none():
    class Impossible:
        pattern = instance("Add_OllvmRule_4").pattern
        replacement = instance("Add_OllvmRule_4").replacement
        from binja_d810.third_party.d810.mba.dsl import Const as DslConst

        c = DslConst("c")
        CONSTRAINTS = [c == 1, c == 2]

        def get_constraints(self, z3_vars):
            return []

    assert solve_constants(Impossible(), 32) is None
```

`tests/unit/test_ir_bits.py`:

```py
import random

from exprgen import random_expr

from binja_d810.ir.bits import decided_comparison, possible_ones, upper_bound
from binja_d810.ir.evaluate import evaluate
from binja_d810.ir.expr import BinOp, Const, UnOp, Var, mask
from binja_d810.ir.parse import parse

x, y = Var("x", 32), Var("y", 32)


def test_a_masked_value_can_only_have_the_mask_bits():
    assert possible_ones(parse("x & 1", 32)) == 1
    assert possible_ones(parse("(x & 6) | (y & 1)", 32)) == 7
    assert possible_ones(parse("(x & 1) ^ 1", 32)) == 1


def test_unknown_values_may_have_every_bit():
    assert possible_ones(x) == mask(32)
    assert possible_ones(parse("(x & 1) + (y & 1)", 32)) == mask(32)  # a carry reaches bit 1
    assert possible_ones(parse("-(x & 1)", 32)) == mask(32)


def test_extensions_truncations_and_constant_shifts_move_the_bits():
    assert possible_ones(UnOp("zx", BinOp("and", Var("b", 8), Const(1, 8), 8), 32)) == 1
    assert possible_ones(UnOp("sx", BinOp("and", Var("b", 8), Const(1, 8), 8), 32)) == 1
    assert possible_ones(UnOp("sx", BinOp("and", Var("b", 8), Const(0x80, 8), 8), 32)) == 0xFFFFFF80
    assert possible_ones(UnOp("trunc", BinOp("and", x, Const(0x1FF, 32), 32), 8)) == 0xFF
    assert possible_ones(parse("(x & 0x10) >> 4", 32)) == 1
    assert possible_ones(parse("(x & 1) << 3", 32)) == 8


def test_possible_ones_is_sound_on_random_expressions():
    rng = random.Random(7)
    ops = ("add", "sub", "mul", "and", "or", "xor", "neg", "not", "shl")
    for _ in range(400):
        e = random_expr(rng, width=16, depth=4, ops=ops)
        bits = possible_ones(e)
        for _ in range(16):
            env = {name: rng.getrandbits(16) for name in ("a", "b", "c")}
            assert evaluate(e, env) & ~bits == 0


def test_a_comparison_with_zero_of_a_zero_or_one_value_is_that_value_or_its_complement():
    from binja_d810.ir.bits import compare_with_zero

    t = parse("x & 1", 32)
    assert compare_with_zero(t, "ne", 32) == t
    assert compare_with_zero(t, "eq", 32) == BinOp("xor", t, Const(1, 32), 32)
    assert compare_with_zero(t, "ne", 8) == UnOp("trunc", t, 8)
    assert compare_with_zero(UnOp("trunc", t, 8), "ne", 32) == UnOp("zx", UnOp("trunc", t, 8), 32)
    for value in (0, 1):
        env = {"x": value}
        assert evaluate(compare_with_zero(t, "ne", 32), env) == int(value != 0)
        assert evaluate(compare_with_zero(t, "eq", 32), env) == int(value == 0)


def test_other_comparisons_with_zero_are_not_modelled():
    from binja_d810.ir.bits import compare_with_zero

    assert compare_with_zero(parse("x & 3", 32), "ne", 32) is None
    assert compare_with_zero(x, "eq", 32) is None


def test_comparisons_decided_by_bounds_hold_on_every_input():
    rng = random.Random(13)
    ops = ("and", "or", "xor", "add", "not")
    decided = 0
    for _ in range(300):
        e = random_expr(rng, width=8, depth=3, ops=ops)
        for op in ("eq", "ne", "ult", "ule", "ugt", "uge"):
            c = Const(rng.choice([0, 1, 0x7F, 0x80, 0xFF, rng.getrandbits(8)]), 8)
            for a, b in ((e, c), (c, e)):
                value = decided_comparison(op, a, b)
                if value is None:
                    continue
                decided += 1
                for env in ({"a": i, "b": rng.getrandbits(8), "c": rng.getrandbits(8)} for i in range(256)):
                    assert evaluate(BinOp(op, a, b, 1), env) == value, (op, a, b)
    assert decided > 50


def test_upper_bound_of_a_division_by_a_variable():
    assert upper_bound(parse("udiv(2, y * y + 1)", 32)) == 2
    assert upper_bound(parse("urem(x, 10)", 32)) == 9
    assert upper_bound(parse("x & 0x30", 32)) == 0x30

```

`tests/unit/test_ir_compare.py`:

```py
import itertools
import random

import pytest
import z3

from binja_d810.ir.evaluate import evaluate
from binja_d810.ir.expr import CMP_OPS, BinOp, Const, UnOp, Var, is_candidate, mask, to_str
from binja_d810.ir.normalize import normalize
from binja_d810.ir.parse import parse
from binja_d810.semantic.verify import to_z3


def reference(op, a, b, w):
    sa = a - (1 << w) if a >> (w - 1) else a
    sb = b - (1 << w) if b >> (w - 1) else b
    return int({"eq": a == b, "ne": a != b, "ult": a < b, "ule": a <= b, "ugt": a > b, "uge": a >= b,
                "slt": sa < sb, "sle": sa <= sb, "sgt": sa > sb, "sge": sa >= sb}[op])


@pytest.mark.parametrize("width", [8, 16, 32, 64])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("op", sorted(CMP_OPS))
def test_comparisons_evaluate_like_the_reference_at_the_boundaries(op, width):
    m = mask(width)
    edges = [0, 1, m, m >> 1, (m >> 1) + 1, 2, m - 1]
    for a, b in itertools.product(edges, edges):
        e = BinOp(op, Const(a, width), Const(b, width), 1)
        assert evaluate(e, {}) == reference(op, a, b, width), (op, a, b)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("op", sorted(CMP_OPS))
def test_comparisons_in_z3_agree_with_evaluate(op):
    x, y = Var("x", 16), Var("y", 16)
    e = BinOp(op, x, y, 1)
    zx_, zy = z3.BitVec("x", 16), z3.BitVec("y", 16)
    rng = random.Random(3)
    for _ in range(200):
        a, b = rng.getrandbits(16), rng.getrandbits(16)
        s = z3.Solver()
        s.add(zx_ == a, zy == b)
        assert s.check() == z3.sat
        assert s.model().eval(to_z3(e, {"x": zx_, "y": zy})).as_long() == evaluate(e, {"x": a, "y": b})


def test_comparisons_have_one_bit_and_equal_operand_widths():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        BinOp("eq", Var("x", 32), Var("y", 16), 1)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        BinOp("eq", Var("x", 32), Var("y", 32), 32)
    assert BinOp("ult", Var("x", 8), Var("y", 8), 1).width == 1


def test_comparisons_print_and_parse():
    e = BinOp("slt", BinOp("and", Var("x", 32), Const(7, 32), 32), Const(8, 32), 1)
    assert to_str(e) == "slt((x & 7), 8)"
    assert parse("slt(x & 7, 8)", 1, {"x": 32}) == e
    assert parse("zx32(ne(x & 1, 0))", 32) == UnOp("zx", BinOp("ne", parse("x & 1", 32), Const(0, 32), 1), 32)


def test_normalization_of_comparisons():
    x = Var("x", 32)
    assert normalize(BinOp("eq", x, x, 1)) == Const(1, 1)
    assert normalize(BinOp("ult", x, x, 1)) == Const(0, 1)
    assert normalize(BinOp("ult", x, Const(0, 32), 1)) == Const(0, 1)
    assert normalize(BinOp("uge", x, Const(0, 32), 1)) == Const(1, 1)
    # bool_to_int of a 0/1 test is the value (v2.1's lifting rule, now an identity)
    t = normalize(parse("x & 1", 32))
    assert normalize(UnOp("zx", BinOp("ne", t, Const(0, 32), 1), 32)) == t
    assert normalize(UnOp("zx", BinOp("eq", t, Const(0, 32), 1), 32)) == normalize(BinOp("xor", t, Const(1, 32), 32))


def test_candidates_are_mbas_or_comparisons_over_bitwise_operations_or_products():
    assert is_candidate(parse("(x ^ y) + 2 * (x & y)", 32))
    assert is_candidate(parse("eq((x * (x + 1)) & 1, 0)", 1, {"x": 32}))
    assert is_candidate(parse("ne(x | 16, 15)", 1, {"x": 32}))
    assert is_candidate(parse("eq(x * y, 3)", 1, {"x": 32, "y": 32}))
    assert not is_candidate(parse("ult(x, y - 1)", 1, {"x": 32, "y": 32}))
    assert not is_candidate(parse("x + 1", 32))


def test_comparisons_decided_by_their_form_or_bit_bounds_are_candidates():
    # Compilers reduce opaque predicates to these: a copy makes both operands one variable
    # (opaque_mba_or at -O2), and (x & 0xff) <= 0xff becomes a zero-extended low byte.
    assert is_candidate(parse("eq(x, x)", 1, {"x": 32}))
    assert is_candidate(parse("ugt(zx32(trunc8(x)), 0xff)", 1, {"x": 32}))
    assert is_candidate(parse("uge(zx32(c), 0x100)", 1, {"c": 8}))
    assert is_candidate(parse("eq(zx32(c), 0x100)", 1, {"c": 8}))
    assert not is_candidate(parse("eq(zx32(c), 0x41)", 1, {"c": 8}))
    assert not is_candidate(parse("ult(zx32(c), 0x80)", 1, {"c": 8}))
    assert not is_candidate(parse("eq(x, y)", 1, {"x": 32, "y": 32}))


def test_one_bit_constants_print_as_zero_or_one():
    # Reports show a folded condition as its value: true is 1, not the signed 1-bit (-1).
    assert to_str(Const(1, 1)) == "1" and to_str(Const(0, 1)) == "0"
    assert to_str(Const(0xFFFFFFFF, 32)) == "(-1)"


def test_nodes_have_at_least_one_bit():
    # A 0-bit operand compares equal to anything 0-bit: a lifter that produced one would let a
    # live condition be "proven" constant (HLIL loop conditions have size 0).
    import pytest

    a = Var("a", 32)
    for build in (lambda: Const(0, 0), lambda: Var("b", 0), lambda: UnOp("trunc", a, 0),
                  lambda: BinOp("add", Var("b", 0), Var("c", 0), 0)):
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            build()

```

`tests/unit/test_ir_expr.py`:

```py
import random

import pytest

from binja_d810.ir.evaluate import evaluate
from binja_d810.ir.expr import (
    BinOp, Const, UnOp, Var, is_bitwise_junk, is_candidate, is_mba, mask, node_count, substitute, to_str,
    variables,
)
from binja_d810.ir.parse import parse

a, b = Var("a", 32), Var("b", 32)
M32 = mask(32)


def mba_add(x, y):  # (x ^ y) + 2*(x & y)
    return BinOp("add", BinOp("xor", x, y, 32), BinOp("mul", Const(2, 32), BinOp("and", x, y, 32), 32), 32)


def test_const_is_masked_to_width():
    assert Const(-1, 8).value == 0xFF
    assert Const(0x1FF, 8).value == 0xFF


def test_binop_rejects_mismatched_widths():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        BinOp("add", Var("a", 32), Var("b", 64), 32)


def test_shift_amount_may_have_another_width():
    BinOp("shl", a, Const(3, 8), 32)


def test_unop_width_rules():
    UnOp("zx", Var("p", 8), 32)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        UnOp("zx", a, 8)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        UnOp("trunc", Var("p", 8), 32)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        UnOp("frob", a, 32)


def test_evaluate_classic_mba_identity():
    rng = random.Random(1)
    for _ in range(200):
        x, y = rng.getrandbits(32), rng.getrandbits(32)
        assert evaluate(mba_add(a, b), {"a": x, "b": y}) == (x + y) & M32


def test_evaluate_shifts_and_extensions():
    assert evaluate(BinOp("ashr", Const(0x80000000, 32), Const(4, 32), 32), {}) == 0xF8000000
    assert evaluate(BinOp("lshr", Const(0x80000000, 32), Const(4, 32), 32), {}) == 0x08000000
    # Counts are reduced modulo max(32, width) (tests/unit/test_shifts.py has the measured reference):
    assert evaluate(BinOp("shl", Const(1, 32), Const(33, 32), 32), {}) == 2  # ARM64 lsl w by 33
    assert evaluate(BinOp("shl", Const(1, 8), Const(8, 8), 8), {}) == 0  # x86 shl al by 8 (v1 said 1)
    assert evaluate(UnOp("sx", Const(0x80, 8), 32), {}) == 0xFFFFFF80
    assert evaluate(UnOp("zx", Const(0x80, 8), 32), {}) == 0x80
    assert evaluate(UnOp("trunc", Const(0x12345678, 32), 8), {}) == 0x78


def test_variables_dedupe_in_first_occurrence_order():
    e = BinOp("add", b, BinOp("xor", a, b, 32), 32)
    assert [v.name for v in variables(e)] == ["b", "a"]


def test_node_count_and_is_mba():
    assert node_count(mba_add(a, b)) == 9
    assert is_mba(mba_add(a, b))
    assert not is_mba(BinOp("add", a, b, 32))
    assert not is_mba(BinOp("xor", a, b, 32))


def test_to_str_is_fully_parenthesised():
    assert to_str(mba_add(a, b)) == "((a ^ b) + (2 * (a & b)))"
    assert to_str(BinOp("add", a, Const(-5, 32), 32)) == "(a + (-5))"
    assert to_str(UnOp("zx", Var("p", 32), 64)) == "zx64(p)"
    assert to_str(BinOp("ashr", a, Const(3, 32), 32)) == "sar(a, 3)"
    assert to_str(Const(0xDEADBEEF, 32)) == "0xdeadbeef"


def test_var_ref_is_ignored_by_equality():
    assert Var("a", 32, ref=object()) == Var("a", 32)


def test_substitute_replaces_by_name():
    e = substitute(BinOp("xor", a, b, 32), {"a": Var("x", 32)})
    assert e == BinOp("xor", Var("x", 32), b, 32)


def test_brief_renders_only_what_it_shows():
    # v3.3: reports rendered whole expressions only to cut them at 2000 characters (10 s of a large
    # function's 133). brief stops at its limit and shows exactly the start of to_str.
    import random
    import time

    from exprgen import random_expr

    from binja_d810.ir.expr import UnOp, brief, to_str

    rng = random.Random(3)
    for _ in range(300):
        e = random_expr(rng, depth=6, ops=("add", "sub", "mul", "and", "or", "xor", "neg", "not", "shl"))
        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            e = UnOp("neg", e, e.width)
        full = to_str(e)
        for limit in (5, 40, 400):
            assert brief(e, limit) == (full if len(full) <= limit else full[:limit] + "..."), (limit, full)
    big = random_expr(random.Random(4), depth=11)
    started = time.perf_counter()
    for _ in range(200):
        brief(big, 40)
    assert time.perf_counter() - started < 0.5


@pytest.mark.parametrize("text", [
    "(x & y) | (x ^ y)", "(x ^ ~y) & x", "(~x & y) | (x & ~y)", "(x ^ (y ^ 1)) & x & 1",
    "x ^ (y ^ x)", "(x | 0xf0) & 0x0f", "((x >> 3) & y) | ((x >> 3) ^ y)",
])
def test_substitution_shapes_are_candidates(text):
    assert is_bitwise_junk(parse(text, 32)) and is_candidate(parse(text, 32))


@pytest.mark.parametrize("text", ["x & 0xff", "a | b", "(h >> 16) ^ h", "(x >> 8) & 0xff", "(x << y) ^ (x & y)"])
def test_plain_masks_and_combinations_are_not_bitwise_junk(text):
    assert not is_bitwise_junk(parse(text, 32))


def test_arithmetic_is_not_bitwise_junk():
    assert not is_bitwise_junk(parse("(x + y) & (x ^ y) & 3", 32))  # an MBA, handled as one


def test_a_shared_subtree_repeats_its_variables():
    t = parse("x & y", 32)
    assert is_bitwise_junk(BinOp("or", t, BinOp("xor", t, Var("z", 32), 32), 32))
```

`tests/unit/test_ir_normalize.py`:

```py
import random

from exprgen import random_expr

from binja_d810.ir.evaluate import evaluate
from binja_d810.ir.expr import BinOp, Const, UnOp, Var
from binja_d810.ir.normalize import normalize
from binja_d810.ir.parse import parse

a, b = Var("a", 32), Var("b", 32)


def n(text, width=32, widths=None):
    return normalize(parse(text, width, widths))


def test_shift_by_constant_becomes_multiply():
    assert n("a << 3") == BinOp("mul", Const(8, 32), a, 32)


def test_not_neg_canonical_forms():
    assert n("a ^ -1") == UnOp("not", a, 32)
    assert n("0 - a") == UnOp("neg", a, 32)
    assert n("-1 * a") == UnOp("neg", a, 32)
    assert n("~~a") == a


def test_add_sub_with_negatives():
    assert n("a + -5") == BinOp("sub", a, Const(5, 32), 32)
    assert n("a - -5") == BinOp("add", Const(5, 32), a, 32)
    assert n("a + -b") == BinOp("sub", a, b, 32)


def test_identities_and_folding():
    assert n("(a & -1) | 0") == a
    assert n("a ^ a") == Const(0, 32)
    assert n("a - a") == Const(0, 32)
    assert n("3 * 7 + 1") == Const(22, 32)


def test_commutative_ordering_puts_constants_first():
    assert n("a + 1") == BinOp("add", Const(1, 32), a, 32)
    assert n("b & a") == n("a & b")


def test_truncation_pushdown():
    assert n("trunc32(zx64(a) + zx64(b))", 32, {"a": 32, "b": 32}) == BinOp("add", a, b, 32)
    assert n("trunc16(sx64(a))", 16, {"a": 32}) == UnOp("trunc", a, 16)


def test_normalize_is_idempotent_and_exact():
    rng = random.Random(7)
    ops = ("add", "sub", "mul", "and", "or", "xor", "neg", "not", "shl")
    for _ in range(300):
        e = random_expr(rng, ops=ops)
        once = normalize(e)
        assert normalize(once) == once
        for _ in range(10):
            env = {name: rng.getrandbits(32) for name in "abc"}
            assert evaluate(once, env) == evaluate(e, env)


def test_normalize_preserves_semantics_at_8_and_16_bits():
    rng = random.Random(8)
    for width in (8, 16):
        for _ in range(150):
            inner = random_expr(rng, width=32)
            narrow = UnOp("trunc", inner, width)
            once = normalize(narrow)
            assert once.width == width
            for _ in range(10):
                env = {name: rng.getrandbits(32) for name in "abc"}
                assert evaluate(once, env) == evaluate(narrow, env)


def test_constants_of_one_associative_operation_are_combined():
    # x86 masks a shift count (cl & 0x1f) that the source already masked: (n & 31) & 31.
    for text, expected in [("((32 - r) & 31) & 31", "(32 - r) & 31"), ("(a | 3) | 12", "a | 15"),
                           ("(a ^ 5) ^ 5", "a"), ("(a + 3) + 4", "a + 7"), ("(a * 3) * 5", "a * 15")]:
        assert normalize(parse(text, 32)) == normalize(parse(expected, 32)), text


def test_redundant_shift_count_mask_is_not_worth_a_rewrite():
    # Ordinary rotate code on i686 -O0 (regression.c reg_rotl): only the mask changes.
    from binja_d810.semantic.backend import default_backends
    from binja_d810.simplify import simplify_expression

    e = parse("x >> (((32 - r) & 31) & 31)", 32)
    assert simplify_expression(e, [], default_backends()).rewrite is None


def test_constant_chains_through_subtraction_are_folded():
    # ((x & 4095) - 3968) - 96 in ordinary code: folding is normalization, not a rewrite.
    for text, expected in [("((x & 4095) - 3968) - 96", "(x & 4095) - 4064"), ("(x - 3) + 10", "x + 7"),
                           ("(x + 10) - 3", "x + 7"), ("(x - 3) - (-3)", "x")]:
        assert normalize(parse(text, 32)) == normalize(parse(expected, 32)), text


def test_a_field_of_a_field_is_one_field_read():
    # rdx = x.di; rdx.dh  ->  byte 1 of x's register: trunc8(trunc16(b) >> 8) == trunc8(b >> 8).
    b = Var("b", 64)
    nested = UnOp("trunc", BinOp("lshr", UnOp("trunc", b, 16), Const(8, 16), 16), 8)
    flat = UnOp("trunc", BinOp("lshr", b, Const(8, 64), 64), 8)
    assert normalize(nested) == normalize(flat)
    rng = random.Random(1)
    for _ in range(200):
        v = rng.getrandbits(64)
        assert evaluate(nested, {"b": v}) == evaluate(flat, {"b": v})
    # Not when the shifted window leaves the inner truncation: trunc8(trunc12(b) >> 8) keeps 4 bits.
    partial = UnOp("trunc", BinOp("lshr", UnOp("trunc", Var("c", 64), 16), Const(12, 16), 16), 8)
    assert normalize(partial) != normalize(UnOp("trunc", BinOp("lshr", Var("c", 64), Const(12, 64), 64), 8))


def test_extending_a_truncation_that_dropped_no_possible_ones_gives_the_value():
    # x86 setne r15b; movzx r15d, r15b: zx32(trunc8(x & 1)) is x & 1.
    t = normalize(BinOp("and", a, Const(1, 32), 32))
    assert normalize(UnOp("zx", UnOp("trunc", t, 8), 32)) == t
    assert normalize(UnOp("zx", UnOp("trunc", t, 8), 16)) == normalize(UnOp("trunc", t, 16))
    wide = UnOp("zx", UnOp("trunc", a, 8), 32)
    assert normalize(wide) == wide


def test_widening_extensions_of_truncations_preserves_values():
    rng = random.Random(11)

    def narrow(depth):
        if depth == 0 or rng.random() < 0.3:
            choice = rng.random()
            if choice < 0.4:
                return UnOp("trunc", Var(rng.choice("ab"), 32), 8)
            if choice < 0.7:
                return UnOp("trunc", BinOp("and", Var(rng.choice("ab"), 32), Const(rng.choice([1, 3, 0x81]), 32), 32), 8)
            return Const(rng.getrandbits(8), 8)
        return BinOp(rng.choice(["and", "or", "xor"]), narrow(depth - 1), narrow(depth - 1), 8)

    for _ in range(300):
        e = UnOp("zx", narrow(3), 32)
        normal = normalize(e)
        for _ in range(8):
            env = {"a": rng.getrandbits(32), "b": rng.getrandbits(32)}
            assert evaluate(e, env) == evaluate(normal, env), (e, normal)
```
